The super creepy atmosphere, the mystery of what has happened to you, and the freaky monsters make a recipe for a great horror game. SOMA blends together every type of scary aspect of horror games, giving you smart enemies, hiding, and no way to defend yourself. If you want a game with some problem solving, and nail biting suspence and great voice acting, this is the game for you.

The scaryness is somewhat contrived when you start to notice patterns in monster encounters, but they're so unpredictable that they're still incredibly terrifying moments.
The lack of variety starts to show itself near the end of the game, but it's not terribly drawn out.
The stealth mechanic is fairly underwhelming once you understand its nuances.
The puzzles in this game can catch you off guard with their difficulty. I'll be the first to admit that I had to grab a guide for one of them.
Modding support has tripled the lifespan of this game. There are still custom stories/full conversions being made five years later...
There are some concepts that aren't fully explored, both gameplay and story-wise; but it's still an amazing game.

The legendary history of development does not equal a legendary end product, and the patchwork game we have as a result is a disappointment for anyone who waited, mediocre for anyone new to the Duke series and completely forgetable if not for the prestige it's predesessor has.

In fact, I don't think this game could work as well in any other way, the horror is simply necessary.
The reason the horror aspect is so essential is because of the philosophical nature of the story. This is one of very few games I've played where I think that players should focus on absorbing the story elements and considering them in a serious manner. If anything, SOMA is like reading a paper on the concept of Neuro-copying and philosophical and ethical problems of said topic. And this is where the horror elements comes into play. The idea of being human one moment, and then the next you're essentially an android or computer program is, well, scary. One of the first characters you meet after the introduction is suffering for delusions as a result of his own inability to accept his fate as a robot.
That a game can set out to tackle a near-future issue in such a way that doesn't feel ridiculous or underestimated is fantastic. The moral and ethical ramifications of neuro-copying are well-considered and integrated into the story in a way that makes them feel like a primary goal of the developers. Frictional could have easily relegated the whole philosophical side of the game to flavor text and simply focused on scaring the player, but they didn't. It's at the forefront of the experience and, as a player, if you ignore this aspect of the game you're not going to get nearly as good of an experience.
So, to back up, the horror element of the game (as far as I am) has been more of an existential one rather than a spooky-boo-monster one (Amnesia, for instance). Sure, there are plenty of tense moments, and there are parts that will make a lot of players panic, but those moments aren't the main focus. The puzzle solving has been trimmed back since Amnesia it seems, with puzzles have a solution requiring a bit of exploring instead of carrying items around.
I'm going to cut this short here, there are plenty of other things to talk about, but with Frictional Games at this point the quality is a given. Physics, sound design, graphics, puzzles, etc are all pretty top notch. I haven't experienced any significant bugs or glitches. Let's just say that this game is definitely a contender for GOTY.

This is basically Empires: Total War. I had never played any of the total war games until steam had a total war weekend, and although I definitely would choose to play a total war game before i'd choose to replay this one due to the wider maps and stronger gameplay, this game does not lag behind. I'm not sure who developed this, but when i play Total War Empires, there isnt a single element of the game that doesnt lead me to believe that Total war blatantly plagarized this entire game. For being made 3 years before Rome and about 6 years before Empires, Imperial Glory beat the Total War series to the punch in Naval RTS. I see no significant difference between the Naval element of this game vs Empires Total War's Naval battles, except maybe asthetics. Even at 5 bucks this is a bargain, but if u're pinching pennies, this goes on sale often at anywhere from .99 to 2.99.
Again, if ure a fan of the Total War games, grand and/or real time strategies, BUY THIS GAME.
Pros:
-Almost entirely Identical to total war empires minus injuh and amrika.
-Flawless integration of RTS in this Grand Strategy
-Fantastic Retail price
-up to 100, 12 turn years of game play
-Had Naval RTS 5 years before total war (Naval engine feels identical to that of Empires Total War)
-Graphics more than adequite
-Diplomacy is WAY more comprehensive than Total War games. In Total War Empires I felt like i could easily cheat the other nations with bribery and fake diplomacy. For instance, if i was at war with a nation, all it would take is a little cash to get a peace accord signed, which meant i could go and conquer a few territories of a nation and then afterwards i could get a peace treaty signed and keep the countries that i conquered, and generally, they wouldnt do♥♥♥♥♥♥about it as long as our diplomatic relations are set at "peace". In Imperial glory, I couldn't put anything past the AI and i had to genuinely practice good diplomacy to earn the trust of my fellow emperors, otherwise they reigned hell down on me. This, I think, is something Total war has never been able to master.
Cons:
-No india or america theatre
-RTS is somewhat limited by comparison to Total war, but not so much that u want to skip the battles. Here are my complaints of the RTS:
=limited map diversity
=less comprehensive defensive features
(The next one is sort of a pro as well)
=Occupation is a prolonged process. it takes many turns to annex a nation and requires a considerable amount of troops to do so. In retrospect, Total war adapted their own version of this by letting the people rebel throughout the game which i think makes it easier to play. So basically, this game is more challenging militarily speaking
EDIT
OH!!! and I have win 8.1 and it did crash a couple times, however the autosave is super frequent. i never lost my place the few times that it did crash, and furthermore, the crashes that i had in Total War weren't any less frequent. I've been reading a lot of the neg reviews, and it seems the only consistent complaints are the crashes. Seriously, dont let that prevent u from buying this game, especially if u like the Total war style grand/rt strategy genre at a really really really cheap price. Imperial Glory was the framework that TOTAL WAR based their games on. dont wait for the movie, read the book. Total war is the movie. Imperial Glory is the book.

With all the high praise for this game (and basically nothing new for me to play until Fallout 4), I gave this a go.
I'm normally not a fan of games where you get no weapons and can't fight back, so for me to play a game like this is a challenge without even trying.  And, considering I mostly enjoyed the somewhat similar Alien Isolation I decided to try Soma, which is way less creepy.
So here you go...
The GOOD:
-- A Slower-paced game - there is minimal rushing through anything
-- Nice graphics, level design, overall look and feel
-- High level of interactivity (lights, doors, switches, etc)
-- Good music and sound design
-- Nice underwater effects
-- Monster effects were neat (ie, screen gets pixelated as they get closer to you)
-- Reminded me of a modern-day "Rapture" from the Bioshock games and also System Shock 2
The BAD:
-- It annoyed me in all the same ways Alien Isolation did - no weapons, you can't fight back (yeah, I read the game description), your character seems like a weakling, you will be forced to repeat the same areas over and over, etc
-- The puzzles were bland and boring
-- The game could have done a better job with giving you some objectives (even mild guidance would've helped), especially in the underwater sections
-- The game is surprisingly linear (though I never expected a full-on open world)
-- The graphics are not optimized and stutter in many places
The UGLY:
-- The voice acting was unbalanced - sometimes the tone was right on, otherwise the actors seemed too whimsical with a "gee, we're under water with robots? like wow"  attitude that did NOT fit the story
-- Yet another check point save system game - I am beyond tired of these (yes I was aware of the "save and exit option", but why should I have to exit the game to save it where I wanted to?  And it didn't always save in the ideal spot either)
I've played it for 6 hours and lost interest.  The first 3-4 hours held my interest - just enough time for me to be ineligible for a refund. Yay.
I'll watch the end on You Tube.

Imperial Glory is one of the best RTS games i'd say, If you're a fan of games like Age of Empires or Divinity Dragon Commander or anything that's like that then this is your game.
For a game that's from 2005 it's still quite a blast, i'd play it for about 3-4 hours non stop and for a game like that, it's quite an achievement.
Alright i'll start by saying you need to play this game for ATLEAST more than 5 hours to COMPLETELY understand how much content it has, at first it does indeed look ugly and really half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥with it's fair share of bugs but it's really fun, though one of the really annoying things is you can only play as one of 5 europian powers, and there's about 15 or more civils so it feels like that's been completely ignored or just rushed at devoloupment.
Anyways you have two ways to play the game, A "Total Victory" type of campaign where you HAVE to unite the entire map, as in just fight every single dude who says no, or just buy every single country (except for capitals which you can't buy :<) till you get the entire world in your hands, or a "Score Victory" where you just have to get the most score. (just build build build and spam peace everywhere.) and the other way is to play one of the four battles that are all related to France and Napoleon at the early 1800's which is a bit of a shame really.
The "Total Victory" is pretty much the best way to play the game, it has the most content and would take you about 15-25 hours to complete atleast one campaign with that way.
Since it's the best way i'll start by explaining it, first off you pick your civil, then you have one of three ways to completely dominate a country/civil, One way is just buy everything they have till they only own their capital, Then just invade that. There's also a "Peaceful" way to completely annex them via just building newspaper offices and consolates and loads of other buildings to force them to like you all the way till they give you everything they have (units - land - resources) This way is gonna cost you ALOT but it's really worth it, and of course it's worth it later on since you get like 4000 gold each turn which is abit overpowered but still is fair since you really need gold at all times along with other resources. Third way is to go with a large army with/without help of anyone else and just try to completely destroy your enemy, I'd go with peaceful since the A.I generates a big army in somewhat of a short while.
Now i would NEVER recommend speedrunning this game as it's also kind of impossible, i'd say just try to get as many allies as you can and build a strong civil.
At first gameplay feels abit slow and also earning resources is abit slow but you quickly improve yourself same as the A.I.
Also the A.I devoloups quickly same as you and it fights somewhat good in battles it feels like you're not fighting an A.I, still you can get an edge over it so i'd say that's good enough.
So i said alot of things and overall the game is really good but let's start talking about the bugs and the annoying things that we all hate.
First off like i said above ^ the first things you notice is there's not that many battles and or ways to play the game which feels like the just rushed it and also you can't play as every single civil.
And when i said map/world map, the world isn't complete. It's mainly europe and north africa and west asia so it's really not that much, and there's not that much attention to detail, ottoman empire has just 3 territories and all of them are REALLY large, then next to it is just Egypt which feels like there could be way more attention to detail there.
Also when the A.I hates you, they literally hate you, they'll completely deny EVERY single political related crap you send except for improving relations with SO many resources or buying territory/land from them which also feels like they lacked detail there.
Anyways to just not make this longer, Overall the game is great for a 2005 one, If it's under $10 i'd say it's a must own but more than that then it's not worth it unless it gets updated and adds more polish and attention to detail. (mind you the high/ist resolution is 1024x768) so i'd give it a 7/10

An interesting romp through Germany at the end of WWII. If you enjoy FPS games set in this era, you'll probably enjoy the environment. Granted, I could have used more detail in the environment to really get into the story, which in itself could have used some more work.
You play as a lone-wolf sniper tasked with infiltrating Germany at the end of WWII to stop the German Scientists behind the German V2 rocket program.  You're going to quickly forget about that as you play the game. I pretty much finished the game with the thought "I killed a ton of soldiers and maybe a scientist or 2."
I couldn't tell if this game wanted me to play stealth or all out gun-ho.  In several places, especially towards the end, you find yourself in several 12 on 1 situations where getting spotted by some eagle-eyed sniper suddenly triggers a huge firefight.  There's only one weapon that comes with a silencer, so I never picked any other pistol as I didn't want to give myself away.  I rarely ever changed the loadout kit.  I never used the dynamite outside of one mission where I was told to use it.
You're given a sub-machine gun and a pistol to suppliment your rifle, but it's obvious they want you using your rifle all the time.  16 rounds in the pistol, 2 mags worth of sub-machine gun ammo, and 100+ rifle rounds.  You do the math.
It's a nice challenge if you're trying to play stealth. But I found myself trying to rush through it to just end the damn game.  I could have used more stealth ways to eliminate an enemy.  For crying out loud, could I have had a suppressor on a rifle?  Or heck, a combat knife?
I don't think I'll be replaying this unless I need a WWII shooter fix.  Overall: 6/10.

It's not the worst game I've ever played, but I don't think it's worth $10.
The game advertises itself as a music based platformer, with a bit of a heavy emphasis on a competetive multiplayer aspect (which I couldn't test since nobody on my friends list owns this game). Playing through the levels makes me think of a Tron-themed Super Meat Boy, except sometimes the obstacles and so forth are extremely unforgiving (forcing you to completely restart the level if you don't get past). I like challenge, but there is such a thing as too much.
The "music based" part is where the game disappoints me, however. Not because of the soundtrack - the game ships with some incredible music, and even has native support for your MP3s if you decide you don't like what it comes with. The problem however, is in the way the game uses the music; or to put it more accurately, how it
. Occasionally there will be little blinky lights or pulsing disc things that will react to the beat, but nothing seems to react to the music in a way that actually effects the gameplay itself. I don't go faster with higher tempos, the obstacles just travel along the same timing patterns...I could load a slow, sad Sinatra song and get the same game as a high tempo Pendulum track.
If you can pick it up as a freebie somewhere, go ahead, but don't drop $10 on it unless you're incredibly rich.

Resident Evil Code Veronica (Dreamcast, 2000) had better facial movement and expressions.  Gunplay on Red Faction 1 (PS2, 2002) was superior and more varied & interesting.  Settings and location in this game run the gamut from uninspired to boring.  Grey Sci-Fi.  Green Alien Ship.  Grey construction zone.  Grey Industrial zone.  With such a long dev time, you'd think there would at least be one location or gun mechanic that was original somehow.  The size of each loading zone is completely unforgivable.  After shooting down the mothership, there was a loading screen.  You crawl through air vents for 20 seconds and get another loading screen.  Any competent studio could have crapped out a turd like this in 3 months.  The first level of the game perfectly represents the game.  You wake up in a crappy, smelly locker room, and start playing with a piece of crap you fished out of a toilet bowl.  Instead of playing this mass of disappointment, we should have been left waiting for Duke Nukem forever.

+Unparalleled soft body vehicle physics model
+Lots of beautiful, fully customizable stock cars that honestly just 'feel good' to drive
+Awesome environments to drive around in
+TONS of community content, most of which works and feels great. Installing mods is as easy as pressing a button.
+The NG engine even supports aerial vehicles (No stock ones, but several quality mods for everything from bombers to helicopters)
+Throw your car off a ♥♥♥♥ing cliff!!!! Reset, repeat.
+Vehicles now catch on fire if you abuse them enough.
+No huge races but the time rallies are a step in the right direction
+Just go get yourself lost driving around in the jungle or desert. (If you just enjoy driving for what it is, you will LOVE this game.)
-Requires a beefy computer. Not really a con if you have a quality rig, but buyer beware!
-No multiplayer support (but there are rumors it's being worked on)

SOMA is one of the best horror games I've encountered in a long time, because it manages to be so much more than that. I've always been a fan of Frictional Games and I enjoyed Amnesia but I always felt that while Amnesia excelled in its horror aspects, it was sorely lacking in the plot department.
SOMA makes up for all of that. The characters in SOMA are compelling, and I felt incredibly drawn into the story from all of the tidbits of information you find during gameplay. Piecing together the events of whatever horrendous happenings occured at Pathos-II feels like solving a giant puzzle, and not the frustrating or overwhelming kind. The game manages to be philosophical without being cheesy or ham-handed. I felt that it was genuinely offering the player questions about humanity and consciousness while still not coming across as preachy. It wants you to reach your own conclusions.
The actual horror aspect of the game is fantastic. It has its fair share of monsters of all different types, including one with the ability to warp wherever it pleases. The unpredictability of a monster's movement, the hiding and trying desperately to locate the sound of its footsteps--that is what made this game so scary for me. The plot of the game really uplifts this aspect of it in my opinion as well; the monsters are terrifying, yes, but I felt this desire to know
they were and where they came from that I often don't feel in your run-of-the-mill horror game.
I also have to note that Catherine is one of my favorite characters I've ever encountered in a game. I don't want to spoil much, but she is complex and layered in the way a
person is and I really enjoyed having her accompany me throughout the game. SOMA has no desire to present characters that are good or bad, simply flawed, and that is something I love about it.

This game is much better than Magic Duels Origins, which is also on Steam. The majority of negative reviews are complaints that were valid prior to the games' numerous updates which have since taken place. The game is now very well polished, finished, and you can easily earn all of the cards for free if you just put in a bit of time. The roster of available cards here is by far the most fun out of all the DOTP games, and there's a ton of variety to work with. It doesn't take years of grinding to earn the cards either, unlike a certain other, newer installment... The campaign is also pretty good if you care about that, and the AI isn't awful when played on the highest difficulty. The explore feature is pretty cool if you can't handle playing online, although it's less extensively replayable than Origins' version of the feature, the design of the decks you play against is far less repetitive and also far less poorly constructed.
Downsides include a soundtrack that is generally inferior to Magic 2014, the lack of 2headedgiant mode (I don't know why people care so immensely about this, it would be nice to have all kinds of modes in DOTP but there's never been any consistency across the games in that regard.), and an arguably imbalanced meta (Though there's so much variety theoretically available to you that if you have a friend or two you don't need to succumb to the good ole' cloudshift combo, spider spawning combo, Doubling season tokens, Jeskai control sweepers, 20 counterspells Izzet deck, truefire paladin killing you by turn 3, etc. etc.)-but this last point is something inherant in all DOTP games, only this time you get to build your deck so you at least have more freedom to try and combat the meta. While you can also build your deck with Origins, it takes about 10 years to unlock cards that aren't garbage-unless you plan on spending an amount equivalent to real world MTG, which defeats the purpose of playing this game virtually to begin with.
The complaints regarding bugginess and p2w are no longer prevalent in this game, UNLIKE Magic Duels Origins, which is why, in my eyes, this game is currently superior, and will remain so until the newer game on the block becomes both reasonably functional and accessible. Unless you're a 2HG fetishist, in which case this game is worthless to you.

I'm writing this mini-review about 6 hours into the game, which is roughly halfway from what I've heard.  I'll update it and write a proper review when I finish the game.
If you played Alien: Isolation and were hoping for something similar, this probably isn't the game you're looking for.  For as long as I've played it, I've only felt even remotely in danger on four very brief occasions, two of which were caused by what I consider to be cases of poor environment design.
I didn't go into SOMA expecting exactly the same type of game as Alien: Isolation but I think I was spoiled by my prior experience with it.  I unavoidably find myself drawing mental comparisons between the two; for example, where SOMA tries to occasionally give you a scare by playing creepy noises, in A:I those noises would've been made by a real, dangerous thing that's actively hunting you.
SOMA instead seems to put most of its focus on storytelling and this isn't an inherently bad thing by any means.  However, while the setting and plot are quite unique, most of the twists I've seen so far have been aggressively foreshadowed to such an extent that the payoff was ruined when they were finally "revealed".
While I do have some mild complaints with parts of the game's design, I'm still enjoying myself so I'm giving the game a thumbs-up for now.

Overall "Amnesia: The Dark Descent" could have been a great game--all the ingredients were there.  It fell pretty flat, however.
I've found that some of the game mechanics are incredibly annoying and detract from the story and gaming experience.  First, light plays too big a role; if you don't stand in the pool of torchlight or have your lantern out (it has limited fuel), then you lose something called "sanity".  What purpose does this serve?  Does it serve to manage how often I use the lantern?  Nope, the limited fuel availability does that.  The second major issue I have with this game has to do with the creatures you encounter.  They generally appear with no purpose other than to provide "now its time to evade/hide" moments.  Further, once the creatures see you, they "know" where you are despite extinguishing light sources; you cannot hide in the shadows or around corners once spotted.
These two problems detract greatly from the "flashback" style storytelling throughout the game.  There doesn't appear to be much purpose behind the appearance of the monsters at any particular time, other than to provide a level of difficulty in completing an objective.  Overall the game suffers tremendously from these problems, and so I can't recommend Amnesia: The Dark Descent.

I am absolutely horrible at this game. I don't think I've won anything outside of the tuturial missions, but while I don't play it much because of that, I can definitely recognise the amount of quality there is in this game.
OTC is a RTS game, but instead of combat being the focus, it's economics. There is no military in this game, the game is built entirely around buying, producing and selling resources in order to become the best trading company on Mars. The economics, from my understanding, is easy to learn, hard to master. Essentially buying increases value, and selling decreases value, so the main layer of strategy in this game is balancing income, making sure you're not in too much debt, and keeping the economy stable. There's also the more questionable side of business, involving buying extra land off the black market, sabotaging competitors, and hacking the market to directly increase or decrease the value of goods.
It's pretty hard, and I don't think I'll ever get how to play it well, but it's interesting and I would definitely recommend it to people who like RTS games, but want something with a unique twist.

What is this game about?:
This is an economic RTS simulator that takes place on Mars. Matches will take around 15-30 minutes depending on how many people you are playing with. This is not a epic-scale game like Civilization!  So you, the player can choose between 4 different factions. The 4 different factions are: Expansive, Robotic, Scientific and Scavenger. Every factions has there ups and downs and you want to use the best faction that you think is good on set random map.
Gameplay:
-Ingame you will have a market window on the left for all the market prices and all the rescource units you might have. This is where all the buying and selling will be taken place.
-In the middle of the screen is where most of the action takes plays. On the map you build buildings that produce rescources which cost claims where you have limited number of. Because of this you need to plan your way through
-On the right top side is where you and other players companies stocks are. The goal to win a game is very simple. Buy every other company out by buying there stock. Each company has 10 stocks. You can buy someone out by having a majority of there stock (6 stocks=60%) or if they bought there own 5 stocks already, you can buy those 5 stocks, double the price, in 1 go.
-To combat the company that is leading a match there is something called the blackmarket. The blackmarket is on the right bottom side of the screen and will have a set of different items. Some items are there for to shutdown the production of your opponents or to boost your own production.
What has the game to Offer?:
-9 Tutorials which are very well done and explain you the game. after every tutorial you pass it will be a bit harder for you which is nice.
-Campaign which consist of 9 different leaders which have there own set of different buildings. You play 6 different matches where you buy into the colony and not a Company. After that there is a final match where you need to buyout the remaining 3 companies. Note: prices are going to be crazy in this mode. Campaign takes about 4-5 hours.
-Skirmish mode up to 8 Players.
-Daily Challenge. Everyone gets the same map and restrictions and you will be competing to get the best time. There is also a leaderboard for that and you can watch replays from other players to see what they did differently.
-Ranking System(online). 1vs1 is available on Monday through Thursday and 4 FFA Friday through Sunday.
-Custom Lobby games(online). Just skirmish matches with your own rules against real people or with/against AI.
-Well balanced AI
-Different types of game modes.

There is a really strong caveat in recommending this, which is that the tags on the store page are extremely deceptive.  This is not an economic game, this is not a simulation game, this is not a trading game, and this is not a base building game.  This is a very fast paced, micro-intensive RTS.
Its an interesting take on the RTS genre, because you don't have any units to control.  But make no mistake, this game plays very similarly to one of the micro practice maps for SC2, and uses essentially the same skillset.  Its just that instead of microing units around a map, you're constantly scanning the map, spamming abilities, and hitting the buy/sell button.  I know it may sound like this is fundamentally different from microing units around, but in practice its not.
If you're someone who likes the micro game in SC2, you'll like this game.  If you're a more casual RTS player then this probably isn't the game for you.
There's nothing wrong with that, and the game itself is quite well done, but the game is definitely targetted towards a relatively small niche and the store page/reviews in no way reflect that.

I am very pleased to give this game the thumbs up - I own it since its launch on Steam. I had a feeling it will grow well and achieve a good level of greatness by the time it was finihsed. Coming back to it now, over 9 months later, I cannot help but enjoy what the developer (Sören Johnson was the lead designer of Civilization 4) has achieved. Regardless whether in single player or multiplayer, you are treated to a fast-paced, ever-be-on-your-toes gameplay. To me, this is the best fast-paced economic sim I have ever played.
So, let's take a look at the good and the bad.
The GOOD:
1. Extremely engaging gameplay - that, to me, outweighs everything else. The game is built in such a way that keeps you on your toes all the time. A small slip-up may result in a loss. I can tell you, there are some real sharks out there.
2. Strategic Thinking + Awareness combo wins the game - you need to know exactly what you want and how to manipulate the situation you have been put in. You need to play a few moves ahead and you need to be ready to adapt and commit to the plan you have in your head.
3. Great single player - the developers have really programmed the AI well, as I expected of them. Even on lower difficulties (say, Employee or Assistant) the AI may suprise you and even buy you out in a skirmish game. In addition to that there is a great campaign (explained in #11), daily challenges, leaderboards, pretty much everything to satisfy your single player demands.
4. Multiplayer is damn good - but be aware, there are people out there who have played the game for a long time and will destroy a newcomer in no time. I know I have 26 hours in the game and got trashed. Do not get disheartened and do your best to learn and improve.
5. You can pick from a number of companies to lead to victory - and each one plays differently to boot! It is quite surprising just how much a dependence on one resource can affect a game, and how huge of a replayability it may provide. You may opt to play the sneaky scavengers, the tech-crazy scientists, the extremely expansive... um... Expansive corporation that gains extra claims on plots, or the Robots, which need no sustenance, but have to replace their parts and chips in a timely fashion.
6. Many ways to victory - while in skirmish the goal remains the same, to be the last man standing, there are many ways to achieve it. You are given lots of obvious and subtle ways to do so. Do not take your eys off that black market, I can tell you that much... or for the same reason off the resource table... or the shares table... uh, I am quite sure that you get my drift.
7. Many hours of enjoyment - due to its awesome replayability, you will easily be looking at 20+ hours of enjoyment, more if you want to test every corporation in various situations, and then go ahead and do some skirmishes, play through the campaign, do the daily challenges, and maybe play online vs other people.
8. An extremely pleasant music - the soundtrack is awesome, very nice and relaxing.
9. Good tutorial comprising of ways to teach you how to win, a number of practice games vs the AI up to Manager difficulty, and in my opinion, a great design decision to have you actually win a game in skirmish first before diving into the campaign. The campaign can be a bit overwhelming, I can tell you that from experience. The AI won't sit back and let you feel smart, MLG Pro gamer. It will crush you like a maggot if you don't play well.
10. Post-game statistics - the post-game statistics have been improved and made even more in-depth, much to my delight. I really like taking a long hard look at them and analyze what I did wrong or not.
11. Great single player campaign -  In its essence, you are given 7 weeks worth of challenges, with your chosen company, vs 3-4 AIs of a difficulty that you choose in the beginning of the campaign. From week 1 to 6, you use the cash you make to improve an AI colony by buying any of the 4 upgrades for it over a 7 day period. The winner with the most purchases gets the best weekly cash bonus. In the final week of the campaign, you enter a skirmish match with the top 4 companies left and to win you must buy them out. Each company starts with a number of upgrades, and you can hire additional staff either for a week or permanently to further boost a building's efficiency (you can boost a windmill's energy output, a metal mine's efficiency so that a single metal mine supports 3 steel mills, etc.). Then you are allowed to select one of the 3 missions given to you. Each one of them carries a different challenge which is clearly explained (example: limited resources, black market items, special conditions, etc.) and satisfies a certain earthbound sponsor (UN, USA, Russia, China), which, gives you another reward (like extra claims, better scans, etc.). Depending on how well you do on the mission, you get to carry more week-based revenue home and use it for further upgrades to your production buildings. And if you think that's not enough - you can even unlock a secondary or even tertiary sponsor and use it on a certain mission! Limited water with a scientific? Play robotic then!
Now, let's take a look at the BAD:
1. The graphics - call me weird, but I actually preferred the basic Early Access, more blocky and sci-fi-ish graphics. Since then, the game evolved into a more colorful, cartoonish look, which to my taste, was unnecessary. It sure gets the job done, but not for me.
2. The UI - the UI underwent a number of changes, which in my opinion made it more complex than it needed to be, with way more tabs and sub-tabs than necessary. Coming back to the game 9 months later, I was a bit overwhelmed myself for the first 5 minutes of play. Granted, I managed to make my way easily around it, but for a new player it will be a lot to process.
3. Punishing AI - yep, that could be a bad thing. If you are not ready to play vs tough AI who can exploit your mistakes, best stick to the lowest difficulties or... stay away from the game.
4. While a number of changes were made, the game did not change dramatically from the first early access build. But then again, the starter build was already quite good, polished, and enjoyable.
5. Huge skill difference in online games - many people who play online since alpha have way better understanding, time proven tactics and thus, the upper hand on someone who's just starting.
6. The price is a huge gripe for many people, and I can understand why. Yesterday, I was looking through my mails to see for just how much did I buy this game, and I was very surprised to find that I got it for 18,50€, which is roughly half of what it costs now. I would argue, that if you watched youtubers play it 9 months ago, that you should have already realized its potential and bought the game. However, on the other side I can totally understand how people like to wait till a game exits early access first, and then buy it. For them, the price tag will be high.
7. Last, but not least, the game suffers from the snowball effect. Once you get ahead, and if you know what you are doing, you will most likely stay ahead till the end of the game. That is a tad off-putting to some gamers, but I can tell you from experience, you can still turn it around... to a point. Then you just lose :)
Conclusion:
If you are willing to forgive the current price tag, this game is an easy buy for gamers who enjoy economic games comprised of a lot of wheeling and dealing, tormenting their opponents by scamming (cook the books for the win), crashing the market, freezing their best production plots for a time, boosting your own effectivenes, destroying their resources (underground nukes, yay!), or even toying with them as they spiral into huge debt. I, personally, find the game a great experience and am looking forward to playing the new and improved campaign, learn the new tricks and quirks of the game, and enjoying myself thoroughly in the process.

Greetings Everyone!  Moving quickly on my next game we have Stellar Impact.  I’ve made it a point to go back into my library and find old games like this to review with a hope to find them better than I left them.  Many times I approach a game like this expecting to only spend a few hours with them before issuing my review because nothing has changed or the community is now dead.  Many times I am proven wrong…this is not one of those times.
Creeps in Space:  So, what kind of game do we have here?  Essentially it is a MOBA that meets space combat in a 2d plane.  In many ways this might have been more at home in a naval environment but I’ve played many 2d space games that I’ve enjoyed greatly.  Instead of champions we have ships and skillshots are replaced by…skillshots with big cannons I guess.  To be honest I’m going by my memory here and the tutorial I replayed because…
Dead Space:  Okay, let’s get this out of the way…the community is dead.  In the several days I checked the servers I never saw more than a handful of players and never saw any public games to join.  To make matters worse there seems to be no way to play against bots which is a shame because when I played this game originally it was an interesting take on the MOBA Genre.  You will see a few vocal players shouting that the game isn’t dead but it really, really is.  I know it may suck but if you want an MOBA there are much more popular ones out there but this one did have a glimmer of originality.
Flashing Lights:  Due to the game being several years old and from an indie developer as well I want to give the game a pass but I can’t.  It just feels like a mobile game in almost every way.  Now that I think of it, this game could make an outstanding browser game or mobile through a tablet.  The game defaults to 4:3 resolution which immediately concerns me whenever a game does that, the graphics really don’t push in any meaningful direction (slight pass as you want your MOBA to work on any system).  I’m fairly sure my cell phone could handle this game.  I was planning on droning on but really all this is moot, the community is dead and there really is no way to play offline (bots).
To be honest this review is a bit like the game, dead and really a waste of time; like the game, no one will probably read this.  I am mainly doing this in an attempt to formulate my thoughts on games like this that have now died out.  Back to the case at hand however, don’t buy this game, wouldn’t even recommend it for free unless you have a good set of friend who would want to play it as well.  If you do, I hope you enjoy.

UBERMOSH is an arcade game about cutting bullets with a sword, in a gun-filled cyberpunk mosh pit.
A fast paced top down shooter and slasher, this game is, in a word, fun. Its addicting, easy to learn, hard to master, and just a great indie game.
The gameplay is you start with a sword and ricochet projectiles at your enemies by reflecting. The reflected projectile kills your foes instantly, and you cut also rush an enemy and cut them instantly too. A dead enemy always drops a gun you can borrow. Each class you play has a varying amount of lives, and can be orientated towards a shooter or a slasher role. The Warlock starts off with the strongest gun in the game, and can reflect bullets, but also only has 2 lives. The no mod class/GREEN(The default class) starts with no gun, 4 lives, and can reflect bullets. Kansai starts off with 6 lives, and a sword, but can't grab guns. Gunner has 2 lives and a fully automactic gun, and can make any weapon, even the strongest weapon automactic.
Only real problem with this game is a lack of content. Theres a Hardboiled mode, and 4 classes with alternate roles, some Steam achievements, and of course Trading Cards. However, the trading cards really have had their value dropped by a ridiuclous amount($0.24 to now $0.07). If this game had local multiplayer, that would be so amazing...*hint hint game developer*
To anyone who enjoys addicting fast paced gameplay, I highly recommend this game. Its speed, pumping electric soundtrack, fast paced action, low price, just mix together to make this one of the best games i've played in a long time.

UBERMOSH is a great arcade twin-stick bullet hell shooter with a cyberpunky retro aesthetic. I recommend this game to anyone who likes pick-up and play games with a good dose of challenge, personality and a classic feeling to them.
It's very basic; you get put into an area with endless enemies and you want to try to get as many kills as you can within 90 seconds or until you run out of lives. You can pick up any of the guns the enemies drop, and slice enemy shots with your sword to split them and send them back. It's simple, but fantastic and satisfying. The guns really feel like they pack a punch because of their sound effects and a minor screen shake whenever you shoot.
You can somewhat change the experience by changing class mod, which can either take away your sword but give you rapid fire, or take away your ability to shoot so you have to rely on cutting enemy bullets as your only means of attacking. There isn't a whole lot of variety in the content, but if you like this content you can easily play it for hours on end, or keep it installed to play from time to time when you've got some minutes to kill. It's also got the right amount of challenge, since it has a learning curve and is unforgiving from the start, but once you get the hang of the gameplay and patterns it's doable and just a blast.
It's definitely worth the 2 bucks it goes for, and during a sale it will be a steal. Grab the pack, even, and get several great games for nearly no money.

This game is tough, but has a ton of potential. If you don't know your build path or your character well enough being pushed out of your build path is BRUTAL. Let alone when your backup area is occupied on top of that. In this game, you have to adapt to the game pace set by other players. Due to the search function to find items/resources to build greater items also being able to find players (I don't know how you could reasonably fix this without slowing the game pace, so the devs can't really change that aspect). Sometimes if you end up panicking or haven't learnt hotkeys for searching and pulling the map up, those precious seconds wasted could cost your life. That can end up being really anti climactic for unready players.
However, when the above ideas are mastered or at least executed to an adequate extent, this game is a really really fun representation of the battle royale genre with a strong and rewarding strategy twist that sets it apart from any other game in the genre that are typically FPS - instead Black Survival kind of incorporates an RPG into the game.
I kinda suck at the game tbh (14.5 hrs into the game currently), but I can see my weaknesses and hope to improve it. You can't just copy paste a build and expect to be at the same level as those that play the game at a high level. There is no "best" build. The great players from the good vary their builds based on the items they get from searching to. This rewards skill and game knowledge but "slower" or more casual players get left behind. Play this game knowing you're entering a competitive environment and you better be up on your A game while dealing with shifting scenarios from being pressured out and bullied from your preferred starting areas, or the areas you need to get that flower for that premier healing item are all occupied by other strong contenders. Be aware that the matchmaking is fair but doesn't account for when you really are still pretty newb to the game, so you can't really sit back every now and then, try out something wacky and expect to win, especially not until you really understand the core of the game's crafting system.
Overall <3 this game, would recommend it to anyone that appreciates a strategy spin and doesn't mind pumping up their competitive spirit to favour the battle royale aspects of the game. The lore for each character/create and sturdily-set setting are all great bonuses to add to this game's replayability.

B) "Can't escape Jason teleport onto you lol". Answer: When your screen does the big stutter VHS effects - dont run in a straight line holding your♥♥♥♥♥♥ move side to side a little.... it kind... makes it...harder... (git gud).
Just felt like adding this - I never watched F13, I didn't kickstart, I'm not some fanboy. I just don't want to see a genuinely fun game tarnished by people whose Mummy wont lend them her credit card or who won't spend a few hours learning how the game works. ty.
(As promised, I'll give a few details and my actual thoughts about the game)
+ When the teamwork happens (using VOIP and various strategies, it's wonderful)
+ Genuinely tense moments when Jason is chasing you
+ Jason is "OP" and amazingly fun to play
+ There is a progression system, you "gamble" your points for perks! Pretty fun
+/- Graphics are okay, but not amazing - but good enough to be immersed and have fun
- Controls are annoying, cant remap them and pretty easy to close the door from the wrong side (its the same button) and find yourself trapping yourself with Jason if not careful
- If the team doesn't coordinate, it isnt so fun and you lose
To the people who say that "Jason is OP, survivors have no chance - I say it simply isnt true. You "NEED" VOIP, after that, hope there is at least a couple of survivors with VOIP who will communicate and use teamwork. I find this happens in about 80% of the games I played. Jason isnt so OP when you taunt him into entering the shack you're in - straight into a bear trap and some sporty dude with high strength ♥♥♥♥♥ him over the back of the head with a baseball bat - knocking him out.
I had some amazing moments - planning in a hut with two german guys with athletic characters who went to give Jason the run around whilst my chick (with high intelligence) quickly repaired the car with the parts we stashed so we could all make the escape. (Amazingly funny moments as you don't have time to let the fat guy inside the car and all drive off together as he screams in despair!)
This really is a team game, and learning the survivors strengths and weaknesses. Alot of the negativity comes from people with low game time not understanding they need to communicate and use the synergy of the characters. When this is learnt and pulled off correctly - Jason doesnt have such an easy time.
All in all - survivor is fun, but team-work is needed (and not always possible depending on your team mates). Jason is fun full stop, staring at your prey through the window and watching them panic is just so, so good! They need to fix the controls and a few other small bugs, which I'm pretty sure they will.
Is it worth $40? Not compared to some other games, which will give you alot more content for half the price - but this is also the best (by far) in the genre (as far as I know). If you like the genre and can afford the $40, then it is worth it.
Believe me - 6 councillors with their own strengths and weaknesses working together as one can lead to Jason battered on the floor, mask knocked off and you and your buddies cruising away in a car cheering together.

Rush Bros is a hardcore platformer taking after the likes of Super Meat Boy, but fails to understand any aspect of why people enjoy these type of games.  Precise controls, level consistency, and a feeling of fairness all elude this game and that makes it impossible recommend.
The game's gimmick is that parts of the level move with the beat of the current music track playing.  It's an interesting idea but one that shouldn't have gone past the prototyping phrase, where it should have been discovered how badly it works out in practice.  This includes traps and not every object responds to every beat, which when mixed together with the sub-par beat detection makes this movement almost impossible to accurately predict.  This also causes certain songs to make certain levels ridiculously hard, if not impossible.  A few of the later levels take this mechanic to such extremes, I firmly believe that they are some of the worst levels ever included in any game.
The other main issue with the level design is invisible traps.  Pretty much every level has spikes, but some of them in some levels will shoot at you when you get close.  There's no way to tell which ones will do this.  Spikes will even shoot at you from off screen with no warning.  What this unfortunately results in is rather than skill-based platforming, you simply have to memorize the levels to do well.  That's not real difficulty, it's poor design.
These problems combined with sloppy controls can make this game very frustrating and it's not hard to see why over 90% of the reviews are negative.  While I did enjoy the music the game has to offer, it would be better to save your sanity and pass on this one.

So you wanna try Duke Nukem Forever despite its bad reception? I'm assuming it's on sale and your willing to throw away five bucks for a game that might give you some hours of decent entertainment, but I won't deny that DNF could provide some players with a satisfying experience.
Duke Nukem Forever is an old-styled FPS with a modern makeover...
what the devs would like to trick you into believing. Actually, Duke Nukem Forever is your standard shooter from the early 2010's with very little old-school about it. It reuses the narrative theming of the original shooter but borrows little from the original's gameplay, and that's a bad thing.
Try to picture your generic FPS from the 2010's and you got the gist of Duke Nukem's gameplay. Linear levels, 2-4 weapon slots, regenerating health, cutscenes, action setpieces feautring QTEs, and a smaller array of enemies. The devs use a smaller array of enemies compared to DN3D and designed certain classes of enemies to have varying firearms, but it all just feels samey when over 75% of enemies you encounter are a reskin of the soldier-with-a-gun enemy archetype.
One of the game's biggest sins is limiting the amount of guns Duke can carry. The player is limited to 2-4 guns at any given time and trust me the devs had to scale back the complexity of enemy encounters to accommodate the fact that the player can only carry two weapons.
And the weapons aren't particularly great either. Many of them are a variant on the rapid-fire assault rifle archetype and not all of them are adequately powerful. I stuck with Ripper because it felt good to use.
Keeping on with the modern touches of DNF, Duke regenerates health over time (or 'ego' as the game calls it). I don't think regenerating health is an interesting gameplay mechanic and in most other games I'd consider it a big problem however in DNF I almost welcome because it makes sense that a big macho guy like Duke Nukem would literally walk off any kind of injury he takes.
The linear levels of DNF might be game's biggest flaws. They're linear, like you would assume. This is total contrast to the delightfully open-ended levels of the DN3D. Despite taking place in similar urban environments like the original, none of the environments feel like they're supposed to thanks to rampant linearity and a lack of mechanical character within the levels. Occasionally you'll get to play around with some level objects and increase your maximum health, but that's barely enough.
And the places you'll venture through are varied but not inspired. You got casinos, desert highways, alien hives and even hydroelectric dams. If you got a taste for urban warfare, DNF at least has that going for it.
The game tries to mix up pacing by adding in vehicle portions or setpieces where Duke is shrunk to miniature size, but those twists don't do too much to make the game fun.
Many of these actions sequences go on too long, especially the “mini-Duke drives a RC car” sequence in the beginning and the “Duke drives a monster truck across the desert highway” sequence toward the end. It's filler and in the cases of Duke getting shrunk down, that just seems odd in a super-masculine story like DNF. Duke getting shrunk happened in the original but it was for a short sequence and was a key to solving a puzzle.
Speaking of puzzles, Duke Nukem has them and although some are a little too gamey and uncharacteristic of DNF, many are acceptable. For all of its modernizations, DNF does not have an arrow on the player's interface telling them where to go next. The game allows the player to figure out how to get to the next room or progress and oftentimes it requires exploration or using a weapon in a creative way, which works with the game's style.
In this latest edition of the Duke Nukem saga, the story is more cinematic as expected in a modernization of a classic shooter. More swearing, more boobs, more violence. It's not drastically different from the original DN3D but DNF doesn't have the same vibe.
I'm sure the developers put in all the sexiness and machismo in good fun but with how better and more “realistic” the presentation of DNF is compared to the originals, the character of DNF grows old quickly and becomes tiring and unlikeable. The original didn't shove its humour and spunk down your throat every minute so even if you don't like the sexualization of bodacious babes or the overly machismo attitude of Nukem, you weren't suffocated by any elements you found unpleasant.
There is an audience to Duke Nukem Forever. If you don't mind overly long levels, driving set pieces, boobs, juvenile humour, and outdated celebrity jokes you might dig Duke Nukem Forever. The best things I can say about it is some guns feel really good to shoot and sometimes the linear level design is inspired in how it directs the player.
If you don't fall within that bullseye of a recommendation, you're better off playing something else.

When I did look into it though, the information  was already enough to sway me into buying, hearing that it was a similar to the likes of Empire Total War. This however being a budget title, very cheap, and well did not take too much of a computer to run. That’s the basis of what convinced me to buy it, currently having  quite a weak laptop to run games on, so I gave it a try.
When you first get into this game, it does take a while to progress through the campaign, its often very confusing at the start as-well. You can start to see the elements in which are similar to Empire TW, but do notice that its clearly not as good, which brought this game down for me. As I said earlier, it takes a while to actually do anything in this game, and so need to be patient, keeping it calm in the early stages. Im going to be honest, you attack anyone early on, your going to get f***ed up pretty easily. Once you have an army etc, it gets interesting, you can trade, form alliances, but that’s pretty much it. While playing this game it always felt as if I was playing a decent title though, graphics are good for the age, but you do have to realise that this game really is just for those who cannot run Empire. I would not purchase this game if I had Empire Total War there in my library, I just wouldn’t! I played a lot of video games in my youth. But I put them away when I reached adulthood. But one day I saw the BeamNG Drive trailer and was impressed. And so for the first time in about 20 years, I bought a video game.  Yes, only a game this good could break my 20 year drought!
This is seriously the best video game I have ever played! The game offers the rare combination of being simple yet profound. It's uncomplicated to play, but allows you to do so much. The producers continue to innovate with each new update, making the game better and better and more interesting. The graphics and maps are often visually stunning with incredible detail. Many of the maps are so interesting with so much to do, they could almost be separate video games themselves. Plus, I love how other people can create maps, vehicles and props for the game.
I also love the flexibility the game provides. In free roam, you can make up your own missions and goals. As well, if you're short on time, you can teleport to any place on the map, rather than spend time driving there. One of the game's best features is the soft-body physics technology, which makes crashes exceedingly realistic. Plus, there are almost endless ways you can damage and crash your car. It never gets old! It's so powerful that rather than merely playing a game, you're having a new experience! Just be aware the game is demanding on your computer. A graphics card is recommended but not required, if you have a pretty good computer. However, a few minor  features in the game may not available without a graphics card.
In sum, BeamNG Drive equals video games at their best. BeamNG Drive is the quintessential driving, crashing and racing video game and the gold standard. I believe this game will be the top video game of the 21st century. Don't miss out and give it a whirl!

I have played Nether for about 12 hours now and I think this game is amazing and worth way more than 15 dollars. Many of the things that people complain about have either been fixed or not even a problem from what I've played in the game.
-Item Spawning:
I have played on many servers and only once have I starved to death. It really depends on your specific server. On some servers, yes I have had a very difficult time finding any items at all, but on others I spawn in and instantly have some BroMax, Crunchy Bens, water, guns, bandages, you name it. Almost any gas station I go in there is usually loads of food and supplies. Only a couple servers have yeilded very limited supplies.
-Community/Player Interaction
This is the main downside of Nether because finding an enemy often means finding death. Although more times than I have been killed, I find another player and I type in the chat "Friend". We then go on to not kill eachother and sometimes even give eachother items. One time a person saw my friend almost shot him, but decided to give him a battle axe instead. Once I even spawned into a game and then a guy added me into his group then gave me weapons. We are actually friends on steam now. One more thing, I try to join the server with the least people possible which usually lowers the chance of being found. Joining a server with 30+ people is just asking to be killed.
-Safe Zones
Safe zones are scattered around the map and contrary to popular belief are very safe except during Nether attacks. I have gone to safe zones hundreds of times and never been ambushed. I have never seen campers. Not once. Now, I have been killed on my way to a safe zone before, but that was from nethers and not real people. Once in the safe zone there are numerous different things to do: Buying, selling, trading, weapon crafting, giving boxes for money, or depositing items to store until later. Once you leave a safe zone you have about 12 seconds until you can take damage again or shoot again. During and after that time I have never been targeted by a player. Anybody who has problems with that has really really bad luck.
-Deaths
Nether is based off a lose all system so when you complain about losing everything then it sucks that the game worked how its supposed to. Although, due to recent patches and the bank system, losing all does not really happen. First of all, if you find something good then run to a safe haven, deposit that stuff and your good to go. Also, now there is and account level system which lets you level up and never lose those levels. It's permanent. It may take time to level up but it is definitely worth it and you can get awesome bonuses like free money on spawn, more health, more hunger, more damage, and many more. You still lose your levels on your player like stealth and stamina when you die, but those levels are actually extremely easy to get back. Kill one or two nethers and you're already level three. A simple solution to not losing your stuff is not dying. It is truthfully not difficult to stay alive for a long time if you crouch or crawl when near golems or the new flying nether. The other nether is typically very easy to kill. Like I sead before the player interaction is not two bad in small servers or if you have nicer people on the server. Also, only one monster actually has the ability to call other monsters to you and that monster only takes two hits with a kitchen knife (the starting knife). If that monster does call others in though, you are screwed unless you have good weapons. That's why you got to kill the calling guys when you can.
-Settings
As of now Nether has limited settings although it has enough graphical settings to go from pretty bad quality to a beautiful game. Brightness is one key setting that Nether is missing, but it does not really get that dark. Even with my monitor at 60% brightness, I can see very well and not to dark even in the darkest atmosphere which is probably the subway. Also, as far as I can tell, mob spawning is the same in any time of day.
-Level Up System
The level system in this game is really good and you can improve almost anything you want. I usually go for stamina and stealth mostly, but other trees are good too. As I said in the death section, you do lose all your levels but it is quite easy to get them back again. The one suggestion I have is for an armor/health level up.
-Microtransactions
A lot of people complained about microtransactions, but in really they are not a problem at all. Any microtransactions you can get are very limited and only for cosmetic items, easily making this game a play2win not pay2win.
-Transportation
The map can be very difficult to travel across, but thankfully a new update added atvs which allow for extremely fast travel across the map. Granted, the vehicle is very rare and very glitchy. I found an atv once and ended up crashing it, but it was really fun.
-Graphics
The game itself looks beautiful with all the settings at max and besides some visual glitches it is amazing. The visual glitches include some floating ground or objects here and there, but not enough to ruin the experience or the gameplay. Another problem is hitboxes on items or hills which sometimes allow for floating people or hiding inside of walls. This is an early access game so these will probably be fixed in later updates.
Overall I would definitely recommend this game to almost anybody and give it a 9/10 for a few problems. There is a great supply of items usually. I rarely starve. Player griefing is very limited depending on the servers you join. The best option is to join servers with very little people. Safe zones are always safe except for when they are attacked by nether. Player camping is very rare. The deaths can be prevented by having good weapons and being careful around certain Nethers. It is also not completely lose everything. The settings on the game are somewhat limited but you have enough to make the game look amazing. The level up system is very indepth and you can level up a lot of things. The microtransactions are easily ignored and only for cosmetic items. The current transportation system with cars is very glitchy and hard to get a car, but it was just added so I will give it some time. Finally, the graphics in this game are astounding and besides a couple visual errors are almost as good as or even better than Battlefield 4 graphics.

Offworld Trading Company is a new genre of game, which is a blend of several styles into its own new style. A fine balance bringing to the table an awesome game.
On some sides, it reminds me of the old RTS Monopoly Tycoon, with the multiplayer capitalism management on one hand and the real time business sim on the other hand. (The auction system is by the way fantastic !) While at the same time, the game is grand by its simplicity of the resources manegement and strategy planning, maybe similar to Settlers with the logistics supply chain of raw materials up to the final produces.
This game can enter into the History of Gaming, that it is at the same time a smart game, with in depth game anaylyzis without having dozens of parameters, just a few interesting resources with different rules and needs which intricately are depending on each other in a beautiful supply and demand concept.
And at the same time, it is a game fun to play, where you don't have to learn dozens of recipes, where you quickly have fun (a few tutorials teach you the basic ropes of the game, same as chess, the game can be learnt in a very short time, but it can require a long time to master :)!). Lots of events occur in game, which can change the whole course of a development, pirates intercepting your cargos, mutiny of your geothermal powerplant at the very wrong time... well you get the picture hehe !
You might be thinking that this game sounds like a very long game to play, spending hours of planification, development and implementation ... such as a Heart of Iron, Total War or a Civ game for instance ... well not at all, the games lasts hardly more than 30 minutes ! And this is in the case you are not losing after a few minutes!
All in all, this game, is, I believe, refreshing with its new genre, smart with its simple but challenging puzzles mechanics for the colonization of Mars, all this while having a good fun when utilizing the resources of the planet.
The question is ... will you challenge yourself ... go play this legendary Offworld Trading company ?

I feel the need to actually go ahead and post a quick review on this particular game. A quick bit of background about myself. When I originally saw Dead Island, I had absolutely 0 interest in the game. All I saw was the beach scene, over and over again, as my friends attempted to play it. I gave up on watching, but happen to run into the game again when it went free on Xbox. I decided to give it another go, and became quickly addicted. The story, weapon customization, and enemy designs were enough to keep me going. I ended up cranking out the game in 2 days and Riptide soon after that.
As for Dead Island: Escape....well this is a different story. I will admit that I enjoy the art style of this game, and the combat can certainly be enjoyable at times. However, that is about where my enjoyment for the game ends. What Deep Silver had here, was an opportunity to create a short story in a fun artstyle that expanded on the Dead Island universe, so that we might be held over until Dead Island 2. What we recieved instead, was a game with unlikable characters, repetitive level designs and backtracking, rehased enemies and a dissapointing story. The last 15 minutes of the game had me so frustrated and disengaged that I considered just giving up on finishing the game. However, I pushed through and can safely say that I was extremely dissapointed in the direction that they decided to take with the story, at the end.
In the end, I managed to get this game and the DLC on sale for $5 on greenmangaming this past week. However, I can't not say that I would not pay that much again for this game. It had such potential to be a short, sweet log into the Dead Island universe....If you are thinking of purchasing the game, save yourself the money and frustration and just look up any backstory from this entry online.
TLDR: Pro/Con List:
Pro: +Artstyle is appealing
+Combat can be rewarding at times
Cons: -Dissapointing story
-Rehashed areas and backtracking
-Unlikable characters
-Repetitive enemy design
-No unique weapon custimization

While this game may not have the charm of M&B:Warband, it definitely scratches that itch to command an army of musket wielding troops and watch them pepper an army of idiot peasants trying to run screaming away from you.
The game itself is much like the rest of the series, start out with almost nothing but the weapons and a horse you are assigned by difficulty, then complete 'quests', join a faction and try to rule the world.  A cast of semi interesting characters join you on your ride through fake history as you lay waste to the country-side.
The customizable troops you can get is a nice touch, and if you get enough cash (eventually you will via plunder or trade) you can effectively travel with an army of epic geared troops, slaughtering everything in your (or your lords) name.
Story?  Bah who needs one in this style of game?  Your story is the story, basically making it so you yourself get to design your own story by destroying army after army.  Or die trying.  And stuff.
Open world games are easy to get lost in, and while the graphics are dated (but being able to display 200+ troops in a FPS styled RTS is impressive in it's own right) there are worse things in life.
I strongly recommend this game for people who wish that M&B had muskets instead of crossbows, as while the story isn't a big leap, the combat definitely feels fresh.  Skyrim this may not be, but in Skyrim you can't honestly lead 200+ troops around attacking people/villages at random or capture yourself a few castles without some serious modding.
Also look into the mods/DLC for this game if you like multiplayer, the community is pretty cool.

Got this for free, and after seeing the metacritic scores I wasn't sold. I decided to try it anyway, but let me tell you now, the Steam reviews are right about this one. I really liked the emphasis on sniping; something that modern shooters put on the backburner or ignore although. I miss my days of MW2 sniping, but this game, although only slightly, reminded me of that. I love the x-ray/slowmo shots and the prepartion and calculation you must make before you attack. It makes it a little less braindead that the other games. It is so satisfying to land a perfect headshot after carefully lining up a shot; its just something that is not rewarded anymore with the arrival of no-scoping and quick-scoping. Overall, the gameplay is fun, although my one gripe is that all guns beside the snipers are garbage, but I guess thats why its called Sniper Elite. Story is forgettable, but not bad, although a little too short. Would recommend at the ~$10-15 price range. 7/10

B) "Can't escape Jason teleport onto you lol". Answer: When your screen does the big stutter VHS effects - dont run in a straight line holding your♥♥♥♥♥♥ move side to side a little.... it kind... makes it...harder... (git gud).
Just felt like adding this - I never watched F13, I didn't kickstart, I'm not some fanboy. I just don't want to see a genuinely fun game tarnished by people whose Mummy wont lend them her credit card or who won't spend a few hours learning how the game works. ty.
(As promised, I'll give a few details and my actual thoughts about the game)
+ When the teamwork happens (using VOIP and various strategies, it's wonderful)
+ Genuinely tense moments when Jason is chasing you
+ Jason is "OP" and amazingly fun to play
+ There is a progression system, you "gamble" your points for perks! Pretty fun
+/- Graphics are okay, but not amazing - but good enough to be immersed and have fun
- Controls are annoying, cant remap them and pretty easy to close the door from the wrong side (its the same button) and find yourself trapping yourself with Jason if not careful
- If the team doesn't coordinate, it isnt so fun and you lose
To the people who say that "Jason is OP, survivors have no chance - I say it simply isnt true. You "NEED" VOIP, after that, hope there is at least a couple of survivors with VOIP who will communicate and use teamwork. I find this happens in about 80% of the games I played. Jason isnt so OP when you taunt him into entering the shack you're in - straight into a bear trap and some sporty dude with high strength ♥♥♥♥♥ him over the back of the head with a baseball bat - knocking him out.
I had some amazing moments - planning in a hut with two german guys with athletic characters who went to give Jason the run around whilst my chick (with high intelligence) quickly repaired the car with the parts we stashed so we could all make the escape. (Amazingly funny moments as you don't have time to let the fat guy inside the car and all drive off together as he screams in despair!)
This really is a team game, and learning the survivors strengths and weaknesses. Alot of the negativity comes from people with low game time not understanding they need to communicate and use the synergy of the characters. When this is learnt and pulled off correctly - Jason doesnt have such an easy time.
All in all - survivor is fun, but team-work is needed (and not always possible depending on your team mates). Jason is fun full stop, staring at your prey through the window and watching them panic is just so, so good! They need to fix the controls and a few other small bugs, which I'm pretty sure they will.
Is it worth $40? Not compared to some other games, which will give you alot more content for half the price - but this is also the best (by far) in the genre (as far as I know). If you like the genre and can afford the $40, then it is worth it.
Believe me - 6 councillors with their own strengths and weaknesses working together as one can lead to Jason battered on the floor, mask knocked off and you and your buddies cruising away in a car cheering together.
Yes, it is hard to escape...but it's Jason! It's meant to be hard - and when you do pull off the escape with a well made plan, it is far more satisfying than having jumped over pallettes for 5 minutes before BMing at the one escape route.
8/10. Any negative review based on "Jason OP, impossible LOL" either probably dont use the VOIP themselves or have low play time and were unlucky to get placed in matches with others who didnt. This really is a special game once you start to co-operate. :)
