I have played the game substantially more and really wish that I could change this review to recommend, because I think the game developer's intent is in the right place, just executed horridly. It really gets a “meh” more than a no. This is why: (all of the bullets tie into each other at the end)
SKILL SYSTEM:  Skill system is built around you not playing as a lone wolf. While it is possible, the skill tree does not exactly allow you to accomplish this task without an unreal amount of game time and multiple characters. 2 or 3 would be needed in order to craft all of the different items. Not saying this is a bad thing, just something the solo gamers need to be aware of.
MAP SIZE:  Sadly, the map "appears" to be larger than it really is. I have walked the island several times now, just to take in all of the different terrain features and how everything is laid out. The map suddenly gets smaller once you do this. Truly.
UI ISSUES/LEARNING CURVE/EMPTINESS:  Steep learning curve due to a fairly poorly implemented UI and overall game mechanics, in my opinion. I joined a good group of people and really got taught the ropes and while I started to understand the game a great deal more and was more successful. The emptiness and game quality around me persisted. The animals run like Ultima Online servers during live world events over 20 years ago. Not kidding you.
BORING WORLD:  Wolves, boars, bears, deer, moose, and every other creature in the land is stiff. Everything is like a still portrait of animals who do not move unless you step on their tail. Even when being shot 20 times with arrows, "peaceful" animals walk 5 feet and stand still. Why do I need to shoot a boar 20 times to kill it? Heck if I know... tough boars in this game, I tell you what. Took 15 arrows to the face and nothing. Every animal of this game is offspring of Chuck Norris.
NOT SO MUCH LIKE LIFE:  Master Hunter? Don't worry, you still can’t tell the difference between a hare, deer, moose, or sow. Maybe my character’s intelligence was too low to tell the difference. LOL. Stupid mechanics.
SERVER POPULATION DISPARITY. Server sizing is one issue that really gets me annoyed. None of the servers are DEV run. The servers that are up, either have 0-20 players or are full during most peak and sometimes off peaks times. 64 players is simply too small to make this game enjoyable, especially if your friends are on a popular server. Which means you need to make the map bigger…which leads me to my next point.
SHANTY ISLAND OR NO MAN’S LAND:  The servers have a tendency to be filled with players every hundred meters or so sporting a shanty hut, or you are left to rot on an island by yourself.
FAIL ADMINS: You are at the mercy of the server admins. Some server admins think it is ok to kick you, so their buddies can get in. Or if you didn’t upper case your character’s name. Didn’t happen to me but one of the people in my group. I am looking at you RPCLiF… fail. What is to stop them from kicking you when you beat them in a fair fight? Nothing really.
TIME SINK:  Total and complete time sink to an unacceptable level. While I do love to play games that allow you to mold your character and really build a city from the ground up, I don't want to do this in game with real time. If the skill increase is default, quit your job or fall behind. You will get your butt kicked by the unemployed and retired.
BOTTOM LINE:  The game is really fun if you have a lot of time on your hands with a good number of friends. Join a lower population server or better yet, create a private one and try to have some fun with it. Joining the wrong public server could leave you and your friends with nothing to show for a great deal of hours’ worth of work. Middle of the road to a little bit below. Avoid buying it unless it is on sale… like 80% off or more.

I am going to get this out of the way first, so please stick with me for this first part (and hopefully you'll understand why I gave this a recommendation afterwards). I am by no means going to sugar coat how broken and unfufilling this game was as a whole.
If you want a game with ANY form of depth or complexity, look somewhere else and stay far away from this game.
Instead of a well-thought, linear gameplay story the first game (2013) implimented so well, I can only describe this new system as trying to replicate an MMO in the worst way it could, and ultimately feels extremely rushed.
Quests are given, loot is collected on completion (pretty damn good loot sometimes), and the different crystals that are used to upgrade weapons that are all based on percentages. There is a hub world with shops that do little other than sell percentages, and Levels are just small maps that are entered an explored multiple times for completely different missions, making it feel very repetative. None of this is bad per-say, however  it is very poorly implemented.
What is more, the story is abysmal. Huge leaps in logic were made, and whole parts of the game make no sense. X person   promises to help you. X person sends you on quests (like 6~ish). X person sends you on quest that goes wrong. X person reveals that they wanted you to die, and now X person expects you to die, despite X person's gracious attitude torwards you with absolutely no motivation. Just that X person felt like it, as far as the player can tell, and the game expects the player to just understand what the ♥♥♥♥ just happened. You are eventually able to guess why X person did it, but not until far in the future. And the ending, OH that ending. If you timed how long it took to fight the final boss, then played that time the moment you beat the boss as a countdown, the ending closes before you would get the the halfway mark, and made even less sense. No one addresses this, which is a HUGE aspect of the game that I would argue makes less sense than that scene in the 1978 Superman movie where superman rewinds time by flying so fast the earth changes rotation. I still cant find someone that actually explains what the hell actually happened, because no one knows.
Now for anyone that is still listening to my rant, which I applaud/thank you, one question remains, why do I recommend this game? Combat. Shadow Warrior 2 improves on the combat in so many aspects, that I would argue it sorta kinda barely makes up for all the previous problems. With such a large variety of unique and fun weapons, as well as adressing some problems from the original, primarily being the doubletapping of WASD in order to activate a skill. The right click strong melee is removed in favor of dedicating it to a sword's special abilities, with chi abilities having their own dedicated buttons. All of this, with the various unique guns make the game amazing and fun, and almost make up for all the other problems. If you want a game purely based on it's ability to replicate the brutal killings of demons with a katana or chainsaw, I recommend it, whole heartedly, 9.5/10. However if you want ANYTHING more from this game, from gameplay complexity to a story that makes even the slightest bit of damn sense , I would highly recommend that you double, triple, and quadruple check that you actually want it, and that none of these problems will effect you. Ultimately I recommend it because of that combat, and how fun it was to use, however that recommendation is given through gritted teeth, as I cannot help but remember the many pains that it has given me. I will never forget this game, yes because of the combat, but mostly because of how highly disappointing it was in all other aspects. 9.5/10 combat with 3/10 everything else.

We spent 2 hard, long years developing Rush Bros. and our biggest weakness right now is word-of-mouth. We're trying to do everything we can to make Rush Bros. known. It's a hard-core racing game which can be enjoyed by both casual players and dedicated speed-runners. The philosophy behind the game is: Play the way you want to. When you're on a playground you don't normally declare the rules before everyone jumps in a sandbox. By the time you get there somebody is probably already making sande castles. Then somebody screams "The Floor is Lava" and things get really interesting. Rush Bros. is themed around this kind of play- this more organic make-up-the-rules-as-you-go-along kind of play. This is a hard concept for some people to understand because it's something more natural / organic and less structured. If anything else Rush Bros. is an experiment with how you can allow your players to design the rules for how the game is played while they are playing it. You choose what levels to play on, you choose the win condition (Cross Finish Line Together Vs. There's One Obvious Winner - Or some other condition based on applied Remixes / Mutators ). Going to start by saying I am a super picky shopper. It takes a bit to reel me into the purchase but I took the bait on this one..... and oh man. I am so glad I did. This game is probably the most fun I've had in a FPS format. It plays like Borderlands and Ninja Gaiden got in bed and a had an awesome baby named "Shadow Warrior 2."
The graphics are nice and vivid, it paints a great atmosphere and I've had only a few moments where I felt things looked a little wonky. It also lends to a Metal Gear Rising cut as you will style. Not as free form but pretty cool when it comes to enemies being carved up. You will be playing in first person and the it can be disorienting trying to fluidly melee at first, but it's not hard.
The gameplay is fueled with action and loot, the combat offering many different options. The weapons are fairly unique and even those of similar classes have their unique differences. The melee combat is beyond fun and satisfies so much it's hard to not spoil the fun toys you will have at your disposal. The ranged weapons can be as exotic as your melee weapons and at times I find my self going back and forth a lot in fights. If that wasn't enough they are all highly customizable with a tiered crafting system that lets you empower them.
The maps are pretty large but not open world large. With it being a game that operates by sending you to large zones to complete objectives or free-roam. I've yet to have a moment where I felt bored and said "Oh great, this place again" even the times I've revisted areas the enemies, paths and objectives offered enough of a twist to make it feel fresh.
I have not personally tested the multiplayer in this game but I have high hopes for it as I've yet to be let down by this game. I'll submit an edit when I get around to it.
If I had to throw a numbered score at this game, I'd have no problem placing it in the 8.5-9.0 range.

Originally played the demo for this on Xbox 360 and thought that while the X-Ray bullet kill cam was a cool gimmick, it would get old fast.
I was wrong.
Picked this up for free on Steam during a 24-hour special sale period and I have been plugging along at it bit by bit.  It's fun in its own way - you have to scope out each mission, make some quick decisions as to how you're going to approach it, and (after dying a few times) perfect it so you can last as long as possible without being detected.  I'm not sure it's possible to go through an entire mission without being spotted by the enemy, but that's fine with me - stealth games haven't always been my favorite, anyway.
Only a couple of downsides:
1. The various traps and things you can set to protect yourself I find to be usually worthless to me personally, as I tend to move around a lot.  I'm not sure if that's just my style or if it's because I don't find myself in situations often where I have been able to anticipate hordes of enemies coming at me while having to snipe others in the distance.
2. When zoomed in, my framerate drops to about half of what it is in normal view.  I don't have the best computer in the world by any stretch of the imagination, but it does get annoying nonetheless (makes it very hard to line up shots quickly).
That having been said, the death cams are awesome, and I'm just having fun in general working my way through the various missions and locales.  In the end, that's all that matters to me, anyway.

Pros:

-Sometimes the frames drop, probably due to point 2 in Pro category and usually on a transition load where the game reloads all the assets and lighting.

Overall:
I'd give this game a 9/10. The only short comings were, as stated in the cons, the 'monsters'. The developers made it so multiple monsters reacted differently and had different ways to 'play around them', however they must have lost some of that mojo later into the game since I just had to bellow out a manly scream and charge right past the monsters instead of baiting them or what not (which may have forced me to skip some documents or other neat non-essential story stuff).
Other than that complaint though I absolutely love this game. The story was so enthralling from the get-go that I completed this game in just two huge sittings; I just didn't want to turn it off!
Make sure to play this game in the dark too, with a headset for complete immersion. After a while even the eerie silence and just the sound of your own footsteps got unnerving while you're waiting for whatever comes next. A definite "Worth" in my book.

This game feels a lot like someone played Bloodbowl, failed at the dice system, and went Free-to-play model, but with a price to get in.
The game is played so that your health pool is also the amount of attacks you get and alike to Blood Bowl you have to dice-off against your opponent and whoever get's most Hits wins by that much damage. This to me is a really aweful way to do it, because the levels of tactical gymnastics you have to do to use everything to your advantage with poor cards (Even Legendaries has to be levelled, which takes FOREVER) and everyone is just better at it than you.
This game has the feel of a Free-to-play but there are no store in it to buy things with real life money and the reason it feels like a free-to-play game is because it's all farming, farming is all you will ever do. You get money from every third win and a randomized quest. When you get enough you can buy a card/unit pack containing 3 TOTALY RANDOM things. These things can in turn be scrapped if you don't like them, levelled up for more scraps when you discard them, or just used if you got nothing better. The problem is that from a Common unit you can get max 10 scraps, and a Legendary unit costs about 600+ to make.
Why do I only focus on Legendary? Because a Legendary can reach 6 levels, a Common unit can only reach 3, and every level beyond those 3 are more than enough to not only push a unit but win the fight. What's worse is that a Legendary unit costs the same to field as a Common unit, so you would never actually keep anything less than legendary (Unless it's one of the few OP units in the game) once it hits full level.
Most of the lessons in the game is not taught, not in the tutorial (Which is hidden past the first part) and in the game tips book, or maybe it is due to the broken english and I missed it, but things like being surrounded and having enemies on either side of you will remove your already very small pool of dice you can roll in a game where you win by drowning the enemy in dice, which really can screw you over. You can use a suicide rusher against an angry farmer, throw out 5 attacks against the farmers 2, and the farmer can still bash your guys head in. At some point strategy just doesn't matter, because of the RNG.
The game comes down to luck and knowing the maps and to always have a counter to everything. What is the list of things you need to counter? Too long to cover properly.
This game is all about grinding so you can grind something else down the line.

So, what is "GoD Factory: Wingmen"? well, it's a very unique throw on the MOBA genre. In this game you get to play as a completely customized ship built to your liking, in a purely skill based action game. You don't have to worry about people outleveling you, as there are no levels in this game. Items are ship parts that do different attacks, for example, one cannon could be a lock on type, and another could be a skillshot that deals three times more damage than the one previously mentioned. This allows you to play any which way you like, instead of having to find one hero or champion out of many. you never feel like losing was someone else's fault, and that's a nice jump from the toxic blaming of normal MOBAS, and for a guy with over 1k hours in DotA 2, I can say for a fact that this game has an amazing community compared to the average MOBA. The "ancient" or "base" is very unique, as there are multiple parts on the enemy base that when destroyed, give you a bonus and the enemy a handicap they have to play the rest of the game with. This game is very refreshing, and the only reason i have not played much of this game is well, the problem with this game is how small the community is.
the problem with this game is that the community is a little bit to small, and it can be hard to find a match. this is probably because as a skill based game, the people that stick with the game will obliterate you untill you have about 3-4 hours of practice, and even then you can barely keep up with them. i pre-purchased this game, and i stopped playing it because of how small the community is, and i would not say that it is worth a 20 dollar price point. but when this game goes on sale, pick it up. it is worth your time.
So, here's a quick summary for you if you were to lazy to read that.
POSITIVE:
-Very good graphics for a MOBA
-Unique, and refreshing
-Great community, Dedicated for the most part
-You can unlock everything in the game, and tweak your ship to your own playstyle
-The Devs are very dedicated to this game
CONS
-the only con in this game is how small the community really is.
Would i get this for 20? no. but when it comes on sale, pick it up. you will love this game if you are into thrilling, fast paced games and MOBAS. And if not, this game still probably has something for you.

I have to say i was on the fence briefly myself as whether or not to get this game, but in the end, the primary complaint in the negative reviews seems to be about RNG.  I mean, it doesn't seem valid to me to complain about a bad roll in a DICE game.  Sometimes you'll roll awesome, sometimes you won't, and sometimes you can go on streaks of either-- the R in RNG stands for random my friends.  As I said though this IS a tactics game, so while the dice can still screw you, you can mitigate this quite a bit with, you know... tactics.  Tactics here involve positioning (some units get an automatic bonus versus surrounded units & other units can use spears to reach over an intervening unit for example) and timing (knowing when to play a card that prevents and enemy from moving for example).
I've paid more than double what this game is asking  for tactics games that aren't nearly as good.

More detailed description but careful *some small spoilers*:
I have played the original Duke Nukem 3D back in the '90s on DOS, then the Duke Nukem Megaton Edition that got released on steam in 2011 (I think), played Duke Nukem Zero Hour on the N64 and the two games on the PSX (Time to Kill, Land of Babes) and I must say that Duke Nukem Forever is the worst Duke Nukem game and one of the worst FPS I have ever played.
The Duke Nukem Universe
----------------------------
When it comes to the levels you visit kind of the same places you also visited in Duke Nukem 3D. Duke Burger, Hive, a Space Station and the game is kind of lacking a mindblowing scenario that lets you make "wow" that is kind of nice.
Everything looks boring and somehow uninspiring. You are following a total linear path through the levels and are
not able to vary the way you finish them.
Remember the annoying remote driving parts in the original "Shadow Warrior"? Where there was a key on a car or a boot
and you had to remote controll it, so you get the key. Well, yeah. They put this in.
Duke has no health.
He has an ego meter that you can upgrade by playing pinball or looking at magazines or working out.
When you get hit twice the meter starts to blink and as long as you don't get hit again, it recharges like a shield.
So no health packs. No health items.
I've played on the highest difficulty level and even with this the game is way too easy.
There are a lot of squences where you have to use a gattling gun and shoot ships. You can't just walk away from that thing.
No. You got to use this weapon so the story goes on.
And.... even more.
Driving sequences. Yes, driving in a car and killing enemies. Jumping above cliffs.
Sequences, where you get shrunk and you got to jump through the level to procede. Wow, just a 3D Jump and Run.
The enemies are boring as well. There are not so many enemies types and definitely no new ones. They not even included the acid alien from the fourth episode of the original Duke Nukem.
The whole game "feels" like a hybrid between Halo and Mass Effect with a little bit of Duke in it.
Weapons
-----------
You can only damage boss enemies with the rocket launcher or the devastator. Not with the other normal weapons.
In the default setting Duke can ONLY CARRY TWO WEAPONS!!!!!
So if you don't know when there is gonna be a boss fight you will always have a rocket launcher with you.
In the option menu you can change the amount of weapons to four at a time.
But still: Why not let him carry all the weapons like in the original Duke Nukem 3D.
There are no new weapons in the game. They just took all the original ones. In the DLC "Doctor who cloned me" you get
a weapon like a small acid grenade launcher, but that's it. No new stuff really.
When you shoot at enemies you also get the feeling that they don't care. The weapons don't have a specific strength on certain enemies. You will find yourself using the shotgun a lot.
Items
-------
Steroids just make you punch like the "Doom-Guy". But you can not shoot at that time. Awesome, while all
the other enemies have projectile weapons.
In the option menu there is a shortcut for the Jetpack. But YOU CAN'T FIND THE JETPACK in the SINGLE PLAYER CAMPAIGN!!
So why even implement it? There is also no scuba gear.
Disturbing moment (*spolier*)
--------------------------------
There is one very disturbing moment in the game. Your girlfriends get kidknapped and you find them in the Hive, while they are literally being♥♥♥♥♥♥♥by the alien hive itself. Then they burst open and little alien creatures appear.
So. First you played through levels that were derpy shmerpy, happy here, shot there and a joke.
And from one moment to another... this stuff.
This is completely inappropriate. I mean even in the alien games (AVP, Alien Colonial Marines) aliens burst out of hosts, but not like that. The developers really went the wrong path here.
Multiplayer
------------
Apparently there is a multiplayer, but nobody seems to play this, so you will find yourself in an empty level.
DLC - Doctor who cloned me (*Spoilers*)
-------------------------------------------
The beginning is kind of nice but then the story will very quickly start to disappoint again.
The last fight is on the moon against the Alien Queen.
It is one of the most annoying boss battles ever. You are really gonna be happy when you finish this boss.
Summary
-----------
Well, DON'T BUY THIS GAME! Let's hope that there is never again gonna be a new Duke Nukem game.
This concept worked in the '90s, but not today anymore.

The animations and graphics are great and the gameplay is very diverse with the available figures. In addition building up your warband and adjusting it to what you have available after earning some booster packs feels great and is a lot of fun.

The game as it stands shows signs of incompletenes, there are just so many many things that are broken:
* NPCs have no interaction and lack expressiveness
* Load times are relatively long, no optimization whatsoever
* You can only use two guns at a time, which is awkward ...
* Any use of vehicles is interesting but lacks any dept, and the physics is a little off
It just has absolutely no polish; it's an excellent alpha that never fully matured. It really doesn't need that much to be a masterpiece, just open development tools and in the span of 3 years it would have lived up to the hype on fan love alone.
But that is the real issue. This was in a way a dead end for the hero I, and perhaps others, waited 12 years to make a return (I bought Duke 3D when it came out). If only it had been given a chance, we would have Borderlands as well as Duke franchises to follow.
So in sum, I love it, I really like Duke Forever. Yes it has childish pimple ladden humor, and never really tries to connect in a deep level (that's for♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It's fun, that's all it is, and that is all it ever needed to be (it's a game for uhm playing in your spare time not a second career or something) The game has a lot of variety, the music is great, graphics are interesting and expressive (yes I'm sure you can find something that could melt your PC this isn't it), puzzles are fun, it has relentless action and if you think highly of Frank Zappa humor (which is all it is) Duke really shouldn't be that offensive to you (just don't expect him to grow up at all, he's trapped forever in the 90's which is ok).
And who knows, if the powers that be ever release modding tools (or simply allow people to actually make them), this could the shiny diamond it was conceived as, and live up to its hype... And just maybe ... catch the interest of a broader fanbase and lead to a sequel, and hence more Duke awesomeness :D
For now take this as it is, something that's incomplete, partially broken, but with glimpses of genius. And rather than think about it, have fun !

I bought this game expecting something terrible, considering it's less than stellar reviews on release. I just bought this game in December of 2016 and I must say that I was pleasantly surprised.
The graphics are like an early PS3/Xbox 360 game. By today's standards, it's pathetic. Ugly textures and the like, none of which are particularly important to me.
The animations are sickening and downright laughable, they are unnatural and when characters speak to you, they are hardly ever focused on you. The voice acting is weak and the sound effects are just as bad. Just generic repeated sounds for almost everything you can think of, including the water, cars, explosion and some of the critters you'll see about.
The game has one major thing going for it, and that is gameplay. The action sections of the game are insanely entertaining. The shooting feels natural and visceral. It's quick and fluid, there are plenty of reasons I enjoyed the action parts of the game, which basically makle the entire game, because... well... the rest of the game is awful. Pathetically designed platforming sections that make you want to tear your hair out, driving sections that control like an early driving sim. I had more toruble in the driving and platforming parts of the game than most of the action bits. But don't take that as the game being easy, because it couldn't be farther from the truth. This game is relentless in it's enemies difficulty. The enemies will not stop until you are dead, naturally. The excellent gunplay helps keep you on your toes and getting the last satisfying hit on your enemies before they turn you into a Duke Burger.
Besides the drawn out driving sections, the annoying puzzles and overall visual and audio downfalls of the game, it is still genuine fun and I am really glad I went through with it. I bought it during the sale and can say that it was at least $5 worth of fun. There are plenty of little hidden secrets in the game and even a virtual pinball machine.
If you are looking for a fun shooter, you can't go wrong with Duke Nukem Forever if the price is right.

So what should I write about this game. I know it is still in Early Access but it doesn't look like it will change much more until the final release. After all it appears pretty much finished so far.
First of all, this game is fun. Actually I like the game style. It is reminds pretty much on playing Civ.
The problem is, where Civ offers a very wide variety of gameplay elements (from war, over diplomacy, economy, religion etc.) this game only took the economic part of if.
This unfortunately offers very little replay value. You basically start every game somewhere on the map, building all type of "farms" for resources and hope for the best.
My biggest problem however is that the interaction with the other companies (e.g. players) is very limited and comes only to light when they are buying a spot of good resources you were looking after.
So then, you end up in a skirmish of selling recources when you can in order to make money and buy the other company shares in order to win.
This looks every game more or less the same because all the elements that made Civ so great are missing.
The only interaction are a few "illegal" actions like sabotage you might do. But even this has limited effect (e.g. the opponent's mines are blocked for a minute).
The game offers no diplomacy (not even on an economic way like making a syndicate, negotiation or trading agreements like I offer you electricity in order to get better offers for your steel producion) or corporate espionage (like stealing other players inventions). After all the game goes very quick (a game might take 30 - 90 minutes. So there is no grand strategy like investing in late-game infrastructure / units etc. Just a bit of research can be done which basically leads to improved production (e.g. instead of 10 electricity, the power plant offers 15).
This leads after all to the strategy of building your own variety of buildings in order to be best prepared for changing prices (if you sell stuff, the price drops) so you might sell what ever looks best at the moment.
To come to a conclusion, this game looks promising. I really like the style, it is easy to start with - no real need for many tutorials but even if you need some, it is done quickly. Still it lacks of gameplay.
So for the time being, I can only reccomend the game for fans of economic realtime strategy gamers (even though there are no units to control).
For people who are looking for another Civ-like game with grand strategy, long term multiplayer sessions with different victory conditions, this game is unfortunately not what you are looking for.

I'm recommending this game.  I do so with a bit of reluctance.  I purchased it on sale, and for the price I paid, I think I got a good deal.  I personally believe every game is priced at what people are willing to pay, and those who whine about "not a top tier game" or "the devs should lower the price" are idiots.  Still, I think it is fair to say a game should be recommended if it gives value for the buck, and at the price I paid it did.  At the nominal price, I would be so happy.
Pros:
* It takes a bit to learn, and the tutorials are not that great at teaching.  But I could figure it out at the easiest setting, and then I read a user guide to understand the underlying strategy.  With just 8 hours of play, I can handle a moderate level of difficulty and have a decent challenge while using nearly all the available game strategies.
* A single round can be played in 20 minutes.
* The pace is interesting.  It is kinda of slow at fast, and then at some point you'll get the clear upper hand (or not) and the end game comes fast.
* The pace means you can think about strategy, which is what I wanted from the game, but then you don't need to wait long to learn if you made the right decisions.
* The graphics are decent.
* The game has a good amount of complexity.
Cons:
* For such a complex strategy game, the pace is almost too fast.
* Some aspects seem important, but I have yet to find them critical.  Without providing spoilers, I'll just say the transport of goods, the offworld market, and the patent system don't seem balanced correctly.
* It is a work in progress, this is both good and bad, but for the price,  think it needs more progress.  I don't think it is as close as the devs suggest, but if they clean up the degenerate strategies, then this will become a pro.
* The stock concept is a bit too simplified, and other than its role in the endgame, it is rather pointless.  This could be resolved if the parameters for the price were explained thus opening up strategies to manipulate shares.  One guide gives some suggestions of strategies, but if that's all it is, then stock system is a con.
* What's the point of the town?  Is it only for the pleasure dome?  Because I can make nearly as much money putting the pleasure dome near my own base.  Is the town what is buying the goods?  If so, why only have transports to go to my base?   I have rockets to get goods to market off planet; what gets goods to the city?
* I guess I'll have to look up how to start an auction.  At first I found them annoying, because they literally pause the game while you play them out.  I would jsut skp them, to get back to game play.  Then I learned some auctions should be won at almost any price.  And then I wanted to know how to make them start.  But this is a con because the few patent options should never be part of the auction.  I think it ruins the patent model, and it doesn't make sense.
If you like strategy business games, then this is enjoyable.  For the price, you'll have more fun with civilization or colonization, but if you already played those and many other similar games; then buy this.  It is definitely different from those games and is fun.
Tip:  While I find little value in the sabotage features of the black market, look over at carefully.  Some black market items are not sabotage items, and they provide key advantages in the game.

It is a unique and fun game and in most scenarios I would readily recommend it.
The problem is that a decision was made at some point by someone who possibly had some economic motivation to save money and the result is a game released today with the most unreliable and cheapest option for multiplayer hosting; peer-to-peer.
Even with a decent internet connection you will get frequent connection issues (pointless joining errors because the game is full, the game ending when a host or somtimes random player leaves) as well as occasional to frequent lag.
P2P introduces all kinds of issues because it relies on everyone ideally connecting to play to be within reasonable distance of each other and with a good connection.
Apart from the negative affect this has, the people that P2P hurts the most is those with slowed internet speeds and those relatively distant from the actual DNS servers so really I think this game deserves a negative review just because the majority of people who will end up buying this game probably won't be able to enjoy it as they should and that just ain't right.
If Ubisoft spent the money that they should on game servers then the amount of connection issues and errors would probably be reduced by something like 90%.
There is absolutely no reason for a company worth two billion dollars to still be using a outdated networking technology that originates from the era of expensive dial-up. The only people they are saving money is themselves.
*If the game has been built around P2P exclusively it is the ultimate♥♥♥♥♥♥take.

Let's break this down:
Beginning Content:
After a quick click through tutorial for those who already know the game, you get to make your choice of colors. Then you can take it a step forward and pick a secondary color for the deck. In my specific instance, I chose black with green as a secondary. That didn't last long either. And even after, you have nothing except the update content, which is next on the review.
Update Content:
Underwhelming, plain and simple. It seemed pretty obvious they were saying one thing when developing this. The black and red cards were practically screaming. Single Player:

Multiplayer:
Nothing you haven't seen playing the physical game on a table. 3 games and I saw the exact same deck by 3 different players. Uhh. Standard Play? Seriously. The same "Tier 1" decks that you have no fighting against unless you pop the wallet out to give yourself a fighting chance.
Actual Gameplay and Other Features:

As a person who previously only played the SE: Nazi Zombie Army games, I decided to check this game out and give it a try, the game feels the same except obviously in a different enviornment and you fight... well not zombies.
The game can be played in full stealth or just killing everyone, on higher difficulties you really have to have a decent amount of situational awareness.. by that I mean the enemies are pretty accurate and you can only take 2 shots before you die and checkpoints are very questionable on various missions.
If you are a beginner, or just like playing for the story, there is a custom difficulty setting where you can pretty much alter whatever you like, which is a fantastic idea imo.
The devs said the game takes around 40 hrs to complete. That is false, it may take 40 if you are playing on the hardest difficulty and trying to 100% the game with all collectables etc. but overall the story should take between 4-10hrs depending on if you just want to do play the missions without collectables or if you are playing stealthily or not.
Overall, if you've started with SE: NZA, its pretty much the same experience, that does NOT mean its a bad one, I really enjoyed SE: v2.

I like the idea of this game, I think the design is great and the gameplay is well thought out, but as much as I want to like the game as a whole, the mechanics simply make this game no fun to play at all.
I have just spent well over an hour, trying to win a battle with 4 units against 10, where entire turns were spent not winning a single dice roll despite 3 of my units being stronger than 8 out of the enemy's 10 (meaning you get more dice to roll than the opponent), several times won dice rolls were ignored by the AI with them not taking any damage, despite hits being scored (dice result being shown, hit animation and sound being played), and enemy attacks being blocked not resulting in counterattacks by my units, despite attacks from the same enemy units blocked by my same units in previous turns having resulted in counterattacks.
This kind of skewed playing out of the SP scenario simply destroys the fun that a game is supposed to be. Being a challange is one thing, this is frustrating, if nothing else.
I don't know whether the issues I have encountered are caused by bugs, or by the fact that the game is Early Access (still in development), or whether the game simply doesn't make the mechanics obvious enough to understand why certain things are happening in the way they are, but with the game being the way I am experiencing it right now, I would strongly recommend not purchasing the game right now. Wait until the Early Access period is over and the game has actually finished development, then wait a little longer to have some reviews coming in of the retail version, and hope for those issues being fixed. Otherwise, you'd be better off investing your money in other games.

Shortly:
Sequel for the previous Shadow Warrior game from the year 2013. While the perviou SW game had linear story to follow, this time in SW2 the game is more open-world..ish. It's not really open-world game, but there are a lot of side missions that you can do along with the main one.
From todays standards, the game doesn't look all that good, but it's decent. Though I have to say that the game was a bit too colorful for mey sensitive eyes. My eyes literally started to hurt if I played it more than 20 minutes at a time.
As for the sound world, it wasn't bad but not that good either.
As for the gameplay itself, unlike in the SW1 where you had no character progression or inventory system, this game has both of them. You can find new weapons from the world or aquire them from the side missions. You can also find relics, if I remember their name corrently, from the fallen enemies, which you can then use and attach them to your gear to boost certain skills or abilities, all depending on your playstyle.
As I mentioned earlier, the game has side missions. These missions provide you with money, skill points, skills and/or weapons. You can use money to buy stuff from the shop keepers in the game.  Skill points are used to upgrade your skills (duh), each giving you more health, more damage, more skill damage etc. etc.
As for the story, I can't tell much about it at all as I refunded the game after 2.5 hours of playing. The reason for that is that I was kinda shocked how different the game actually was from its predecessors. The more I played, the more I realised how different it is, I just couldn't bring myself to play any longer than I did.  =(
Overall, I wasn't as impressed with the game as I was with its predecessor back from the year 2013. My biggest issue with the game was probably the fact that it wasn't as linear as the previous game was, but instead it was more open-worldish. After each mission you would return to your home base, where you could then pick new missions and teleport to next area and kill some more demons. I wasn't impressed.  =(
Pros:
+ Enemy variety
+ Lo Wang's comments from time to time
+ Combat is fun, but overused sometimes
Cons:
- Feels like b-graded game
- Too open-world-ish,  I would have preferred the game to be more linear like its predecessor was
- A bit too colorful
Do I recommend:
I wish there was middle ground in the Steam's Thumps up or down recommendation, as its really hard to say sometimes. I didn't like this game all that much, but you might think otherwise. But for now, I'm gonna go with thumbs down. Don't buy it if you're expecting the game to be like the SW1 (2013) was.
Verdict: 5 / 10 - Average shooter game with mild RPG elements in it

I am going to come back to this game I think, but so far I've played the first campaign and struggled with it. Sure, I may not be very good at the game but even when I start trying to lay down some decent tactics the thing that always, and I mean ALWAYS, screws me over are the dice. I can never seem to get any dice rolls to go my way. 5 dice against 3 and my guys are still getting chunks of health knocked off them. The fights involving 4 or 5 guys against 2 just mean that my guys get surrounded and end up with even less dice. The only way I've won any of the fights has been pure luck. The cards help, but only by giving you more dice and if you're not rolling the right results, you're just getting slaughtered.
On top of that, I can't say the game is balanced very well. I mean, I'm getting hit by multiple guys that are the same toughness and armour as one of my guys (the other guy is worse and normally dies fairly quickly). I mean, how are you meant to win if not by luck?
One way to do it is to constantly spam 'On Guard', because it gives you an extra dice for defence and there doesn't seem to be any disadvantage from constantly defending. Maybe I'm missing something but giving the defender the same amount of dice as when they're attacking just means that every attack is the same, no matter what side you're on.
Let me put my amateur game designer hat on instead and consider that it might be better to give the defender a dice penalty, so that it's harder to counter everything and 'On Guard' just gives you a better defence, not an advantage over attackers.
The main thing to take away from this review, if you've read this far, is that the game has promise but you're completely at the mercy of random numbers. There's elements of skill and tactics here, but ultimately it falls over because of unreliable damage and poor balance. I'm sure the PvP in an even fight is much more fun, but the campaign so far has just left me feeling a bit deflated.

I had heard it was bad, but it was super cheap on Steam so I felt I could get at least a couple bucks entertainment out of it.  eh...
The only real positive to the game is that once you beat the single player mode, you get access to concept art and videos from the game.  One of the videos were the original E3 trailers of Duke Nukem Forever that was released around 2003, which were awesome trailers then and still looked like it would have been fun as heck even today.  Those bonus videos just made me wish that that was the game us Duke Nukem fans had gotten instead of the game I has just beaten.
There were a couple of neat/amusing moments in the game such as a couple levels where Duke has been shrunk and has to work his way around a kitchen without touching the floor, or having to drive RC cars through a casino, etc.  The shrunken Duke levels got boring pretty quick as the novelty wore off yet Duke keeps getting shrunk.  The 3D updated aliens of Duke Nukem 3D looked pretty cool.
Overall the game wasn't that good though.   Most of the levels were boring, or tedious.  The colors felt washed out and bland for the most part.  I found myself wishing I was playing the Duke Nukem Forever game that we were introduced to in the 2003 - 2005 E3 game trailers.  The color tones used in this release made me not care about how a single level looked.
Several of the levels are tedious or poorly designed.  The most annoying thing was the number of times I died in the game because of technical problems in the game.  There are clipping issues everywhere in the levels..  Say you get jumped by a group of monsters so you start moving around strafing and weaving through cover to avoid damage while trying to do some killing.  Out of the blue, you get snagged onto some object in the level.  You know you hit an object so you try to slide around it, or jump it or something, but no....Duke doesn't move.  You are forced to move the exact oppsite direction you were moving when you hit the object to get off of it. (e.g. You strafe left into an crate, you can't move forward, or backward then continue strafing, you have to strafe back to the right.)   By the time you figure it out you are usually cornered and...dead.  The aliens don't  have large hit boxes, but they have huge collision boxes.  If one gets right up on you, it's hard has heck to get around it because you can't strafe around, or jump.  You have to move directly away, yet you can't easily get enough distance to strafe around before the alien almost kills you, and many times does.
The water levels suck.  Not once did I die to an enemy under water, but I died 20+ times because of all the clipping issues in the levels.  A doorway (because you didn't go precisely through the middle of tghe doorway, or piece of seaweed, or something stopped me cold and I couldn't get around it fast enough.  Duke is so sluggish swimming in water that you can't afford to get stopped since you are trying to get to air pockets to breath.  Duke kept drowning.
Sadly Duke Nukem Forever was barely worth the $2 or $3 dollars I paid for it on Steam.

This game may still be in early access, but it is definitely worth it.
There are already two single player campaigns for those who don't like PVP.
PVP games are quick - a match takes perhaps 15 minutes, often less, so it's perfect for a lunchbreak.
The rules are rather simple, they could really work as physical board game and making a tactical mistake can be quite unforgiving against a clever opponent.
Since all attacks are made with die-rolls lucky/unlucky rolls can make quite a difference. Also, most of the time a bad attack roll may result in a counterattack, damaging the attacker. It is very important to optimize your chances by clever positioning (attacking from opposite sides gives both attackers a bonus for exmaple). Another important factor are special abilities and order cards for attack bonuses or attacks that can't be countered. Using these abilities costs morale points, however, which are limited and only slowly are regained by certain die-rolls.
Your units can be leveled to get more abilities and stats increases.
The graphics are nice, the sound is atmospheric, though a little repetitive.
For 6 Euros, this is game is a real gem and definitely worth buying if you like turn based tactics with a little bit of RPG elements and deck building. It can be a somewhat grindy, though, because the units you can choose from only level in PVP games and not in solo mode.

Follow up to a critically acclaimed RPG by BIOWARE from over a decade back, the original release was severely cut down from the original vision that OBSIDIAN had in mind. Nevertheless the game was strong in its own right and deservedly so.
It picked up and iterated on almost every point that BIOWARE had explored in the original, the most obvious being,
1) DIALOGUE: The game improves on this point the most, sure BIOWARE had put in decent dialogue and writing in the original KoTOR but OBSIDIAN's work is a class apart. There are more dialogue options informed by a range of variables apart from the Speech skill of your character. Your standing and influence with factions / characters can get them to divulge information without having to have a superior Speech / Persuade / Force Persuade roll.
2) CHARACTERS: Having been treated to a basic Light Side, Dark Side struggle in the original KoTOR (with a single exception), the player is treated to a more nuanced fare of characters in the follow up game. Sure there are still the tropes but the depth of character play has certainly been explored better in KoTOR II. Your influence over party characters can not only open more character interaction options but confers certain benefits on them when they align with your world view.
3) COMBAT: Something as simple as adding another set of weapon slots to make it easier to switch between melee and ranged support roles.
A great game, released a decade ago and still a damn fine game especially with the Restoration MOD guys adding a lot of cut content back inside the title, you can find the content here,
.
Would highly recommend every RPG player to check out the title if just to see where the standards of role-playing were once and how far they have fallen, also, the dedication of a community to raise a flawed star to its fullest potential.

For a little over 2 dollars you can buy a candy bar or a soft drink from a store. However for the same price you can buy a pretty sweet game that goes by the name of Ubermosh.
Similar Games:
CS GO 2D and the Hotline Miami series are what I can think of right off the bat.
Gameplay:
The rounds start off with a trickle of foes, you might even wonder where's the action? Well no worries, in around 10 seconds the screen will be filled with a deluge of pixel foes who wish nothing more than to delete your sorry♥♥♥♥♥from the arena.
To combat these hordes of incoming foes you can choose 3 distinct classes, each with their own playstyle. The classes are Kensai, Gunner, and Warlock.
The Kensai is the most durable of the three but is restricted to using the blade only.
The Gunner has no defensive abilities besides dodging bullets, however she gains the ability to go full auto with her guns, like the saying goes, the best defense is a great offense.
The Warlock gives you the best gun right off the bat and lets you swing your sword, sounds pretty OP right? It is, to a certain extent, but you only have 2 health (Although you can deflect bullets leading to a debate if the Warlock actually is less durable than the Gunner.)
If you don't want to be restricted by class, running without a class is a good way to get into the flow for Ubermosh.
Pros:
Cheap
Faced paced action
Sense of satisfaction when you do well
Cons:
Spawns are wonky sometimes
Can get repetitive with only one map
Gets frustrating if you force yourself too much
Would I recommend this game? Hell yes, for the low price of 2.19 it's definately worth it, although you may wish to buy Ubermosh Black instead for a similar price if you are willing to devote 1 more dollar to this kind of game :).

SOMA very quickly became one of my favorite games I've ever played (Wizardry 1, Skyrim, Talos Principle). It's not every day that a game makes you think like this. If you transfer your mind to a simulation, would you still be you? If you started a task that you would never be able to see completed, would you still do it? Are human minds simply computers whose state is instantiated by a memory and a sophisticated algorithm? Is all of existence simply a simulation in some vast computer?
Pros:
Wonderfully atmospheric graphics. The underwater scenes trecking between stations was my favorite part. The lighting and sense of isolation was fantastic. It felt like a combination of the movies Aliens and the Abyss.
The final scene at Phi. Just wow.
The imagination of the story, and the characters.
Cons:
I honestly felt this game could've done without the monsters. The story and the graphics would've held up the game just fine without the (sometimes) frustration that they introduced. Why does this game need to have any horror elements at all?
On a scale of 1 to 10, where it's actually possible to score a 1-5 (ahem, IGN), I would easily give this a 10.

There are only a few things that can be said for Ubermosh; almost none of them are negative. It's a simple game, really. You're thrown into an arena, tasked with killing as many enemies as you can, while simultaneously trying to last for the duration of the event. There are several guns, and a blade which allows you to cut enemy bullets, winging them back at the shooters. I can't level any worthwhile complaints at the mechanics of the game. If this was all that Ubermosh offered, it would be a solid - albeit, lackluster - game. However, I haven't touched on its best parts, yet.
At its core, Ubermosh is a frenzied bullet-hell shooter. It's arcade-y in all of the best ways - simple, clean, and addictive. But, this isn't what makes Ubermosh so much fun. No, it's the chaotic, electric-neon adrenaline rush the game manages to create.
The soundtrack for Ubermosh fits the gameplay and visual style completely. The gritty, pounding electronic vibes blend perfectly to the frenzied tempo of pulsing laser weapons and slashing projectiles. Visually, Ubermosh conjures something akin to the neon-drenched arcades of Gibson's Sprawl Trilogy; it's a mix of static and pixelated splashes of vibrant color.
Ubermosh is a simple game, yes. Simple enough that some might consider it a negative. However, it's a steal at $2 - well worth the price of admission.
Ultimately, Ubermosh is an addictive, pulse-pounding pixelated frenzy of a game; it's a game with the look and sound of a cyberpunk dream, which delivers frantic combat. And, I can't help but recommend it.

This is a very nice RTS. The only RTS I'm playing now (so I finally abandon AoE and Rise of Nation). So i think the idea worth the price (I've bought it on sale, though). The realisation as well is expensive (good AI, stable code). So I was surprised to see just "mostly positive" as a summary of user reviews. I really want this game to be fully published.
Point by point:
1. No blood. You do not have to rise and command an army. Still, you are able to be offensive and there are plenty of things you do have to command.
2. True fast-paced RTS - you can limit your gaming time to one round - to 30-50 minutes. You do not have to do low-level micromanagment, you have to be fast as well as smart. However, there are meditating moments as well.
3. Very original. I had to spend an hour just to learn what are the rules. And these are very interesting rules. There are simularities with Civilization (and Catan as well). Still, this is something new for me. Basically, you have to buy opponents' companies. There are different strategic decisions you have to do - which type of base to build, whether to invest or not into intellectual property (patents), wich materials you have to mine, which you are able to buy in the market, which type of energy to choose, do you want to use lending or not. There is a lot of tactics here as well. So.. The rules are balanced and there is a lot to master here. However, they still tune the balance so you might find one day that the game had changed and you have to adopt.
4. The rules are tunebale. So you can turn off some of the things people are complaining about in other comments and make the game more balanced and make the "rush" stratagy more hard to implement.
5. The AI is strong. So offline is challenging as well. Looks like there is online option - never tried that.
6. Nice GUI, music and animations. No crashes - high level of coding for early access.
So if you enjoy economic part in RTS games or if you enjoy both RTS and Civilization-like games, you defenitely should try this one. This is a new kind of experience.

WATCH \"LETS PLAY\" VIDEOS TO GET STARTED WITH THIS GAME!
Okay, I first played LiF:YO back in 2015, when it was in EA. At the time, I had serious trouble figuring out the interface, how to build anything more than a campfire, let alone how to find food. I refrained from writing a bad review, because it was still in heavy development, and I really wanted to see where the game would go.
Over a year later, with the help of some \"let’s play\" starter videos, I got back into LiF. I gotta say, they have come very far in a year! While the interface was still tricky to get accustomed to, I quickly got over it and began to build my first items and structures. While grinding away on an official server is very tedious, starting a local game with max advancement settings can really help a novice player get into the game.
With all the improvements, I can really make a serious recommendation for this game. It has a lot to offer, especially if you have some friends that you can play with. With a private server geared towards PVE, you have a good chance to get started towards joining a public server for some good, long-term PVP or clan vs clan action. (plus, the high potential for some Monty Python jokes)
There are still some cons about the game, which include lots of grinding on some servers, and some features are till \"incomplete\". The game is technically still in development, and with the future \"MMO\" game being developed on the same engine/base-game, lots of features are still being added and completed.
There is a bright future for this game, and it\'s in a \"play ready\" state. I suggest you check it out!

I love the hell out of this game. Its a nice balance of arcady dog fighting action and pseudo simulation space combat.
You want to feel like Luke Skywalker fighting off the Deathstar? Fly in to the enemy ship take out their shield generator, then hit their core and by the time you finish that off the enemy carrier is about to go up in smoke.
It has a really interesting hit and run mechanic. It takes time to repair your ship, which can mostly only be done in the docking bay of your own carrier. Also burning through ammo happens pretty frequent. So it really encourages you to go back to the dock and swap out your ships to repair/reload your old one.
The ship customizing is a lot of fun. There are a lot of variables to take in to account to customize your fighter. Slow ships seem like they'll be better at defending your own carrier. Fast ships with light payloads seem better for hit and run tactics on the enemy carrier. But if you're to slow at hit and running the enemy carrier parts may heal up your damage. So, maybe its better to take more ammo or higher damaging weapons, but then it'll slow you down and make it harder to run away in a dog fight. So many things to consider, and so much fun to be had.
Its also nice that fighter parts aren't 100% better upgrades. You can level up parts to make them stronger, but they come at the cost of requiring more energy, heat, or weight. So sometimes it is better to go with a lower level part just so you don't weigh yourself down and can boost for longer and faster. This also means that low level ships when you first start do have some small advantages over higher level ships. While you don't be able to stand toe to toe with the highest level guys, you still won't be completely screwed either.
Also, unlocking and leveling up parts is at a very steady progression. When you first start the game you'll have more credits then you know what to do with. But after that you won't have enough credits to get what you really want, but it only takes about 2 games to get enough credits to unlock what you want. So it never feels too grindy.
The current game community is really small. But I personally have been having a lot of fun still just playing against Bots. I've been in one game with 4v4 and the game completely changes. Suddenly those hit and run tactics aren't so effective against players (because bots are stupid).  But I assume its still viable, just need to rethink it a bit.
I feel this game is the perfect level of space sim and arcade dog fighting action. For example, it's really satisfying to fly past an enemy fighter, do a quick 180 degree maneuver, cut out the engines for a sec to continue to drift forwards and blow your enemy to ribbons as they attempt to do the same thing. Some real epic space combat there.
I highly recommend this game. Its awesome. Buy it so I have more people to play with.

I bought and played Amnesia because it seemed to be pretty favorably reviewed. The game was praised for being atmospheric and scary. The problem is, that's not enough.
It certainly is atmospheric, and it has some startingly unique gameplay mechanics. When I first woke up in that castle I was excited to explore it.
But a couple hours in and the magic has worn off. You're in the same setting the entire time, so the environment gets old and boring, no matter how atmospheric it was to start. And once you master the mechancis the only new thing to challenge you is the puzzles, which vary from simple to obtuse, but in general are not that well designed. Moving through the levels is pretty linear and exploring doesn't benefit you nearly as much as I'd hoped it would.
The game does have a few truly scary moments, but most of it is just typical pop-out cheap-horror-movie fare.
The voice acting is really good - it's probably the game's high point in my mind. But the story they're telling isn't all that interesting. It opens some good questions in the first act, but by the time you finish this short adventure none of the intriguing points have been explored. I suspect the writers themselves didn't know the answers.
Despite a couple praise-worthy points, there just isn't a whole lot of game here.

I have quite a few hours on this off Steam. It's one of the few games I like enough to buy twice.
Most people who've played both seem to like Warband better, and I'd have to agree that certain aspects of WB do make it a little easier to get into, one of the major ones being that you'll probably never get killed by some ♥♥♥♥ing peasant with a musket in the land of Calradia.
That said, I think that the majority of the people who don't like this game much only feel that way because they don't realize that you need to play it very differently than Warband. It's about commanding your army more than glorious personal combat, all because of the guns. This is a good thing, really, because an unskilled dude being able to kill someone who'd trained all their life for melee combat and had invested a small fortune into their equipment by simply pointing a cheap, crude little stick at them is what ended the feudal era. Very, very few games set around this time (or even far, far later) really accurately represent how game changing a gun really is.
The key to having alot of fun with F&S is to play it more like a first person strategy game. Don't charge in there with your mass of calvalry, maybe telling your handful of ranged guys to stand just a ways off of where the collision will occur. This will probably work if you personally don't get killed, but you will take some ridiculous losses. Instead, fight like you would if you were engaging a wall of enemies with deadly ranged weapons. Move up behind hills, set your own musket lines up, and let them slug it out  for a bit. Move around the side with your calvalry. When the moment is right, and the enemy is a little scattered, fix your bayonettes, sound the pipes, and ♥♥♥♥ing CHARGE! Your losses will still be noticable, depending on your army composition, but you can always get more conscripts, and the odds of you getting shot by just one or two ♥♥♥♥ing peasants with muskets is pretty slim.
This is the uncaring, unglorious, bloody fighting that is musket warfare, and this is the whole reason to buy this game.
In every other way, the game is actually quite a bit better than vanilla Warband. UI is better, menus are better, recruiting isn't really better per se, but much more realistic. Trade is better, etc. etc. It's sort of like fallout 3 and New Vegas - one seems pretty great untill you play the other, then it's hard to really go back and get the same sort of enjoyment out of it.
Buy it if you want to support a good franchise, or if you think fighting with muskets sounds fun. If you want glorious personal combat, the ability to strike terror into your foes with Winged Helms, and battles that can always be won just by riding your horse in a circle, buy Warband instead.

SOMA very quickly became one of my favorite games I've ever played (Wizardry 1, Skyrim, Talos Principle). It's not every day that a game makes you think like this. If you transfer your mind to a simulation, would you still be you? If you started a task that you would never be able to see completed, would you still do it? Are human minds simply computers whose state is instantiated by a memory and a sophisticated algorithm? Is all of existence simply a simulation in some vast computer?
Pros:
Wonderfully atmospheric graphics. The underwater scenes trecking between stations was my favorite part. The lighting and sense of isolation was fantastic. It felt like a combination of the movies Aliens and the Abyss.
The final scene at Phi. Just wow.
The imagination of the story, and the characters.
Cons:
I honestly felt this game could've done without the monsters. The story and the graphics would've held up the game just fine without the (sometimes) frustration that they introduced. Why does this game need to have any horror elements at all?
On a scale of 1 to 10, where it's actually possible to score a 1-5 (ahem, IGN), I would easily give this a 10.

SOMA is a must have in your library - even if you're not a fan of Frictional games, this one stands out by not being a tedious medieval setting with somewhat shallow storyline and a bunch of uninpisred monsters crawling around abandoned castles.
This is so much more than a simple "survival horror" game - it's does not rely on your typical jump scares, it doesn't have an ending with a predictable twist that makes you question the morality of your past actions, it doesn't come off as a blunt and in-your-face. What this game does is gradually mess with your mind to the point that when you finish the game and you see the credits roll, you really start pondering about what humanity is really about. It starts off with a simple questionnaire, you simply tick how you feel and throughout the game it makes you reconsider every single decision you marked.
It forces you to look at yourself from another perspective.
You feel for the characters and it leaves with more question than answers. It does so in a very refined way through a compelling storyline, interesting and claustrohpbic environment, rather simple logical puzzles and last but not least, without any gimmicky elements.
This is Frictional Game's finest work and one of the most important PC releases this year - saying anything more would be a huge spoiler. Just grab the game and "dive" in to one of the most mindboggling adventures that will eat your heart out.
10/10, highly recommended.

Übermosh is an intense ride through and through. You get 90 seconds to survive and take down as many gun-wielding alien goons as possible, and initially, you only get a sword. You bring a knife to a massive gunfight. Luckily your blade is capable of reflecting and splitting enemy fire and forcing them to eat their own bullets.
Graphically, the game is very simple, but effectively incredibly intense. You'll see classic pixel sprites and a constant smooth 60fps throughout. It's also incredibly color and plain fun to look at.
Gameplay wise, this game is a roller coaster. You get a few different classes to choose from, and each of which you'll have to master if you plan on 100% completing this game. No Class Mod has you start with a sword only, but allows you to pick up enemy guns, and you get 4 hits before you fall. Kensai allows use of only the sword, but you get six hits before game over. Gunner gives you a fully automatic gun at the cost of your sword and give you only three hits. The last and frankly best class is Warlock, which gives you use of the sword and the best gun in the game right out the gate. However, just two hits and you're down for the count. Completing this game requires you to get 150 points with each class, 200 points with any class seven times, surviving the full 90 seconds seven times, and attempting (but not beating) Hardboiled Mode. If you love games that are purely score-based and are easily motivated to beat your own high score, this game is tailor-made just for you and I guarantee you'll have hours of fun.. If you don't break your mouse. By the way, I do highly recommend using the keyboard and mouse over a controller. I personally find the twin-stick shooter controls awkward and troublesome. It works smoothly and everything, but it's simply not my cup of tea.
The music in this game is by far the best element, and the developer was smart to include the soundtrack as DLC. I can't really describe it well but I guarantee you could listen to it while fighting off an alien invasion and be pumped and focused the entire time.
I absolutely recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun, difficult time killer! It's hectic, fast-passed and difficult, so beginning gamers may have a tougher time, but give it a bit of practice and you'll have it completed in a matter of hours.
9/10

TL:DR  I've wasted almost 19 days of my life playing this game which says more then this review ever could. Cons are very present but you'll most likely get addicted and have to buy a new keyboard because you smashed yours against your desk from getting headshotted by a boneless Ash.
Cons
-Exterme learning curve
This game while very fun is one of the most challenging shooters I've ever played. Map knowledge, operator knowledge, and weapon knowledge is the key to becoming decent at this game. There is so much to learn and when you are thrown into the game with just 10 situations and a few tutorials it is hard to really understand the game until you have at least maybe 50 hours in the game which is where things start to click. You start knowing where objective locations are, drone out spots, and understand the peekers advantage. This game is fun but you will be put on you a** many times when starting out.
-Toxic community
This can be taken with a grain of salt because it all depends on how you look at this. My experience after 400 or so hours is that you get a mixed bag but there are no in between you either get some decent people who are team players, communicate, and play the game the way it was hopefully intended. On the other end of the spectrum there are many players who are just looking to ruin your, and others day. TKing, killing hostage, s**t talking, and throwing games are very present in this game. Ubisoft has taken "some steps" to "prevent" these things from happening but a 15 minute ban for TKing and screaming at teammates to kill themselves because of a lost round is more of a slap on this wrist then anything. This may not seem like much and honestly it isn't to some many other game communities have worse players and things that happen but this is something that has finally started to bother me enough to say something.
-Ubisoft
This isn't so much a dig at Ubisoft themselves but the support for the game since it has released has been lacking. There are tons of bugs, poor servers, and lack of solutions for this because everytime Ubisodt tries to fix something they break 10 new things. The devs did launch operation health which fixed at least for me the long match queue times, and some random disconnects but this is an Ubisoft game and you should know what your getting into
Now for the pros I won't write essays for these unless needed because I still think this game is great and it has the numbers and playerbase to prove it. This game is one of my most played games and regardless of the frustration and anger it brings me I still kept coming back for more and thats says something.

As I'm writing this its hard for me to think of pros for this game which is weird because I've wasted about 19 days of my life playing this game which says more then this review ever could and other people have tons more hours than me.

Having bought the game after 'A Kind Ale War' (Australian youtuber... watch him you) I knew what I was getting into and I can say that it does not dissapoint.
It is a simple game; you spawn on an alien planet with a sword and some Health. You deflect an aliens bullets back at him, kill it, take its gun and kill everything else until you die. Its simple but fun; and its gameplay is sploffing fantastic. There are a few modes, in one of which you spawn with the best gun in the game and you go on a rampage; another limits you to your sword (I love it) and another limits you to your gun.
There is a Hard mode for you suicidal folks out there which is not needed because the game is not easy, far from it. Not that its hard to learn, its just hard in general; you are going to need twitch skills to avoid jumpscaring damn Aliens coming out of the corner of your screen.
What about the problems? Well, there is one. One huge one. There is not enough content; as soon as you spawn and play for a Min or so (if you do not die) you have seen most of the content on display. I reccomend a few updates to the game to increase its content; new enemies, new maps (I wanna see a jungle damn you!), new weapons, new everything! This game has a fantastic OST and its gameplay is perfect, if it were to have more content it would be a fantastic game.
For now its a very good game in its own right, little bursts of gameplay for the lols every now and again (because the loading times are brilliant) are nice, but if you dont give me enough content to keep my intrested I will not stay intrested and I will go off to play a game with more substance.
I rate it a 8/10. Why not less because it has little content? Well, look at its price. Its great value, every pence you put towards this game will be rewarded with a good amount of content. Bang for your buck.
PS: You know that announcer at the start? I want to get that guy's voice in my life.

Offword Trading Company is a fun, challenging, economic trading sim. It's the only early access game I've played that I would actually recommend buying in its current state. It already feels like a complete game, and a fun one at that.
To start a match, you and your competitors search mars for a place to start your business ventures. The map is randomly comprised of different resources, used to either support your colony, or turn a profit. There are a couple of different colonies, all of which use the available resources differently, providing a slight variety on play-styles.
The matches last around 30 minutes or so, which I think is a nice change from the time-investment of the Civ games.
There is also a blackmarket, where you can purchase goods to sabotage your competitors, or even manipulate the market in your favor. Be aware: the AI are very well programmed -- don't expect any mercy!
"Is it worth the price?" Yes! Stop asking and start playing.

I can't recommend this game. Do not pick it up. It is conceptionally flawed in a way that prevents any newbie to win against a veteran player. I bought this game during a sale, because its concept was nice. Back then, it was a few months after release, the game was almost dead already. (It is dead right now)
The game was fun for the first couple matches, because there were a good amount of newbies and 2nd Tier ships at most around. At that point the game was balanced. After a few more matches a Vetern joined with a Tier 5 ship. In a 5v5 match setup our complete team, all newbies in Tier 1 and Tier 2 ships, kept firing at that guys ship and he won. He literally outtanked all of our damage and killed us 1v5. It wasn't that we were bad, it was just that our ships weren't leveled enough. Not enough damage, not enough hull. The Tiers are balanced to each other but as newbie in this game you have lost the match before it even started.
It is the reason this game is dead. No one will put up the required hours to die their way to a max level Ship, just to be on equal footing with people that played the game much longer. I soon there after abandoned the match, as the realisation sunk in with the end of the promo weekend, that there just weren't enough newbies around anymore to have fun or level up.
The game's mechanics canabilse its own newbies, by making it completely impossible for them to have fun if they are in a match with people that played the game for much longer.
It was a good and interesting game, as long everything was balanced, but the low player base means you'll be joining matches with veterns in much stronger ships than your little dingy ship can measure up to. Its a fun game to play during sales, when new blood gets into the game, but as soon as the sale dies down, you are most likely going to deinstall the game.
Save your money.

In short, this is 3d shooter-maneuver game with 4x4 lobby action.
Features:
* 1 v 1 space mothership battle in space
* getting and choosing upgrades for your ships
* using two customizable in-battle abilities
* coordination with your [up to 3] teammates
* running away from angry enemies who don't like you near their mothership
Pros:
* not Yet Another World War 2 Simulation with "real planes" which is disbalanced
* not Yet Another Game Pretending To Be Space Sim (space simulations do not exist)
* upgrades for ships are directly influencing your balance levels and showed in percentage weight of your team setup - easier team setting
* maps are quite big, with jumps and regeneration zones (though I did't get in everything this yet)
* 4 races with only 2 slots leaves you with at least 6 combinations [but usually much more setups]
* after you get your hand with it, allows you establish your team for fighting more skillful and good teams
* weapons allow you to choose different combat role
* unique: weapon powers combinations
* unique: power-heat-weight ship balancing
Cons:
* no single player things -  it is MP game
* not fun to be played with bots - obviously, as it is same as Counter-Strike in space
* game not have much popularity [yet], but there is always some guys in lobby
Verdict: Counter-Strike in 3d is unique game idea, which no other product offers.
