This was one of my very first adventure games when I was a kid. I used to make my parents rent this from the video store (back then you could rent PC games). Anyway, I really loved the original Gabriel Knight: Sins of the Father. The story was so rich, gritty and romantic. I played that game so much that the playthrough had been burnt into my memory. I was super excited that it was going to be remade, and lo and behold, it was JUST like the original. I mean, everything played exactly the same. (Of course it's not completely the same without the big name voice actors the original had - but the new cast does a solid job for the limited budget this remade had.) I still recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a good point and click adventure. The story is really good, and the characters grow on you in a big way. If you played the original - you might want to grab this just for a walk down memory lane - but there isn't really anything new story-wise. I got 100 percent completion 20 years later from memorizing the same exact game. That's how much I loved this game in the first place. :) Was still a lot of fun and I appreciate the attention this old treasure got.
Update: I read some negative reviews complaining about the graphics and stuff of this game. The original game was very cutting edge back in the day (animation, voice acting, etc)...so it's hard to re-capture what was felt back then in a remake with today's standards. This is a low budget remake of a 20+ year old game that's one of the grand-daddys of a genre that's pretty much dead (point and click). Don't expect Witcher III.

I came into this game knowing nothing about the concept or what to expect from the story. I have to say, this took some time to get into, but it was worth it.
My first impression, after the first couple of puzzles, was that this game is style over substance. In my puzzle games, I expect there to be a logical, contextual reason behind why they appear. The vast majority of Tormentum's puzzles appear to exist for the sake of the puzzle, which initially put me off. It was hard to get a good grip on how the world and characters function.
, the gorgeous art and surreal tone made me continue playing, and I got a hunch about how this could all make sense. I saw it through to the end, and despite my earlier negative thoughts about the story and setup, I ended up really enjoying it and valuing the experience.
It's a neat little story that took me four hours to complete, and I feel my time was well spent. It's nothing exceptionally original when you break it down, but it's presented through unusual setups that match the solid stylistic choices. The writing matches Giger's art style beautifully.
I would say that its price tag is perhaps a little high for what gameplay you get out of it, as I don't think there is a whole lot of replay value. On the other hand, there must have been incredible time and effort put into all the art in this game, and with that in mind the game is cheap.
Tormentum is dark and beautiful without making me feel like it's trying too hard to be edgy or disturbing, and it left me appreciating the experience. In the end I have to recommend it.

I love Magic: The Gathering, but I can't say Magic 2015 is worth buying. If you get it in a bundle like I did, it's somewhat worth trying just to have a go at building your own deck (something that Magic 2014 did not provide). In fact, the Humble Bundle is the only reason I even own this game. I actually refused to pay retail for it because of the rumours about its quality. As such, I cannot recommend buying it at its standard price for two reasons. Firstly, £6.99 gets you the bare bones of Magic 2015. If you buy this version, you will need to unlock all your booster packs in game, either by winning games or buying cards through micro-transactions. Alternatively, you can buy the special edition to get the DLC which gives you the boosters in advance. Given that the decks you are given to start with are poor quality compared to the decks used by the AI, many frustrated new players will be driven to buying the DLC to unlock the cards without having to win games. I consider this to be a massive money grab. Not to say that Wizards/Hasbro haven't tried this tactic before. It's just in this particular case, the game's design which combines basic decks and an overpowered AI, coupled with an easy way out (buying the cards) and a more challenging one (grinding for boosters) will draw many people to the easy way, because the hard one will take far too long.
The only reason I will continue to play Magic 2015 is for the deck building feature, since I love to build decks, but cannot justify buying the physical cards. The lack of a Puzzle mode, Two Headed Giant and Planechase (something I've missed since Magic 2013) makes this installment of the game barely passable. If Magic 2014 gave you the freedom to fully customise your decks, Magic 2015 may as well not have been released at all. Don't waste your money buying this game and definitely don't waste it buying the DLC booster packs.
Hasbro, you failed. 2/10 (Were it not for the deck building, it'd be a flat 0).

After the legendary development hell, and the near legendary last-minute rescue by Gearbox, Duke Nukem Forever had no chance to meet any kind of expectation. Reviews were poor to scathing though the game sold more copies than expected, perhaps at the cost of longtime PR companies' reputation.
As a historical relic, it is a fascinating journey through trends in game design. Almost in chronological order, the game meanders it's way from era to era, adapting the conventions of the Half-Life 2 era, moving on through Doom 3, and eventually settling on Halo-esque recharging health and COD cover based shooting.
It is a startlingly ugly game both in tone and look. The early levels have a post-processed spit-shine, and depth-of-field is abused like a crack ♥♥♥♥♥'s dignity. Later levels become exercises in how unfinished the game can appear and still function.
Following a Duke who made famous by his world-saving exploits, locations include parts of Vegas and the desert. Women are plastic and disposable, thought they are obstensibly the point of the plot as saving them is the driving force for what resembles a plot.
The blantent mysoginy culminates in a unintentionally disturbing trip through a dark underground Hive where women are not only naked, and glued to columns but actively being impregnated by alien spiders. The only recourse is to watch them explode into baby spiders or to explode them by shooting them before they blow up.
As an independant exercise in circle-strafing, DNF can be fun and early on the unapologetic sexism results in some funny moments but the game wears quickly.
DNF is longer than expected or wanted, and after fighting the same three stage boss 10 times, I quit Duke 4 chapters from the end, but not before Duke quit me.

A good, fast-pased but relativley relaxing economy game.
In it's current state, this game litterally throws you into the deep(ish) end. Non-intuitive game mechanics and lack of any true and thorough tutorial makes searching up a guide on build orders and tips almost essential. To give you an idea of the situation; I failed the first tutorial twice because it's not clear, nor does it explain that you have a "claim" limit. (more on this later)
Once the surface is scratched, and mechanics are better understood, the game becomes much better. Many things in the game will appeal to fans of mass, streaming-economy RTSs. Real-time indirect agression against the enemy player is very remeniscent of other games such a Sid Mier's "Trains".
The game can be very punishing towards mistakes made, a single wrong move in the early-mid game can spell disaster for your company. One such example is the "claims" mechanic, which gives you a limit on the number of tiles you can take before progressing. Take the wrong tile, and even if you remove the building there, you cannot unclaim it, leaving you with an incorrect, useless tile for the rest of the game.
Despite it's unforgiving nature, Offworld Trading Company is already (despite being early access) an excellent game with great potential for hours of fun.

I have been playing Offworld Trading Company since release in March and have found it to be an excellent game.  The game is easy to learn and play but has a depth that belies it simplicity.
There are 4 HQ types with different traits and advantages, they provide a wide variety of strategies to win the game.  Offworld Trading is best described as an Economic RTS, as you upgrade your HQ you receive more claims to mine resources or refine them via factories/plants, sell your products into the market to gain cold hard cash.  Use your cash buy shares in completing companies eventually taking them over and reigning supreme as the only corporation left standing.
There is no combat system as such, no need to furiously click your way to victory, however there is a Black Market function where you can buy various items to either slow you opponents down, like an EMP to freeze his/her factories for a short time or mutiny their power plant glassworks, taking those tasty profits for yourself.  Other items will give you a boost, increasing your production or a goon squad to catch those stinking saboteurs.  The game is very well balanced and there are many ways to squeeze the most profit out of your tiles.
I play multiplayer exclusively because it's so much fun, the AI is excellent and well programmed, but playing against 6 other people is miles better, this game really shines when you have a good group of human players.  Typical game lasts 20 -40mins which is the perfect length for me.
Pros
Simple to play and very rewarding for the casual player, but plenty of depth for more serious gamers
Very well polished, stable and balanced for an Early Access game, imo it could be released tomorrow at full price.
Gameplay is intense and very fun but not frantic like other RTS games.
Devs are very active in the community and actually listen to feedback.
Cons
Difficult to find higher level players to play with if you live in Europe (unless you want to stay up till 2am)
If you like RTS games then this is a must buy, I am very happy with my purchase, great re playability, really shines in multiplayer.  10/10

So the Duke Nukem 3d 20th Anniversary World Tour is going to be released soon, so in order to celebrate I decided to play Duke Nukem Forever again, to see if I hated it as much now as I did when I preordered it. So, do I still think it's the worst game ever? Well...no. I've certainly played games that were much worse. But I still think it's pretty bad.
Duke Nukem Forever is guilty of using just about every gimmick and cliche used in FPS games made in the 2000-2009 era, and I wish I was joking. Magically regenerating health, limited stamina, only being able to carry two weapons, forcing you to solve puzzles to progress, events where you either have to take control of a turret or drive a vehicle...you name it. But out of all these tired and overdone cliches, what really seals the coffin on this game for me is that this game is made up entirely of quicktime and scripted events, and the levels are so linear there's no room for any exploring whatsoever.
In other words, instead of the fast-paced and intense gameplay in a large map that required us to explore high and low for secrets, health,  ammo and keys to progress, while at the same time trying not to die to entire armies of aliens? That's all been replaced with linear paths, scripted events and NPCs that refuse to let you progress until you've either killed a few aliens the game wanted you to kill, or force you to listen to meaningless dialogue that adds little or nothing to the game, but thought you should listen to it anyway.
So did Duke Nukem Forever do anything correctly? Kind of. Duke is still that womanizing horndog that we got to know and love in 1996 that spews one liners and cracks jokes. However, unlike Duke 3d where it was done with some moderation, this game feels like it was filled to the brim with almost nothing but toilet humor and nudity galore. Not necessarily a bad thing, but my goodness does it tend to get old quickly.
I didn't exactly expect Duke Nukem Forever to be a masterpiece after waiting for more than a decade for it to come out, but I did expect it to be something refreshing and new. Unfortunately it was neither of these things, and while I don't think it's the worst game ever, I've played far too many games that were just like it. 1.5/5.0

It's difficult to view and judge Duke without taking his past into account; and this is partly good and partly bad. It's good because Duke is a legend in the gaming world, therefore anything involving him gains automatically a lot of value. And it's bad because seeing how the game Duke Nukem Forever, after taking forever to be completed and relased, didn't turn out as glorious as Duke the man deserved, it's somewhat unfair.
That said, Duke Nukem Forever is not a bad game; it's a generally nice game and on certain occasions it's very good. It has well-made environments - sometimes particularly atmospheric, like the Ghost Town in the main game or the Tunnels in the DLC; the music is fine and fitting; there are several known enemies making a comeback (the Octabrains are back with a vengeance), and of course Duke is his usual badass self, with his hilarious lines and his ever-mighty boot.
What doesn't seem to work that well is the general gameplay design; it feels rushed and incomplete. Some of the puzzles look complicated, but in fact they are so easy, you may end up solving them without realizing it. The vehicle mechanics are frustrating at times, and some of the boss fights drag on too long. And you may find that, apart from wanting to get certain Achievements, there is probably no big replay value. I guess that all that went wrong with this game is due to the fact the development team didn't remain stable from start to finish and at the end they had to complete the game somehow and release it with no further delay (just like it happened with Tomb Raider: The Angel of Darkness).
Still, I did enjoy the game to some degree, which is why I am recommending it; also for sentimental reasons, because Duke Nukem 3D was one of the very first games that I played years ago.

Alright, after playing in the alpha, beta, and now the finished product I can say this is by far one of the funnest games I've played in a long time. The story (I'm only in chapter two) is not half bad for the style of game that For Honor is. I see the story as there to help you learn to play the different heros and give you a nice little collection of items and steel to start playing the multiplayer. It has enough there to make it feel like a short storyand doesn't feel bogged down with an array of detail and cut scenes that can actually make a game worse (the Final Fantasy series after Final Fantasy IX is a great example of detailed story ruining gameplay).
The multiplayer isn't nearly as bad as those who don't like it say. For Honor has a unique battle system that actually requires skill to be good at. If you aren't paying attention to where you need to block, you will die; doesn't matter who you are. You have to time when you want to start your combo and if you miss, you have to be smart enough to quit swinging your weapon so that you don't loose all your stamina. I prefer the assassin style hero because I can't block for♥♥♥♥♥♥ but I know I can dodge; not getting hit and not dying are key to winning a match reguardless of game mode, hero or skill level. I've beaten players who had better gear, higher levels, etc. Just by having better timing and blocking/dodging than the other player.
After seeing what the delux, gold and season pass offer it boils down to wether you want to pay to unlock everything immediately or you can just buy the base game and unlock everything the old fassioned way (which is how games are meant to be played). Not paying the extra money, the only thing you won't get is a few skins. Sure you get new heros a week earlier than everyone else for your money but in a week everyone will have it and they didn't pay for it. If you want this game, don't waste your money on the extras it's not worth it in my opinion. Maybe an expansion with new maps would be worth paying for but as of now what is offered is not worth the $40+.
All in all I think this is a great multiplayer game, the story mode is more of an extended tutorial that takes you through each of the basic classes for each fraction.

I've never played Knights of the Old Republic (and it's 2015) so my review will be based on my experience alone.
Personally, I don't think it's aged too well, graphically it looks like a PS2 game, the voice acting isn't great, and the default controls for a gamepad are missing some of the vital commands. (Support for gamepads are from a new update, but don't do the game full service)
However, the game seems to be rich in dialogue, characters, Star Wars lore, and filled with RPG elements and plenty of loot to make each step feel rewarding. It does a great job to make you feel like you are in a large Star Wars Universe filled with uncertanties and adventure. (controlling droids is actually pretty cool)
The combat system is... kind of dated. It's basically a real time action turn-based system where you select what attack you want to do, and your character will basically move for you and do the attack.  I kind of feel like this is where I was let down.  If there is ever a sequel, I'm hoping that it'll be more like an FPS or Third-Person with more user control.
Overall, I feel like it's a good, but a bit dated. If you are a fan of RPGs, want some Star Wars lore, and are okay playing with some PS2 era graphics / gameplay, than I'd definitely reccomend this for $5 or so.

I usually don't preorder games, but I preordered SOMA because I finished Amnesia just a while ago, and wanted more.
If you have played Amnesia, you kind of know what to expect:
Puzzles
Story
Enemies chasing you
However, there are also many differences:
+Enemies no longer despawn after killing you; instead they knock you unconscious, giving you a "second chance" before having to restart at a savepoint
+The story is ALOT more interesting - instead of an "I am Daniel, I have lost my memory, I have to kill Alexander"  we now have a quite involving story with multiple twists. However, the smallest spoiler could ruin the story quickly!
+/- Puzzles are quite simple, but instructions are unclear in a few cases - got tentacle stuck in interdimensional portal to Tartarus
+/- The inventory system is simplified - no need to combine items in your inventory or something
*/- Health and Sanity are not restored by potions anymore - "Sanity" restores itself over time, and Health is restored by shoving your fist into a space-robot butt placed at fixed points
+/-Your Flashlight has unlimited battery power - no more Oil management or running out in critical situations, less tension
-Enemies are more scripted encounters that they were in Amnesia - they pop in at spot A then they pop out again at spot B; one enemy is literally waiting behind a door for you to open it, and then chase you around while another door is taking like 20 minutes to open
?-We also have support for Custom Stories with the Steam Workshop, but right now, we only have test files uploaded by the devs - time will tell whether we can get amazing custom stories like we had for amnesia.
Overall, this game was fun to play and a good way to get a nice scare here and there.
TL;DR: If you only want horror, get Amnesia; if you want horror combined with an engaging story, get SOMA

Voodoo down in the Bayou.  You play as Gabriel Knight, a sometimes successful, sometimes creepy, playboy and author.  You haven't sold a book in like, forever, but that doesn't stop you from owning a book shop in downtown New Orleans and employing Grace, your assistant who helps you with writing and managing your shop.  She also stays even though you can't pay her- and despite your *constant* creepy advances.  Currently you are working on a new book involving voodoo and it just so happens there has been a string of "Voodoo Murders" in the Crescent city.  You happen to be buds with one of the detectives on the case and ask him if you might look around....for the story, of course...
I'm not normally drawn to these kinds of game, the point and click genre, but between Alpha Polaris and Gabriel Knight, I'm hooked and looking for more.  Also you get to learn about voodoo.  Who do?  You do.  Do what?  Learn about the voodoo.
Pros: This game intrigued me and sat on my wishlist for nearly a year before I got it cheap on a sale.  At first the game seemed a little slow figuring out the interface and the controls, and the story seemed wanting in the beginning, but when the wheels start turning, they start turning good and fast.  The story hooked me and though the ending was a little "meh", I felt overall joyed by this game.  The art and visuals were appealing, and the voice acting was actually good, despite me initially hating Gabriel's accent - I've grown to like it now.
Cons: Plotwise, I did have to check the internet every so often for clues on what to do next to keep the story progressing. And not innocent clues like "the key you need to unlock the door is on the shelf next to it, you silly!" but more of "You need to pull the lever in the basement to open the secret panel on the wall in the dining room to access the hidden keypad where you dial 39A90 to open the garage door so you can get the rock to smash the kitchen window to scare the bird so it drops the key.  But you have to talk to Paul first so he can tell you the code, and if you don't talk to him the code won't work."  There were at least three instances of this where there was no indication as what to do next.  The first one, without spoiling involves a mime, a hotdog, and a small child. Good luck!
Overall: 9.5/10

I got this game from the Humble Bundle, at a friend's recommendation, and I'm very happy that I did. (I'd definitely recommend that you wait until it's on sale before purchase, but that's just because of the state of the game. It's constantly being patched though, which is nice.)
It's a very complicated game, and if you don't like to ask for advice or use the Wiki to get an idea of what you should be doing, then this game isn't for you (YET) - keep in mind that most servers have a very helpful playerbase, though, as they all started where you are! Skill caps can be painful (though some servers have it set at 3000, which means with time you can do everything yourself if you want to keep busy), but do encourage a grouping mentality and specialisation, which is nice. I've made some good friends on the game already.
If you're playing on a server where Judgement Hour and Decay are in effect, suit up and claim up respectively. I've found that PVPers enjoy using JH as an excuse to grief or troll, as it doesn't reduce your alignment to 'commit crimes' during this time; if you're a bandit outside of it, your alignment decreases and your name changes from white, to orange and then to red below -50. It does, however, encourage tactics and teamwork, whether offensive or defensive, amongst your guild.
Decay is what keeps each server clean. Items off-claim decay and are destroyed at a pre-assigned (by the GM) rate, or not at all on some servers. It's easy to tell because damage effects are applied, and it's just better to make even a tier-1 monument claim and store all your stuff on it, than to lose it all the time.
Server Wipes are done on many servers every few months; I've avoided servers with server wipes, so I can't really judge, but I'd rather avoid my hours of hard work being put to the torch!
Best Advice: If you want to travel fast and ride horses eventually, set Warhorse Handling to 60 at character creation. It is by FAR the most painful skill to level otherwise!

Verdict: Get it! Its low price is very worth it.

This game is pure art and an experience. I took certain paths in my first playthrough and fully intend to replay enough to make all the other choices. The world the game takes place in, is essentially a living Zdzislaw Beksinski painting with a little Hieronymus Bosch and H.R. Giger thrown in. That in itself was enough of a selling point for me, but I also really enjoyed the narrative and the puzzles.
Some people who have played this game are upset about the way the morality works, but I think its fine if you remember the lens this world is viewed through. It's more mercy/compassion vs torture/suffering than a good vs evil dichotomy - which works pretty well, especially when you consider works of the artists that inspired this game. Other heavy themes are redemption and not passing harsh judgement on others, even on those who made very bad mistakes. I think that's pretty important considering the main character has obviously done something wrong (even though the exact nature of what, is a mystery until the end). But if you believe no one deserves a second chance, why should one be extended to you?
I didn't necessarily personally agree with one specific choice, but I also understood why it was that way. Also you have to play more than once to get the endings + achievements and its fairly short, so multiple playthroughs are encouraged anyway.
I really enjoyed this game a whole lot but I also love all the artists that inspired this game and am always interested in any sort of philosophical or psychological story. I recommend it, especially if these things appeal to you as well.

Alright, after playing in the alpha, beta, and now the finished product I can say this is by far one of the funnest games I've played in a long time. The story (I'm only in chapter two) is not half bad for the style of game that For Honor is. I see the story as there to help you learn to play the different heros and give you a nice little collection of items and steel to start playing the multiplayer. It has enough there to make it feel like a short storyand doesn't feel bogged down with an array of detail and cut scenes that can actually make a game worse (the Final Fantasy series after Final Fantasy IX is a great example of detailed story ruining gameplay).
The multiplayer isn't nearly as bad as those who don't like it say. For Honor has a unique battle system that actually requires skill to be good at. If you aren't paying attention to where you need to block, you will die; doesn't matter who you are. You have to time when you want to start your combo and if you miss, you have to be smart enough to quit swinging your weapon so that you don't loose all your stamina. I prefer the assassin style hero because I can't block for♥♥♥♥♥♥ but I know I can dodge; not getting hit and not dying are key to winning a match reguardless of game mode, hero or skill level. I've beaten players who had better gear, higher levels, etc. Just by having better timing and blocking/dodging than the other player.
After seeing what the delux, gold and season pass offer it boils down to wether you want to pay to unlock everything immediately or you can just buy the base game and unlock everything the old fassioned way (which is how games are meant to be played). Not paying the extra money, the only thing you won't get is a few skins. Sure you get new heros a week earlier than everyone else for your money but in a week everyone will have it and they didn't pay for it. If you want this game, don't waste your money on the extras it's not worth it in my opinion. Maybe an expansion with new maps would be worth paying for but as of now what is offered is not worth the $40+.
All in all I think this is a great multiplayer game, the story mode is more of an extended tutorial that takes you through each of the basic classes for each fraction.

I'm really not to sure if i should give it a good or bad review for a mulitude of reasons. I do want to start of by saying a few things about some of the reviews though.
Yes there multiplayer is broke as hell BUT the game did just make its full launch and it's gonna take time for them to come up with a solution for their servers.
NOW for my pros and cons. Both during, and after my beta experience.
During Beta:
The Beat was surprisingly well done.  I truly felt as the the beta WAS A BETA. And by that i mean the the game was near completion and you could tell it only needed few tweaks. Yes, some of the combat can be clunky at first but once you really started to understand the character, it would gradually become more fluid. On top of it, there really wasn't an over powered character. They each had there own way of going about a fight, and lacked in certain areas that you could exploit if you could find it.
When you launch the game you got a brief overview of the story that was going on before you jumped into multiplayer. Everyone chooses a faction and you can probably guess what happens from there. You fight to the death in one of 3 game modes: Brawls(1v1 + 2v2), Dominion, and Team Death Match. Que times were generally short(30s - 90s) but the main problem with the beta was creating a party. My friend and i never could connect with each other unless we used a third party application like Evolve(or hamachi), to directly link our pc connections. Wich sure, that's fine, because it was a simple work around. I personally love to have a 1v1 brawl because of how complex and drawn out a fight can be between to evenly skilled player. Dominon was ok, but most of the time i played, i was ganked about 90% of the time or the team balance was uneven, once again though, this is the beta i'm talking about and this is what they were looking to fix.
Though the Menu layout was tricky at first, once you take a few minutes to explore the menu's, it becomes more familiar, like most games. All around after the Beta i was expecting a grade A title game, 8/10 just forr the Beta.
After Full Release:
Now i'm not gonna go over every thing i just stated above because i feel as though you'r not gonna wanna hear me repeat the same thing 5 times over. So here's were im gonna start. Multiplayer: It's broke as hell. As i mentioned above, we had a simple fix that allowed us to que up and go right into a match and enjoy the game. Now it's not possible. I can understand were the problem lies because of the way their cheat engine works, becuase it doesnt allow 3rd party applications, it pretty much negates the work around. There is some hope that they'll fix this later but that's another story of it's own. As for getting into a match, it's impossible unless you decide you want to port forward to open up your NAT type. THIS IS RIDICULOUS. If i'm going to pay $60 for a game that primarly focuses on the multiplayer, i shouldnt have to learn how to port forward the game to BE ABLE TO ACESS THE CONTENT. Yes, i can do 1v1 brawls, but i have to wait anywere from 3-7 minutes, with only a chance to connect, and my NAT type is only moderate. I will never be able to join a dominion, teamdeath match, or a 2v2. At that point, the value in my mind, for a game that allows me to 1v1 2 or 3 of the same people, is roughly about $10.  Even with the extra characters they gave us. Along with the characters though, they decided to change some apects of combat. Now i'm an avid darksouls player, so getting use to new timings is fine and dandy till you break it. During the beta, people would use wahts called a guardbreak, wich pretty much gives you one free hit, or you can throw the other player around, BUT you were able to counter it by doing the same thing, it u timed it right after they did it. Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic: The Sith Lords (KOTOR 2) is an RPG developed by Obsidian and sequel to Bioware's Knights of the Old rebulic (KOTOR 1). Renowned for being released unfinished and buggy, I chose to play the game with 'Restored Content Mod' (Fixes bugs and adds cut content), Glowing lightsabre (lightsabres look much better) just so I can get the best experience.
- Excellent soundtrack = Definitely reminds you of Star Wars.
- Interesting characters = Your companions have a wide range of personalities, credits to Kreia and HK-47.
- Plenty of armor and weapons = Your can waer light, medium or heavy armor (when you unlock the ability) which have unique perks. There  are tons of weapons including pistols, blaster rifles, grenades and lightsabres. Weapons and armor can also be upgraded to have various effects and efficiency.
- Wide range of powers = You get a wide range of dark, light and universal jedi powers to play with.
- Train jedi/sith = As you play the game you can impact your "influence" over party mmebers by either your dialogues with them or actions (when they are in the party). When you have enough infleunce and meet certain conditions, you can train your companions into Jedi or Sith, giving them a wide range of abilities and access to lightsabres.
- Plenty of side quests = Each planet you travel to has plenty of things for you to do.
- Darker atmosphere = The plot is alot darker than it's predecessor.
- You can get lightsabre earlier = Unlike the first game where you can only get lightsabre mid/late game, in KOTOR 2 you are able to get your lightsabre early on if you go to certain planets first.
- Better graphics = The animations and lighting look better than the original KOTOR
- Controller support
- Widescreen support
- Still buggy = Got stuck (unable to move character) a few times while playing.
- Ending not that great = Just didn't feel as good as the previous game.
- Pazaak is a pain = Pazaak is a card game where you need to score higher than your opponent without busting (going higher than) 20. The draws are random and it can get frustrating since the game is linked to some side quests. There is a mod in workshop that makes it easier if your just want to progress through quests.
- Swoop Racing isn't fun = Similar to the first game with a few alterations at different araes. The problem is that you need to get an almost perfect score to win (fastest time), which generally involves not colliding to anything and getting most boosts (or else you need to start from begging). There is a mod in workshop to make this easier as well.
- Not Morally Grey enough = After you go to 'Nar Shadar', you are told that sometimes good actions can have offorseen consequences (such as when individual got mugged after giving him money). However whilst playing the game I found that this wasn't prevailent at all with 'Good' choices not having any consequences and vice versa.
- Shorter than original KOTOR = There are fewer planets to explore than the previous game and gameplay was shorter.
- Environments/map design isn't that great = I just didn't find them that interesting. They needed more things to make them feel more alive, like the previous KOTOR
- HK Factory boring = (Restored content mod) This factory wasn't interesting at all and it was understandable why it was cut. It is also very difficult so you need to make sure you have plenty of repaire kist and items for HK-47.
- Difficulty Curve = Also prevailent in previous game, sometimes you will face enemies which are a cakewalk to get through. Other times you'll be struggling to survive against the relentless horde.
Overall, KOTOR 2 is a good RPG. It's improves upon the previous games in a few areas, though in others it takes a step backwards. I highly recommend you play this game with mods to get best experience.

The game lets you roam around a house surrounded by attractive females. That's not to say that's the only reason to play. It contains a variety of puzzles to takle in order to get people to like you more.
Such as get me a certain item. For me I seemed to get stuck on one task for ages then i realised another mechanic of the game and i solved it swiftly. It's not necessarily the nudity that is the best part it's the challenge of getting there that is rewarding.
One issue is that saves don't always seem to work so you may want to save frequently. Also saying the wrong thing can close some dialogue options so you may be seeing quite a lot of restarts. But it's all in the fun of learning the little quirks of the game.
Try not to fall into the trap of thinking that each character has an ending because some are unfinished as i spent a few hours on trying to figure out what to do next. As me being a person that doesn't like to look at guides i went and researched to find out that the ending hadn't been completed yet. But it's in early access so what can you expect.
A lot of the story line is creative and fun. You'll be doing stuff that you wouldn't expect and it's very interesting.
The characted pathing can go a little wrong sometimes with a few people stuck on the stairs, but the AI seems to always manage to get to its location which is great. You can also move people out of the way by walking into them.
Also about the nudity there is a very simple patch you can apply to get it back. Took me about 5 mins to sort that out.
The story creator mode is great, although a little complicated as you have to go through a few downloads. But once you understand it there's a lot of fun to be had. You don't need programming knowledge to do it either as it's done with drop down boxes where you can select what you want.
The voice acting is good and they all have very distinct tones.
Overall if you like to be creative and do all sorts of things then this is the game for you. Laters and happy house partying.

Fire and Sword takes place much further along in history than the other Mount and Blade games. The inclusion of flintlock pistols and rifles may not seem like to much, but the game becomes very unbalanced with these new weapons. While trying to fight your way to capture a town, a single stray shot will hit and kill you. Thus the game thinks the battle has ended, but to continue fighting you have to use the automatic fight protocol (which sucks). I realize the developers were trying to modernize the game to include a bit different play style, but the balance is way off to allow for an enjoyable playthrough.
Try either the original Mount and Blade or Mount and Blade: Warband if you want that combat oriented conquering goodness of a game. Those two are much better balanced.

A fun little zombie side-scroller. In this game you shoot zombies, loot abandond buildings, and try to run to safety.
This game is very arcade-y, offers a few game modes, and keeps you entertained for its money's worth, and more.
Wide selection of guns and zombies, surprisingly for such a simple-looking game. The boss fights are pretty fun, but once you "get the hang of it" the game kinda becomes boring and less enjoyable.
There's not too much replayability and the local-only co-op isn't too convenient.
But nonetheless, it was a really fun little game while it lasted and I definitely enjoyed my time playing it.

I'm going to be honest, this game is nothing you havent seen already in games like WarZ, DayZ, among others. So what makes me come back(and you can the time I spent playing it which is something already)? Many things really but If I have to chose only one... I'lll choose pressure. When I enter the game, I feel an incredible amount of pressure, adrenaline, excitement. Why is this? Because these Nether creatures are deadly. These are no zombies which can be killed with a a hit or a shot. You got to be extremely careful and belive me, in this game is very comun to be kill by it's monsters. There are several types of Nether and each one has it's tactics, powers, caracteristics, etc.
But this is just one side. On the other one we have the players. Now, this game is full PVP, but I found some conforting in this small comunity. Sure most of the players kill everyone on sight, but in this game, you actually socialize more then I ever did in other games like this. You have groups now which is great, and doing missions with other people is amazing.
Now lets talk about the map shall we? It's small. Very small.... for now! For now because we only have access to like 15% off the full map. And the full map looks huge!! hehe. But the fact that the map is small right now, it does not bother me. On the contrary! This is what gives me such excitement! Being in a small map with other players and Nether creatures! And this isnt open land. This is full city! +1 point to the excitement stuff. Everything happens in a city and you have to survive in a city. You don't need to walk 92387592874528518451 miles to meet another player or important locations, you are in the important location. There's no resting, you need to pay attention to everything.
We also have diffrent types of missions. Like escorting people, delivering packages to other outposts, repairing the Anti-Nether devices at the lakeside outpost. And I'm sure we are getting more soon! =D My favorite is the package delivery. It's the best way to make money in this game, and I mean ALOT of money if you deliver it in the right place. But this gives me even more adreneline and excitement. It reminds me of the times I played silkroad online back in the day when I did some trades from city to city and you had to hire people(real players) to protect you from thieves(Real players too), and this revival of memories while I'm doing these jobs, it's the cherry on top for me.
Has for the developers, I don't know them or anything but with what I've seen so far, I'm really happy with these guys. They are diffrent, they feel diffrent. They listen to the comunity, they make this game better, and they are really quick. I think they are great.
If you like what I wrote and are an excitement junckie like meeeaaaii then I would love if you tried this game. You deserve it.
If you don't like what I wrote, no worries. I love you anyway and I want you to play this game.
If you like this kind of games, what are you waiting for? The next "walking simulator" patch? (a.k.a. DayZ)
If this is something you never played before, there's always a faaaahhhrrriiisssst timmeeee.
If you don't feel or don't like the game, re-read review. Repeat this step if the problem still occurs.
If you have no money... hmm...... go work for the local pizzaria and deliver a few pizzas. Perform some kind of minishow to get tips when you deliver it and the go home and buy this one.

It's got nice interface, comprehensive tutorial and decent engine, and as an old 'M&B' fan I felt myself almost at home here right away.. until I tried game hunting. Man, all the animations are so clunky it's painful to see in 2016! I've been playing 'M&B' since almost 10 years ago (alfa) and now I don't see any substantial progress in that respect. Stupid horses and then that elk.. I feel pity for them. Ok, I'll take a deep breath and tell you how it was.
The tutorial said I should select a patch of soil and choose 'search for peaceful animal tracks'. There was nothing. Being a city dweller I still surmised to look at a nearby lake's shore. I found tracks of cloven hoof, they appeared at the ground as highlighted texture spots leading to the forest. I followed that curved line and it seemed funny how it passed right through some large trees, that's where I started to feel suspitious about the software. After a while I spotted a couple of horses.. which should be odd-toed. Eh, who needs that foolish botany anyway? I closed on them, they just lied down before me. I thought it will be an easy task, maybe a part of tutorial.
My axe hit the nearest one in the head for no visible effect, it jumped up and ran away, but not far. I started chasing it to the lake, then to the mountain, it went through trees not noticing them and ploughed into uneven ground. On our way we also spooked an elk and some geese. I switched to chasing the elk. I managed to make a slingshot while it waited for me nearby. The animals also lacked animations, as well as the brains, they seemed to follow just one algorythm - kept some distance. After I had hit the mammal for the 20th time with a stone it turned on me and horned me till I fell unconscious.. without any animation.
The game is not finished, it's totally unpolished, crude as a stone axe, and it's technological basis already feels outdated! All in all, if you are very patient I strongly advise you to go build yourself a real house in the woods instead of playing this. For others there are much more cheerful middle-age lifestyle simulators on the market.

В основе своей это ваш симулятор колхоза, многопользовательская "Бешеная ферма" про управление временем, обогащенная чем-то типа боевой системы "Седла и клинка"/"Войны роз". Тут приятный интерфейс, понятное обучение и неплохой движок, и как старый фанат "СиК" я почувствовал себя сразу почти как дома... пока не попробовал охотиться на дичь. Боже, анимация так груба, что больно смотреть в 2016 году! Я начинал играть в "СиК" почти 10 лет назад (с альфы), и вот я не вижу серьезного прогресса в этом отношении. Глупые лошади, и потом этот лось... мне жалко их. Ладно, давайте я сделаю вдох и расскажу по порядку.
В обучении сказали выделить клочок земли и выбрать "поиск следов мирного животного". Ничего не было. Будучи гордским жителем, я все же сообразил поискать на берегу ближайшего озера. Нашел следы раздвоенных копыт, они появились на земле в виде подсвеченных текстурных пятен и вели в лес. Последовав по этой извилистой линии, я порадовался тому, как она проходила прямо сквозь большие деревья, тут я начал что-то подозревать об этой программе. Потом я заметил впереди пару лошадей... которые по идее непарнокопытные. Э, да кому нужна эта дурацкая ботаника? Я приблизился к ним, они просто улеглись передо мной. Я подумал, что это будет легко, как этап обучения.
Топор ударил ближайшую в голову без видимых последствий, она вскочила и убежала, но не далеко. Я за ней к озеру, потом на гору, она неслась сквозь деревья и тонула в неровностях почвы. По дороге вспугнули лося и гусей. Я переключился на лося. Умудрился смастерить пращу, пока он меня ждал неподалеку. Животным не хватало анимаций, равно как и мозга, похоже, у них был единственный алгоритм - держать некоторое расстояние. Когда я попал в эту тушу камнем в двадцатый раз, он развернулся и бросился меня бодать без всякой анимации, я упал в обиорок.
Игра не закончена, совершенно не доведена до ума, груба как каменный топор, а ее техническая база уже смотрится устаревшей! В общем, если вы очень терпеливы, настоятельно вам советую построить себе настоящий домик в лесу вместо этой игры. Для прочих на рынке представлены гораздо более веселые симуляторы средневековой житухи.

There are four types of indie games - bad indie game, "meh, just another indie game", good indie game and ASTONISHING indie game. And surprisingly - Beast Boxing Turbo is representing the last type.
First of all - gameplay is gorgeous. From the very beginning. Control is simple and intuitive (you need to pass through tutorial, but it's painless). Every match is very engaging and entertaining - some of them can be considered as too easy though, due to limits of AI (you can find some gaps in behaviour of your opponent), but don't worry - overall, it's still challenging experience.
It's incredible, that with relatively small amount of mediocre graphic  you can have so much remarkable and well animated characters. It's for sure not the most beautiful game in Steam library, but believe me - it's not bothering at all.
I really like music in this game - some themes are so memorable, that I like to listen them even long after beating the game.
As you probably guessed, this game is not too long. And that's unfortunately true. It has some replayability value, but still - I really would like to see more in-game opponents and multiplayer mode, but unfortunately, it seems that we can't count on any of those things in future.
Nevertheless - just for satisfactory and juicy gameplay I can recommend this game without hesitation. For everyone - due to its quite simple control and entertaining gameplay.

Do you know the feeling of nostalgica if you take an old game, start it and realize... it is still great?
A game I played last week was such an experience: Jets'n'Guns.
TL;DR: Jets'n'Guns is a great horizontal sidescroll shooter.
The story is typical. You are a freelance hero taking jobs from suspicious people in bars untill you're called to safe the universe. This leads you through dozens of levels spread over different settings, ranging from killing everything, planetary setting, different cities, zombieinfested worlds to metal festivals. \m/
The game is is held in 2D with good weapon animations and a great soundtrack delivered by the SID-Metalband Machinae Supremacy.
The game has half a dozen of different ships and dizens of different weapons. Just taking the strongest weapon won't help in most missions because of the ships mechanics. Each ship has a ifferent number of weapon slots for missiles, bombs and front and back weapon slots. each weapon generates heat while firing, limiting the use of weapons so you can't simply keep firing all the time. You need to wait for the right moment to shoot or you'll be run over by the enemy as the enemy does know how to shoot back, or simply fly into you and kill you that way. This leads to tinkering over the right equipment for each level.
Some levels end with bosses which require a special tactic each. Sadly most of them are equal to beat bosses in WoW: learn their attack pattern and evade their attacks, but stil, they are always challenging.
I recommend Jets'n'Guns to all action game and arcade lovers. You can get a solid 6 hours of gameplay for 6 €, and after playing through once, you can restart the game with your current equipment. Sadly, the enemy strength isn't adjusted, but at least you can take revenge for all those miserable deaths.

The game is a little too expensive. It's relatively short, and really easy. I'm really disappointed in it. Okay, I admit, because of an article (and the overwhelmingly positive reviews?) I'd read, I expected it to be REALLY GREAT, but even without that, I still would've been disappointed. So I think it's not an unfair judgement.
I want to at least start with the positive thing - the art. Clearly inspired by the works of H.R. Giger. At one point there are monsters that are pretty much copy+paste Alien. Also, there's a cute kitty that makes a real kitty sound, it's adorable. However, the game only takes up like half of my screen (in "full screen"), so I could hardly see anything well enough to really appreciate it. It makes it more disappointing though that the art had such a potential that completely went to waste.
Pretty much everything else is either bland or just bad.
- The mechanics of the game are kinda annoying. I know, in point&click games, you shouldn't expect too many shortcuts, but really, the screen scrolling with every move of the mouse when my laptop is just a little bit slow doesn't help. Also, having to open the bag each time to take an item out of it (at least the bag is not an extra screen), come on! Maybe there are games where the clumsiness of it is a good thing, but this one doesn't make up for the clumsiness.
- There's a lot lot LOT of mini-puzzles that have nothing to do with the game and are there just to make it last longer and seem more difficult, I guess. Yeah, yeah, I get it, before I open this door, I have to put an item into it, and then solve the puzzle which really doesn't require a lot of thinking, mostly just a lot of clicking. And then do the same thing ten times more.
- It's really easy. There isn't really much thinking about what item to use where, and that's not a bad thing, but my problem is that there aren't really any riddles. Just put this ball into this ball-shaped box and retrieve the item you need for that character who asked for it, so they can give you an item to put in another puzzle. But not before solving two mini-puzzles, of course.
- Also, the game doesn't really let you find stuff out on your own. The moment you enter a room, all the spots that need interaction start glowing. And don't get me wrong, I don't like those games that hide the important item in that one pixel you have to find after walking around for two hours and finally just resolving to scanning the whole screen with the cursor. But what they did here is kind of the exact opposite, and it's going too far. And to be honest, the one time I did really get stuck, it was because I missed an arrow to another room. They didn't make those glow for some reason.
- OH, also, remember clues you didn't realise were clues until you came across the puzzle you needed them for? Remember making notes? That must've been too 90's for the makers of this game. The character writes down everything he deems useful in a notebook he somehow has at all times. Yes, it absolutely is convenient, and it's also absolutely ridiculous.
But what most surprised and disappointed me is the dissonance between the reviews and the actual game, about the atmosphere and plot. Plot, what plot? It hardly has any. The game really tries to be super dark and atmospheric, and that's it. It tries. And fails. Honestly, I was hoping for creepy stuff! The art is helping, but it's not enough on its own, and I could barely see it (also, the screenshots on the store page are way brighter than in my game, but I didn't see any graphics options. I don't know if this is my laptop's fault). All the game does is talk about suffering. Wow, so deep. Very suffering. Much dark. I'm so moved. Also, you get choices that you have to make that are basically "do the good thing or do the bad thing", but nothing is as it seems! And it may turn out that you ended up doing the opposite. So eye-opening! The game doesn't even let you ponder  in peace how boring the plot "twist" was, the character sums it up with a big ol' moral of the story. And dear god, how didactic this whole game is, especially at the end. I got the feeling like it was intended for ten year olds. Also, at least in my (negative) ending, the credits get some pop metal song that really doesn't fit all the other music and overall theme of the game, and it's really pretty cringeworthy. The credits sum up the whole game: it really wants to be DARK, and it really isn't. And that's just sad.

I could grind on a random selection of the repeatable decks (they mostly get old really fast as you never have the removal necessary to effeicently defeat their creature synergy and aura strategies), but why bother? AND THEN THERE ARE MICROTRANSACTIONS TO ACCESS OTHERWISE UNAVAILABLE CARDS.  At least that's what I've heard, because I'm sure as hell not paying another $40 into this mess.  I already regret paying the money I already have for this game and I bought it in a humble bundle!

It looks like 2013 with it's planechase was the best version of DotP, and that is only if you don't count the original Microprose version that 17 years ago blew this pathetic pile of crap out of the water.  This game is a shameless cash grab and unworthy of anyone's time.

enjoy this chicken stir fry recpie
- Serves 4
- 10 mins to prepare and 10 mins to cook
- 325 calories / serving
- Healthy
INGREDIENTS:
- 1 orange, zested and juiced
- 2tbsp soy sauce
- 2tbsp sesame oil
- 250g (8oz) tender stem broccoli
- 5cm (2in) piece root ginger
- 1tbsp sunflower oil
- 1 garlic clove, finely sliced
- 1 red pepper, deseeded and thinly sliced
- 150g Straight To Wok Noodles
- 400g (13oz) chicken fillet, cut into thin slices
METHOD
Step 1 - Mix together the orange zest and juice, soy sauce and sesame oil and set aside.
Step 2 - Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain well and set aside.
Step 3 - Finely shred the ginger. Then heat a large frying pan or wok, add the sunflower oil, heat it until sizzling, and fry the ginger till it's crisp.
Step 4 - When it's done, remove with a slotted spoon. Add the chicken and garlic, and stir-fry until just browned. Remove the meat using a slotted spoon and set aside.
Step 5 - Add the red pepper and broccoli and stir-fry for around 2-3 minutes until it's just tender. Add the soy sauce mixture, bring it to the boil then return the chicken to the pan

UBERMOSH is a very fun arcade-style game where the player has 90 seconds to kill armed aliens and people and acquire a high score. That's basically all there is to it, and that's a major part of the appeal. It's a simple kill-everything game, and it does it well.
Something that I think should be changed is the display. The widescreen aspect ratio gives the enemies the perfect opportunity (which they take, frequently) to shoot the player the very instant they pop in by coming in from the bottom or the top. Changing the display to 4:3 and zooming out slightly would help greatly with this.
On top of the instant pop-in shots, another thing that makes rank progression difficult is the random nature of the game. Enemies don't spawn until 5 seconds into the round, and sometimes can't be found until around 10 seconds in. The enemy spawn rate will also change in the course of the round, I frequently find myself destroying a set of enemies then there's a large lull before more appear. It makes it feel like rank progression is based on the game's whims rather than personal skill when I can go 45 seconds and get about 100 kills sometimes and then other times go the full 90 and only get the same amount of kills.
This game isn't focused on being a game. It is amazing as the story of the guy who wrote "Why I'm so great" fighting off yet another wave of alien invaders all by himself.

Short review:
Its really fun, its fast paced, lots of killing, its in development, so that means that they will add more stuff, its cheap!... You should get it
(it still needs lots of work, but its fun)
Long review:
Like i said, its really fun and fast, it actually makes you want to start over and over as soon as you die.
Ill start by saying:
I know its in development, and thats the reason im going to express mi opinion of what could make this fun game an even greater game.
- Problem when dying:
Something i found a bit annoying (its not  a big deal, but it bothers me a bit) everytime you die it immediately throws you to a screen saying you died then main screen. And also, sometimes you dont even know what kills you, you simply die  (even when you thought no one was around)
- Probable Solution:
Add a screen in game when you die with the basic "Retry - Quit" Options.
and maybe add a "Killed by _____" in that same screen.
- More Game Modes:
- Time Survival with 3 lives, killing an elite or boss (you will see what im talking about below) get extra time bonus, or a extra life, everytime you die you get -15 sec or something like that.
A Game mode that will allow you to use the perks and abilities (see at the end of the review)
- Problem Variety of enemies:
its cool killing enemies over and over again, but since its a really fast paced game where enemies die in 1 shot (no matter which weapon you have, i will talk about this later) you start seeing the same enemies over and over again.
- Solution:
Im pretty sure this will be done, which is adding more kinds and types of enemies, but id be cool to see Elite enemies, maybe bosses? (which can handle way more than just 1 hit from any kind of weapon)
- Problem Weapons:
Same as enemies, nice weapons, specially the sword and the blaster that shoots purple thingys (which is op)
I think you should have a reason to why pick up any other weapon, other than the purple blaster, since enemies die from 1 shot and that thing has an amazing spread just spam it = Win (i was able to survive and get SSS rank by sitting in a corner spamming that gun. Since there is no reason to why pick up a slow 1 bullet per shot gun"
- Probable solution: Balancing weapons.
*Rifle/Magnum - slow, 1 bullet per shot = Big Damage
*Shotgun - decent spread, big damage BUT short range
*Automatic rifle - lots of fire rate, very low spread, mid damage.
And so on, you get the idea.
-Problem Maps:
Same, im pretty sure they will add more maps, but i think they should add more esthetic stuff to the maps, at the moment theres only 1 map and in only has these boring Tetris shaped walls and nothing more.
- Probable Solution:
When adding new maps or in the existing map, maybe add a few simple things to make it look better (depending on where the map is located at) adding stuff like wrecked cars, barrels, wrecked spaceships, stuff like that.
Maybe we can have a map located inside a spaceship?, that would be AWESOME!
Other Suggestions:
Bonus points -
Adding  Multi-Kill bonus.
X2 Points - maybe enemies drop the X2 bonus or if you keep killing enemies without stopping for like 2-3 seconds it keeps adding up?
Abilites or Perks:
Granade: After killing X number of enemies you will be able to throw a granade that wipes the screen
Shield: Grants you immunity to only 1 hit, slow recharged time. Killing an elite or a boss reduces the cooldown
Melee: Grants you more melee range, after a multi-kill everytime you swing your sword it will throw a wave killing everything on the path.

There's something about these fast paced, low-res ultra violence games that bring out that primal rampage part deep within your temporal cortex. Pump that adrenalin producing game full of bassy low but fast music and hard impact effects and you get a brutal thump of a game that deserves those capital letters; UBERMOSH.
Simple, pure rampage fun with no frills. There are a few games developed in full by a single person (
,
, et al) which really shine as a result, and this is one of them.
* Low price deserves special mention, there aren't many games on Steam I can comfortably recommend at full price, this is one of those rarities
* 10 Updates within 44 days of Early Access- this title isn't going to be lost in the wind
* Good effects that work well for the low-res
* Thumping low bass soundtrack
Unlike most Early Access games, there are very few issues, probably because of the games simple, hard-hitting nature. Currently the only real issue with UBERMOSH is it's lack of variety in bad guys, maps and content. There are a number of small things I'd like to see added, like Achievements, but they can't be classed as mistakes. If you're looking for reasons not to buy this, remember that it's currently being worked on full time by the developer, and anything below may have been changed since the time of review.
* The main menu is pretty unintuitive and messy. There are currently only 4 menu items and a class selector wheel, yet 90% of the title screen is taken up by the title image and the 4 selections somehow feel cluttered
* There's no reason to use anything other than the sword and the 6-Shot gun (which is currently the best gun in the game) so there's almost no variety in attacks after a certain time
* The aim-fixed camera and bobbing can cause light motion sickness for some
I'm usually hesitant to suggest buying Early Access, but for only £1.59/1.99€/$1.99 it's an oversight not to pick this one up and it's likely only going to get fuller. If you like the music featured in the promo video then it's also worth the extra £1.20/1.99€/$1.99 for the Soundtrack.
The one thing to hold you back is that it's likely to come up on sale for just a few pennies in the future, and will probably be all over Indie Bundles for less.
* If you're hankering for more of the awesome music, you can listen to the equally good and freely available soundtrack for
, by the same developer,
.

TL;DR: A fun action boxing game with a short career mode.
Set in an alternative universe with slums, aliens and monsters, you become the slum girl who wants to participate in the beast boxing tournament: boxing for monsters and only monsters, because humans are viewed weak and not up to the challenge. Thus a human wouldn't be able or even allowed to try their brawn in the ring. How's the girl going to fight the discrimination? Dressing up as a monster, of course!
The fight for equality aside, the story is very basic with the unlikely protagonist rising and training hard to become a champion. Albeit basic and familiar in a sense, the story is still very nicely presented and interesting to see through. Music and sound effects fit the setting well.
The game itself is really fun action boxing! One important thing keeping you hooked until the end is the career mode, which is also the main mode of the game. You start fighting in rings against lowest of the lowest opponents and even in higher difficulty levels the opponents will easily fall in front of you. Not going to how this is fairly unrealistic (the protagonist being a teenager against bigger monsters), but the fights sure are a lot of fun. It's surely not a simulation but it's not trying to be one anyway: for realism you might want to look elsewhere.
The opponents are talking pigs, aliens, turkeys, all kinds of vaguely bipedal fantasy monster races. There are even some ridiculous ones like a skeleton and a treeherd. They are hilarious and fit the theme well. All opponents have different attributes, like strength, health and speed and their own special attacks. Other than that, they are a bit too similar. There are basically just two archetypes: the speedy one and the heavy hitter, who might or might not require a different tactic to beat them depending on your difficulty setting.
Fighting is straightforward and easy to understand and works like fluid playing with a keyboard. You (and your opponents) may attack with any of the more or less familiar boxing strikes, like jabs or hooks. It's important to keep track of your stamina, which drains when punching or taking hits but also replenishes fast when not attacking. You win a round by emptying the opponent's health bar by landing punches and not letting the opponent do the same to you by blocking and dodging.
The AI can be nasty: it fights you giving fast punches when you're preparing for a strong strike and doing heavier hits when you are down. It even learns to anticipate your strikes if you don't change your strategy often enough. It was still fairly easy to shoot a hook at them when they're approaching and they would almost never see that coming, even when repeating the action.
One thing about the AI bugs me though: when the opponent is low on health they'll retreat to a corner. They will stay there so you have to follow them. When you do, they will always give you a punch or two and then retreat to the opposite corner. This exploitative tactic was really annoying when trying to finally down the opponent and call it a round.
In the story you get a couch who teaches you some important techniques (i.e. game mechanics) in the practice (tutorials). As the story goes on, your previous opponents decide to join your dojo and teach you more things. This is a nice and convenient way of handling the tutorials.
As you progress you win money, which you can use to train and buy equipment. The monster boxing rules don't seem to mind the fighters having some extra equipment while in the ring, though they are otherwise honourable to the basic rules of boxing. The equipment makes you e.g. stronger or faster but can also penalize you while giving higher bonuses to other things. Likewise, training naturally also makes you stronger and helps you especially when facing the highest tier foes.
If you really get into the game there is the endless mode, in which you just fight opponent after opponent without healing or upgrades until you inevitably drop, trying to last as long as possible. You can then track your score on global leaderboards and compete for the highest place.
Having only 12 opponents, the game is unfortunately quite short: myself, I finished it (all achievements) in 4 hours and having played through New Game++: the career mode can be start anew with the previous upgrades but stronger opponents. Still, this can only last so far.
For longevity it would need more opponents, a longer career mode and more distinct difficulties (frankly I saw little difference between normal and hard). Perhaps playing different characters or having multiplayer would be cool as well. Here's for hoping there will be a sequel that addresses at least some of these issues.
For the glorious full price of 5 bucks though the price is still good, and on sale it's even better! For the short time it lasted for me it was a blast, an excellent choice for killing a few hours for fun.

KOTOR 2 is my all-time favorite Star Wars game and in my top 5 for RPGs.
Positives-
*Very dark atmosphere and storyline. I think its a lot better than the first one's story
*The climax of the game is really good. The writing in general is very solid. Not going to spoil the climax, but I love how they played with the KOTOR's combat mechanics and fit it into the story.
*One of the best soundtracks in a Star Wars-related product and in a video game in general.
*Very good variety of weapons and customization options, though sometimes can get a little overwhelming.
*Kreia is one of the best characters in a Star Wars game. She's like a Yoda if he wasn't a devout follower of the Jedi Code and plays a huge part in the story. Atton Rand is a really solid character as well. Canderous, HK-47, and T3-M4 also make a return, all of which pleases me.
*The ability to teach the Jedi ways to some of your followers is a neat addition to the game.
Negatives-
*Without the Complete Overhaul Mod, the game feels incomplete. There's still a good amount of content otherwise but be sure to get the mod.
*The final boss fight is kind of a let down
*The ending of the game is a real let down
*Still buggy, though they have fixed quite a bit of them during the July patch.
*The companions I mentioned above are really good, but unfortunately, the rest are pretty dull. The first KOTOR had a much better cast in my opinion.
*Special combat techniques in the game are a cool idea, but it does not execute well in practice. If you like them, then good on ya! I'm not a fan personally.
*Graphically its not a very pretty game, but its not distracting either.
Overall, this game is worth buying if your a Star Wars fan or a RPG fan.

I remember pre-ordering the original Gabriel Knight 20 years ago or more.  I loved it and this remake is absolutely great.  It's not perfect, but it's definitely worthwhile to play either for nostalgic purposes or if this is your first time.  Gabriel Knight is investigating voodoo murders occurring in New Orleans with his friend Moseley who works for the police.  Gabriel is working on a book about the occult.  However, it turns out that the occult is much more real than he had imagined.  You follow Gabriel, Moseley, and many other wonderful characters from New Orleans to other places around the world.  The story is top notch and still holds very well in today's world of entertainment.
Here's what I didn't like about it.  It is an EXACT replica of the original, but with enhanced sound, graphics, and new voices (which some will gripe about).  This means that the very ridiculously tough puzzles such as knowing exactly what to play on the rada drums at the end of the game still persist.  I wish they had remastered it, but with enhancements to the issues it had.  There are many graphical glitches, though not too serious.  Overall, a wonderful experience though.  Proves that adventure gaming is definitely not dead, it just needs a great storyline to go along with the rest of the game to make it in today's market.

If you're new to Magic the Gathering or simply you want to play some duel, this is the game you want to buy. I think this is the perfect digital introduction to Magic. The thing you have to really mind is the choice of your starting deck just before the last tutorial duel. Yes, one deck and that's all. You will unlock cards and eventually other decks, but you will start with one so be really carefull. Maybe you can read the basic strategy of all starting deck and choose the one that fits you.
All in all, I think that this is the best implementation of Magic the gathering for a casual player like I am. The game is packed with fun and it's not so hard to beat. It has a sense of progression and strategy building all for few bucks. If you are a more serious player maybe you can try Magic online. I'm sure Wizards of the Coast will welcome you there.

This game is a mixed bag of funny parts and some crappy game design ideas.
Instead of pros and cons let's take a look what's fun and what's crappy.
Fun:
- weapons are fun
- enemy design is also fun
- ego boost mechanism - it's always fun to have some minor advantage by finding some secrets
- vehicles
- humor in the DLC
- shooting aliens
- 4 weapons option
- The Doctor Who Cloned Me DLC is probably better than the whole DNF vanilla game
Not funny:
- turd jokes can be fun but not when encountered en masse. Overall the humor in the baseline game as well as in the DLC can be really crude and primitive sometimes
- 2 weapons option - really, in a modern shooter? What were they thinking! (line borrowed from AVGN)
- level design - in some levels you must go from point A to point B and it takes about forever
- not that much shooting in a shooter game, I would rather call it a walking/running with a gun and pressing buttons simulator
- vehicles when you need to spend there too much time (like in this canyon level or moon level from DLC)
- boss fights are scripted and somewhat disappointing
- no bots in multiplayer - and you bet that servers are pretty much empty now
To be honest - I've had a great time playing DNF some time ago (about a year or two after release) and I've got a great time playing this fun DLC - The Doctor Who Cloned Me not that long ago. I would rather not play single player campaign again. Not that it's not fun because it is fun but because those not funny elements are dominating over funny ones - large levels where you need to run from point to point and shoot about three enemies in the meantime or some puzzles that you need to solve in order to proceed forward.
In conclusion, this is a shooter game with a moderate amount of shooting. Well, I call it a Duke Nukem Adventure Game rather than a shooter game. Those shooting scenes can get pretty intense, but after that there is a prolonged scene where you need to walk here and there and not much is going on.
I give this game thumbs up, for the fond memories of it. If you've never played it then go on, it's not that bad. Definitely try the DLC The Doctor Who Cloned Me. It's short and it's fun. It's what's good in DNF without boring parts.

I played Amnesia: The Dark Descent a fair bit after most of the initial spoophype had died down, but I can't say I was disappointed. Not nearly as scared as some may have been, but I absolutely enjoyed almost every minute.
When it comes to establishing and enforcing a constant sense of dread, The Dark Descent is spot-on. Frictional clearly came a long way from their Penumbra days in this respect with Amnesia, and I must say, I'm glad for it. Keeping opposition to very few creatures that were very effective at ending your chances of survival was a good call, and when you first start running into them, they're absolutely terrifying. However, spend enough time going deeper and deeper, and you'll find easy enough ways around most of them to make their presence much less threatening. Except for that one wet bit. I still have flashbacks to that.
The story does most of the work instilling fear rather than any critter, as it's drip-fed through a series of letters and monologues that barely tell you anything individually. These tidbits are just enough to keep your mind whirring in regards to why you're where you are and what's going on, which is something you have to keep in check for the more evasion-intensive bits lest you walk right into one of your new friends. Gameplay aside from stealth consists primarily of puzzles, all of which aren't too taxing in regards to coming up with the solutions but require enough legwork and the occasional interruption to keep things interesting.
Another benefit the game has going for it is its openness to expanded content. There are plenty of new stories and levels to give a try once you've finished the main game, which is nice for replay value.
Seeing as how this game is starting to get up there in the years, it's on sale often enough that not adding it to your collection, if you're a horror fan, would probably be considered criminal. Give it a try, play it with headphones, and turn the lights out when you do.

I really, really, really wanted to like this game. It is right up my alley and I thought it would be a blast. Unfortunately not.  There is no joy in building an economic engine or a profitable company. There is no satisfaction in making good strategies. There is no logic in the buy-out end-game.
There will be games in which you are hit three four times a minute by sabotage. Every company will attack you and you can't execute a strategy for the spam.
There will be games in which you are the strongest company and suddenly find yourself bought out by a company worth half of your value. And I mean sudden. One moment you are thinking "wow, I am actually generating a profitable company here and then WHAM! Game over!.
It's a total WTF moment because there is no clue it's coming.
In Railroad Tycoon you could buy up your shares to keep from getting taken over.
Not in this game.
It's simply not fun.
It could be, and should be. But I think the developers have gone down the path of playing so many games with each other that they see the fun in it, but forgot that the fun they are having is only because they know each other and designed the game themselves. I'm sure if I played several hundred hours I would start to get into the nuances of play. But why spend that much time on something that isn't enjoyable just to get to where it might be enjoyable?
This is a real shame and the first time in a long time I really feel my money was wasted on a steam purchase.
