Now then, What is Ubermosh? Well, it's a fun little game where you're placed in a desert with nothing but a sword to kill people. Your first kill gives you a gun, if you remember to pick it up. You'll work your way up to the best gun in the game, a quad-shot red gun that I personally feel looks like the Lancer from the Gears Of War Franchise.
You'll probably die alot, but that's okay, the gameplay is so simplistic and fun, that you're always coming back for more!
The main idea of the game is to survive as long as you can, and beat your highscore, but as of update 13, There are now some bonus objectives to complete, such as survive 7 rounds, or get 150 kills with a certain playstyle, adding to the fun.
The music is so kick♥♥♥♥♥and awesome, making the rounds super fun to play, that it's surprising to know it was all done by one guy.
There's only a handful of enemies, but that doesn't really matter, since they all do the same thing. The only differences being, the gun they hold, and the blood they spill on the ground. Sadly, this also means there's not a big variety in guns.
You can currently choose between two different modes, Easy, and Hardboiled.
Easy is, well, easy, not much to say about it.
Hardboiled, well, that's where it really gets fun and difficult! Edit: Originally, I had beleived Hardboiled mode to be a bit TOO difficult, as a result of removing Full-Auto, but after playing a little more, I realize, it's perfect the way it is. It becomes a fun, callenging, and true fight for survival in Hardboiled mode, and after going a few rounds in easy, I encourage you to take it up a notch!
Update: You can now choose between different playstyles, called Class Mods. Kensai, Gunner, Wizard, or Normal.
Kensai: Melee only,Not too impressive, but a good idea. Originally I'd assumed it to be too easy, but after being forced to play it consistantly, I've realized, it takes skill to get anywhere in this mode. Originally, I said you could just stand there and wait for the bullets, well, that's not entirely true. You could, but you'd get killed. Enemies have the tendancy to fire their guns only when they're near you, whether you let them get close to you, or you walk close to them, the bullets will fire, and you'll need skill and quick reflexes to survive longer than a few seconds.
Gunner: Of the three new playstyles, Gunner is by far the best. Full auto gives you the opportunity to attack nonstop, and cause absolute mayhem,But only with a gun. You have no sword to deflect bullets. You're given 3 HP, and a gun to start you off with. Without the ability to deflect oncoming bullets, survival is made much more difficult, as any bullet that escaes your sight, can cost you.
Warlock: Warlock serves as a companion to Hardboiled mode, as It gives you only 2 HP, But it starts you off with the best gun, and gives you use of the blade. I suppose the point is to offer a balance between surviving, and scoring, but I feel it's a bit bland.
As it stands, there's not much else I can say about the game, and I do feel it could be something more. At the same time,I think it's a complete experience, that will provide you with hours of fun.
The Pros ,the cons, and Inbetweens
Pros
-Awesome music
-Simple, yet difficult gameplay which provides an addicting experience.
-Two modes (Possibly more to come)
-4 unique playstyle options that each add a different level of difficulty
Inbetween
- The only real objective is to beat your high-score.
-You'll die, alot, and I really mean that.
Cons
-Not many enemies to fight, means not many guns.
Keep in mind, this game is made by a one man team, so some features may not make it in.
For what it is, I give it a good score of 8.9/10, and I HIGHLY recommend it.
Here's hoping this game will become your new addiction!

Your main goal is to collect resources, watch the stock market, and plan out your life of business on Mars, ultimately outsmarting your opponents and taking control of their base. The game looks pretty good overall and presents a refreshing taste on the genre. But because it is in Early Access, it isn't perfect. It may be a bit pricy right now, and the fact that the tutorial isn't actually a tutorial, and that there isn't a great amount of content to the game at the moment, but the developers, as far as I know, are putting their hearts into this game, and i'm anxious to see what this game has in store for the future. At it's core, Ubermosh is one of the best retro shooters out there. It keeps gameplay a simple matter of beating your high score in a 16 bit arena full of respawning goons, like a super-basic isometric-ish Unreal Tournament. There are 4 different weapons to choose from, and a melee weapon that can reflect bullets back at enemies, which (aside from melee which you start with) you get by killing off aforementioned goons, and the game objective is as simple as this: Kill as many opponents in the 90 second time limit as possible while not getting killed yourself.
It's a staggeringly simple concept that for the most part is excellently implemented. Right now, there is only very barebones content, but the game price is reflecting this, and where many games have tons of content but are seriously lacking in enjoyment, Ubermosh is great fun to play and easy to lose hours playing due to it's dip in/dip out gameplay.
That said, the only dark cloud on this game is that it's early access and developer Walter (it's a one man game team) isn't quite happy with the brass tacks of the gameplay mechanic yet. As such, minor but significant changes are happening within the game all the time (I've had the game about a month max and it's been radically overhauled 10 times already, each time significantly changing the play style required) and right now, each update is resetting your score, which for a game that is purely score-attack and score-attack only can be disheartening and frustrating.
If you want to support a hard-working solo developer intent on making a well-balanced arcade throwback, and play a game that isn't finished yet but already has piles of one-more-go addictive gameplay, then buy it now.
If you feel having said game continuously morph overnight into different adaptations of said gameplay, or indeed losing your progress each time it morphs is going to upset you in anyway, I would advise you to wait til Ubermosh comes out of Early Access, because Walter is still very much actively working on it, and as such sometimes it has features added for as little as 4 hours until he decides actually they weren't a good idea. Which if he's reading is absolutely fine, that's development xD. But be aware that the game is being built in front of us.

[EARLY ACCESS REVIEW]
Do you feel as if the pit fights at The Pitt in Fallout 3 wasn't tense? Alittle bit too easy?
Do you want a Hotline Miami-eque game set out in a desert where the only trusty weapons are a neon orange cyber sabre  that cuts bullets and random guns?
Meet this lil' gem: UBERMOSH.
UBERMOSH must've been the best Early Access game I've bought and enjoyed for a long time.
The cyberpunk arcade at it's current state may be small, but surprisingly, it's hella addictive.
The consept is simple: You're a Samus Aran 2.0 stuck in a Kerrigan betrayal situation where a load of alien beasts with blasters storming at you. The goal? Survive by cutting and shooting, and a 5 slot chance counter before it's game over.
I will adress a few pros and cons, though:
+ Features a fast paced gameplay with a neat control balance and trigger response.
+ Brings a upbeat punk soundtrack that makes the expirience much larger.
+ A unique type of arcade in a mosh pit where you either kill or get killed by aliens equipped with a multitude of guns.
+ Perfect for a quick play during the day and can make you return just to beat the high score.
+ Morgan Freeman
+ Self customized skins for each ranked reached.
+ Gives the option to play with different class mods such as Warlock, Kensai and Gunner, holding different playstyles for each one.
~ Alien spawning comes at a really short intervals, making the player more aware around the enviorment. Problem here is that the cursor play a large role when it comes to scouting out the area, and can cause the player to be vulnerable.

- Endless ammunition. There could've been a limited capacity before the gun is deemed unusable.
- Guns laying spread across the player area, making it abit of an issue when using one gun and suddenly it's auto-swapped.
- The swap time between the cyber sabre and the gun doesn't go faster or slow enough to make either a speedy gameplay with both slicing and dicing plus gunning or the player naked enough out in the battlefield for the enemy to shoot you.
- The game tend to lose saved data, nulling out the rank and kill counter, resetting the whole thing back. Don't know if this is intentional or if that only happens if no internet connection. Regardless, it's abit sad, but it can work as a motivator for some hardcores. (UPDATE 14th of August: This has not occured in the latest updates so I believe the score deletion issue is fixed.)
What I wish from this game in the future:
* An options menu for resolution, volume/sfx adjustment, and fullscreen/miniscreen option.
* Maybe online co-op.
* For Extras: A retro 80s arcade window mode.
* An option to play with controller. (Partial controller support added as of the 0010 update)
* Possible additions of ingame/Steam achievements. Not utmost important. (Achievements added and class modifications added as of update 0.12-14)
Overall, the whole game in it's current state (as of 5th of May, 2015), it is really well made, and a absolute bargain with the price tag it's on now.
Would recommend to those who seek out something fresh, loves cyberpunk, retro games (Metroid like), and a game to kill time with a short session of good action.

If you enjoy being one shotted by everyone with a 9mm pistol, then have fun wasting your money! This game is just like infestation in every aspect (other than setting and monsters of course). The combat consists of fighting teleporting zombie aliens that do varying and sometimes unfair damage. Players typically sit in bushes in back areas of the map literally just waiting, for hours on end to get that one kill. So if you're into pvp that consists of crouching in a bush for hours on end, this game might be for you, but if you intend on being a scavenger who searches building to building for that precious loot, be prepared to be inevitably shot down by the guy with the smores, who apparently was disguised as that bush all along. This game has a long way to go before I can give it more credit than the abomination known as Infestation: Survivor Stories. Granted this game's combat with the AI is much more pleasurable than that of ISS.
Pros: Good AI combat system (smooth); global storage so you can stockpile the unretrievable loot; when you do kill a player, you feel on top of the world; protection system when leaving safe zones; party (group) system to locate friends on map; various events.
Cons: Poor aiming with guns (who swings their gun from side to side when aiming??);high camper population (especially outside of safe zones); difficult enemies when melee fighting; scarce loot (other than crunchy bens).
>4/10: Regret my purchase.

If I had one complaint about this game, it would only be that it's too short. However I'll also say that the Continue+ mode, Endless mode and several difficulty levels mitigates this as well as it can.
I usually judge a game based on 5 criteria, listed in order of important: Gameplay, Controls, Replayability, Sound & Graphics.
Gameplay: As many people before me have said this is definitely an homage to Punch Out from the slew of eccentric and quirky characters to the first person boxing mode. The gameplay though is very tight. The AI doesn't feel like it cheats, there's no psuedo difficulty or anything of that nature. The AI learns from your patterns and which attacks you're using most and will guard against it in the current and next round, forcing players to avoid a specific pattern or style of play.
Controls: You can rock the keyboard or you can rock a gamepad, fully customizable and absolutely no complaints here. Controls are such an important part of a game, they can make a game or break it and while you might think it's standard practice to allow customizable controls, it's the few games that don't that stand out like a sore thumb. Thankfully this game isn't one of them.
Replayability: As long as you're in the mood for the game, there's content there to play. From exhibition missions to completing/replaying the story, or trying your hand at endless mode. The only thing I can foresee ruining this is becoming bored with the game itself which will happen, as with most games, eventually.
Sound: The sound effects are definitely on point and the music is about what you'd expect: standard background music that you actually hear for a few minutes and then start tuning out after that.
Graphics: The graphics for this game are great. They're not super polished high end but for what they are they look awesome and I had a ball seeing new characters and the blending of art for story and 3d in the ring.
Overall on a scale of 0-10, I'd give this game an 8.

The other day I had the inclination to hit something. Bouncing around the house with a lot of energy makes me want to expel it in different ways. I'm not a boxer myself but thinking about it made me remember this game and I'm glad I did.
Beast Boxing Turbo is a fun little fighting game. There aren't many boxing games out there but this is one of the good ones. Your character's story is that she wants to participate in the Beast Boxing fight circuit but since humans aren't allowed you're fighting incognito. Your goal at first is just to prove you're as good as any beast as you just want to be accepted but of course you turn out to have mad boxing skills then get the idea that you can actually be the best. A rags to Rocky story if you will.
Controls are tight and even though you can get by with pretty much just jabs you face an good variety of fighters that have their own unique moves and fighting styles. You fight in a first person view reminiscent of Super Punchout, if you're old enough to remember that. You can also buy equipment and train to increase your skills. I play this with a gamepad and the controls feel natural and responsive.
If there was one area I feel that this game falls a bit shot in is that I would have enjoyed if the training exercises included a short mini-game of some sort so it adds a bit of play time and variation to just straight boxing matches. Another thing I feel that could have been a bit of an improvement was if there was some need to use other punches besides the jab. You can do uppercuts and hooks. Even though those punches are more effective when they do hit they tend to be slower and easily dodged by the majority of the opponents you face.
Other than that this game is fun to play albeit is pretty short. One playthrough will take you about 90 minutes. There's no grinding involved. The story is peppered with humor and the characters you face have a surprising bit of personality as well. Overall it's a really good boxing game.

This is the world of Beast Boxing, where newcomer and secret human Char must train herself to win against a dozen other fearsome monsters, including:
,

. The game is short, lasting about 2 to 4 hours worth of gameplay, depending on how much you grind or repeat levels. Likewise, the game only has a dozen stages/opponents, which are reused for the game's endless mode. However, this is reasonable considering the game's base price of CDN$5.49
Plus, if you consider the gameplay, then this game is well worth the price! Every match in this game is a punchy
fast-paced slugfest where quick reflexes and thoughtful movements are necessary for an assured victory. The sensation of jabbing and strafing, seeking the right moment to unleash a flurry of fists, keeps every fight exciting. This game is an appreciative nod to Nintendo's Punch-Out, and if you need quick sessions of boxing action to fill in the smaller gaps in your schedule, this game is an ideal contender. I give this two boxing gloves up, and eagerly await the starting bell for this game's sequel!

I've never played the original gabriel knight games, so I'm new into the storyline, but I gotta say, if you're a story driven gamer Like me, you should give this one a go.
Basically, Play it for the marvelous story, the gameplay is good, not great, but  if the graphics are an important factor in your gaming experience.... steer clear of it.
First the good:
The Story is interesting and develops at a nice rate, and draws you in with every chapter - or day - you play through.
You follow gabriel Knight, a writer that investigates a series of murders with voodoo roots in New orleans in 1993 with the police department for his supposed best seller, and then the story grows deeper.
I found it quite charming that they didnt try and modernize it, quite refreshing.
The voice acting is quite good, and the scripts are witty and enjoyable. 10/10 in this part.
Now... the bad:
being this a point and click you wont expect QTEs or car chases, or fighting segments, But the characters could move in a really disturbingly clunky way. You need gabriel to go to on side of a room to get... a pair of scissors. he will crawl there, take the scissors, say something and then, there's a pause.
Its a couple of seconds in which the character stays still, you cant control it, or order any actions and you just have to wait for it to pass. Its as if you took the scissors, and then needed to look at them and think "oh these are scissors, Scissors cut stuff. NOW i can move on". This was a recurring thing and it broke down the flow of the game more often than it should.
Another thing, that really disappointed me, was the appearance.
It was a bit all over the place. I'm not obsessed with graphics, but its a bit of an eyesore that You're playing a remaster issued somewhere between 2013/14 and the models seem to be out of the sims 1, with clunky animations and odd textures. This by itself isn't bad, but you have beautifully painted backgrounds and lovely cutscenes in a painting like style. THEN you had another style of art in the same game, when you interacted with NPCs. Two drawn portraits would appear over the game with facial animations that sometimes cutted down the drawing on the lip or brow area and that had Nothing to do with the cutscenes Nor the game models.
I would love love love to see it in some sort of animated style like... I don't know, any of the daedalic games, consistent and according to the marvelous story.

I highly recommend this game!
Gabriel Knight: Sins of the father, a classic point and click adventure that was once Game of the year in 1994. The expectations for the remake were therefore big. Did it succeed in achieving glory this time too? In my opinion yes. :)
Graphics don't make a game. We experienced gamers have had ample proof of that. So what is it, that this Gabriel Knight remake has which makes it so special? Charisma! And more importantly, a very good and well written story, that hasn’t lost the magic even after 20 years!
What did I like?
+ The story
+ The characters
+ The world
+ The point & click
+ The humor
+ The voice acting
+ The puzzles
What did I dislike?
- The blood
- The mutilated animals
- The difficulty of some puzzles
- The short length
- The linear story
If you haven't played the original game, or any of the Gabriel Knight series (perhaps because you were too young...) you’ll find in this modern version the right mix of adventure, action, plot, interesting characters, and pretty looking pictures that might just make you fall in love (again) with point & click games. Don’t forget the horror, violence, blood, murder, snakes and mutilated bodies of people and animal alike.
Yes, Gabriel Knight is not for the kiddies, that much is sure. Please also keep in mind that the main subject of the game is voodoo. If this is a theme that makes you uncomfortable or that you simply don’t like, look elsewhere for your adventure. ^^
First thing that strikes me in the game, after the ‘fiery’ introduction, is the southern accent, yes you heard right. That drawl *giggles* NCIS New Orleans for the Win! :D
Apparently it is particularly effective on the ladies lol but I must say Gabriel’s male charm leaves me quite unmoved. But I guess it’s one of the reasons I like him, he makes me laugh :) that and his ‘relationship’ with Grace Nakimura!
If you ever wanted to know about New Orleans (insert the proper accent here) this is the game for you! I loved getting to know so much history and culture about it, even if only through a specific angle. :D For that alone this is an unique game. ^^
The game focuses of course on the resolution of puzzles and a LOT of talking to NPCs. Both present their challenges. The puzzles can’t be simple nor too easy and thankfully aren’t, even if  the game is logical in how to get from A to B, however, it won’t provide any help on how to do so, it makes certain tasks rather frustrating at times.
The game system will, however, give you hints on all pertinent things to do as well as force you to stay on the same day until you have accomplished them.
If you are in the habit of playing mystery or detective games or even just RPG games you’ll find that the story isn’t exactly challenging, it’s not full of twists and surprises, but the trip will still be worth it, at least it was in my book. :)
I guess this game just touched a nostalgic chord in me, which accounts for my good opinion of it and made me want to play all Gabriel Knight games again. :P (which I shall hopefully be doing).
All things said, this game is worth trying or replaying! :) If only to help make possible other remakes of this successful series :D If Gabriel Knight can’t charm you then you must be cold blooded like a snake. Get it? :P No? Play the game please. XD
Please keep in mind this is only my personal opinion.
Kind regards,
Keiyan

Its not often I come across a game which is a totally new genre but I think Offworld fits the bill.
Offworld is a strange hybrid of 4X and RTS but without the combat, however that description alone does not come close.
Matches are generally short (30 min) and start off with a similar feel to 4X games, you explore expand and start to exploit the landscape, but you need keep moving, resting on your laurels will get you left behind by the AI, time is the unlisted resource in this game.
Each game is a struggle for economic dominance with the winner buying out the shares of the opposing companies, now this may sound a little dry, but the fun comes with
you achieve this.
There are many ways of getting the upper hand in Offworld, with strategies ranging from predicting trends, to dominating resources, outpacing others with research and new techs, managing your debt, or using a miriad of black market options.

The technical quality of this game is very good, it works better than some "finished" games, no crashes, everything works smoothly and looks great.
Content wise I may like a few more victory conditions or changes to the current ones, other than that just needs some more tooltips and tutorials.
The campaign mode offers a small meta game involving highering engineers and expanding colonies, it also has some new victory conditions, and can been played with a variety of different colony "managers".
Matches end too abruptly for my likeing, and I usually find it disapionting when they do... but this hasn't stopped diving right back in to new matches to try out new strategies.
A few tweaks to the victory mechanics should help a lot here, maybe adding multiple victory conditions, and or making current ones more obvious and exciting.
I've not completed the campiagn or tried multiplayer yet, so I'll update things when I do.
This is a different type of RTS, centred around economy rather than battles, but still very satisfying, forethought and timing are a must, a very enjoyable game.

You should get hold of a copy of the original (you can get it here on Steam as well) since it has a truly great voice cast with Tim Curry as Gabriel, Mark Hamill as his friend Moseley, Efraim Zimbalist Jr. as Wolfgang Ritter, Micheal Dorn as Dr. John, Virginia Capers (AKA grandma Huxtable) as the narrator and Leah Remini as Grace Nakimura. Even the voice cast of some of the minor characters is worth mentioning (like Jim Cummings). The new voice cast is okay, but nowhere near the level of that of the original game.
- Many glitched animations.
On several occasions I've seen Gabriels upper torso or head spinning around in a way that reminded me of the Exorcist. At several occasions seated characters are suddenly (partly) standing up before continuing their conversation. The butler of Malia Gedde can be seen briefly standing before the door each time he has closed it. And at one time I was looking out of the window in Mosely's office and clicked on the door to leave the room. Only to see Gabriel standing up from an invisible chair (without sitting down first), moon-walking to the door and spinning once round his axis before leaving the room. It never interfered with the game but these glitches should've been removed before release.
- Musicians in the park
Another thing that bothered me were the guys playing the banjo and electric guitar in the park. Neither of them is using a shoulder strap. I know from experience it's impossible to play either a classic guitar or a electric guitar while standing up without one and I think it's safe to assume that's also true for playing a banjo. Even worse the electric guitar IS NOT PLUGGED INTO AN AMPLIFIER!. An electric guitar that's not plugged in will make less noise than one of those cheap plastic kid guitars. Someone should have noticed this and replaced it with an acoustic guitar.
It's worth buying, especially when it's on sale. But it's got some issues that I think you should be aware of. And it's not a worthy replacement of the original since the original voice cast isn't reused.

I got this game a long time ago after watching two youtubers play it around Christmas of that year. I didn't play it until many years later with a group of friends for a Halloween event. It was the best horror game experiance of my life. The game does not have many jump scares, not many intended jump scares at least. Its entirely atmosphereic, witch leaves a lasting affect on you. For a few days after playing this game I found a problem with walking around my own house at night, and opening doors into dark rooms. Granted im quite weak when it comes to horror games so this may be the reason but the fact a video game could leave such an lasting affect on me is amazing. I could play or watch a Five Nights at Freddy's and be scared out of my mind, but the a few moments after quitting the game i'd be fine. But Amnesia... I would play this game and be just as scared but for the entire experiance and then close the game and still be just as paranoid and fearful. Now lets jump into the game itself. The game mechanics are nice, not much to complain about. Maybe a bit clunky when it comes to picking up and moving objects but it was no problem for me and shouldn't cause any problems for you. The lighting is very very dark, even the lite up areas are dark buts thats intended, this game wants you to be afraid of the dark. Another review I saw a long time ago put it perfectly "Their's Dark, and then their's Darker in this game". The lights you do get are going to be your best friend. When you open a chest and see a thing of oil you will shed tears of joy. If you do use your oil correctly and only when you have too it isn't a problem, but if you waste your lantern for little reason you will find darkness. As for the story I found it to be immursive. There will be no plot point spoilers besides the obvious point you find out soon(its in the title). The character you play(Daniel) as wakes up and has Amnesia. As you progress through the game you discover Daniel's backstory and so does your Daniel, witch is a nice touch. So many games have it so you find out the characters backstory witch of corse the character already knows and it sometimes makes for weird story development. As for combat, there is none. You find a monster you need to hide and pray he dosen't find you or that you can out run him and lose him. This is good because so many horror games give you weapons that you can use to kill things witch takes away a aspect of horror in the game. A horror game that makes me feel helpless is much more scarier than games with scary looking monsters that I can kill. Another thing about this game was, it pushed you forward and gave you direction as to where to go and what to do but it didn't put you on tracks.
I give this game a 10/10 and I feel like game developers should look at this game and take notes on how to make a good atmospheric horror game.

... when it decides it wants to work.
And for what it costs, I don't think it's worth the risk that it won't work.
Let me elaborate.
The gameplay is that of the Magic card game, so if you like the game, you'll enjoy this game. If you're used to the Magic PC games by now, none of this will be too odd or out of place. It plays like it should.

Recommendation - Pass with the might of a thousand passes
The words I want to use when describing this game are unsuitable for children, the elderly, the pregnant, those with a heart condition, and people with sensitive ears.
I have not raged this hard at a game since I was a kid, playing the arena mode of Armored Core. If it were not for me having already unlocked the multiplayer, my desk would be split in half and pieces of my mouse would be embedded in the drywall for how hard I would have smashed the "delete local content" button.
The reason for my rage is the single player campaign. Put simply, it is god-awful. It is terrible. It is horrifically unfair and completely stupid. You will have the bone-stock vanilla uber-generic weak deck up against ridiculously powerful enemies. You will lose and lose and lose and lose unless you just happen to start with a great hand AND your opponent simultaneously gets a bad one.
Let me know if the following scenario sounds fun: You go to the local game shop where Magic players gather, you buy a $10 starter deck, and then sit down to battle a pro-level player who has a masterfully-built multicolored deck filled with holographic, prismatic, epically-rare legendary creatures.
Sound fun? NO!?? Well, gasp and shock! OH, UNKNOWABLE UNIVERSE! I would have to take off my shoes to count how many things I would rather do than slog through that garbage. I'm honestly having more fun typing up this review than I did playing that stupid campaign.
You might be thinking "well just play multiplayer!" and you're right, to a point. The multiplayer can certainly be fun (assuming you're against a player with a similarly-terrible deck), but unfortunately, YOU HAVE TO PLAY THE CAMPAIGN TO UNLOCK MULTIPLAYER!!! 4 tough battles, one of whom is a boss.
Magic is a multiplayer game. Magic has ALWAYS been a multiplayer game. The card game version has never been anything BUT a multiplayer game. Before the elctronic version, it was literally impossible to NOT play with other people. So kudos to the devs for locking the main feature that the game was built around and that 99% of all players want behind hours and hours of campaign-fueled frustration and nonsense.
The multiplayer is fun, but the rest of the game is terrible. There are SO many other card games to play with friends (many of them free) that unless you can pick this game up for a couple bucks or you have a superhuman amount of patience, don't even make direct eye-contact with it.

It is like if your favourite porn sequel tried to have a story and special effects.
To begin with, I am not a Duke Nukem super fan. I did play Duke Nukem 3D a long time ago and completed about one episode of it and few levels of other episodes. I do love classic FPS games such as the original Doom, Heretic, Hexen,Star Wars Dark Forces and Blood.
The only good thing I found about Duke Nukem Forever is some of the complexity in level designs, especially the parts when Duke becomes tiny and everything around you is huge.
The rest of the game is either average or bad.
Graphics and animations feels very rushed like the game did not take its time (apperantly 12 years aren't enough). You can easily spot bad textures and you can notice how some 3d objects in the map have poor details. Animations for monsters are about as average and Duke's animations are horrible. Never in my life saw poor execution of QTE (Which is totally unnecessary in an FPS Game!).
Story is very uninspired and has no plot. This detail can be overlooked but just like a bad porno, the game can't stop shoving flat uninteresting character to your face. The dialoug is very corny and horribly acted. Even Duke's voice acting makes me feel like the voice actor is uninterested or "disconnected" from the game. I wouldn't be surprised if he voiced his lines over the phone.
Gameplay as mentioned above, can get interesting with how complex you travel inside the level. Some shining moments were such as trying to get an item from a locked room by controling a remote car. However, the levels feels very unlively especially in the later part of the game. For example, interactivity with items is surprisingly limited beyond the first chapter (the casino and the strip club). Most of the environment is not affected by physics and most NPCs don't even feature lines to talk to you.
The game's asset is also extremely repetitive. It feels like every place in Duke's world owns barrels and wooden boxes. This is very surprising considering that 3D realm made games like Max Payne which had far much assets. Monsters types are extremely limited. Weapons are few and some of them are unnecessary such as Shrink Ray and the Freezing Ray.
Finally, the most annoying and straight up bad design decision in this game is: Horde battles. You will find yourself mostly entering vast area, only to be locked in to face a horde of enemeies and a mini boss. It is very uninspiring and unfitting for this game.
In the end, this has been a very disappointing experience. I did knew the game scored bad but I kept myself open-minded as much as possible but after the horrible distastful ending, I couldn't. The level design concept could have been in a lot better game with another studio such as Valve or id softwares. Save your money and another game.

The premise of Dead Pixels is simple. Your pixel hero runs across the screen killing zombies until he clears all the screens. Graphics and Sound are basic but fit the games style as a homage to the 8/16-bit eras. It's also full of of great references, mostly to Resident Evil but there a few other horror references tucked away (such as Ash's boomstick from Evil Dead).
In between all the zombie shooting and side scrolling there is the opportunity to visit shops (With bizzarely calm shop keepers in them. There are hundreds of zombies outside guys, runaway!) In these shops you can upgrade abilities, weapons or ammunition. This does add some much needed depth and replay value to the game as it lets you change the way you play.
In my case I stocked up on med packs, upgraded my health and speed and killed zombies only when necessarily. When I first started I was trying to kill everything but I soon realised what a drain on ammo this was! Judging from other playthroughs I've seen other people didn't let that put them off, buying loads of weapons and ammo and upgrading their combat abilities in order to massacre hundreds of zombies.
Definitely worth a buy considering its regularly available for about the price of a Freddo, and you're guaranteed at least 20 minutes more fun out of Dead Pixels.

Tl;dr at the bottom
When I put "Yes" on this review, it was because I wish that there was a sort of middle area between yes and no for reviews, like a "maybe" or "depends" option. It's a great game for playing with physics, but not so great for actually driving the cars. Ovbiously, this is because of the fact that left and right keys can't determine how much you really want to turn the car, so you often find yourself swerving off of the road just trying to turn left, when you were driving about 9 mph. You can also use your mouse to turn the car, which sounds helpful at first, but is pretty much the same as the keys. I even tried to take it down a notch with the sensitivity on the mouse, but I still got the same result. Now, if you want this game for destroying the cars, buy it, because its worth the money on that part. The physics engine for this game is stunning, BeamNG very evidently put a lot of work into it. Watch the video on it's store page to see how great it is.
Tl;dr: Buy it if you want to see cars get demolished, but don't if you want to go on a joy ride.
(Also, if anyone knows if there is an easier way to drive the cars, please tell me, because I'm at a loss here. It was what I primarily wanted the game for.)

SOMA is a step in a fantastic direction for Frictional Games. Since Amnesia, the games may have lost some of their fear inducing monsters and scream causing enviroments, but it is a rivetting story and a maddening emotional ride from start to finish. The voice acting is A+, delivering as much immersion as possible. The enviroment is meticulously crafted and jaw dropping, a truly believable sci-fi world beneath the sea. The plot is top notch, as Frictional's story writers deliver one of the greatest and thought-provoking science fiction tale I've ever seen in any media. My one true gripe is that it feels as if the 'monsters' that Frictional tries to cram into their games detracts from the story a bit, ocassionally forcing you to skip through levels faster than you would normally. I would have preferred only scripted monster moments for plot reasons, rather than tedious monster dodging through narrow halls. It became less a scare and more a nuisance. What made Amnesia great was the fear, but what makes Soma great is the story. Frictional games proves with Soma that they could easily deliver the greatest written atmospherical games on the market without relying on scares, and still sell.
Regardless, I give Soma the prestigious 10/10 for a near perfect horror game, and a perfect as hell sci-fi story that will stick with you forever, and will make you forever question our existance.

First: I'd verify what most people say about the graphics and shooting mechs - they're nice and they work well enough.
Second. here's how I feel about the overall design of the game:
I'd like my money back at this point. I enjoyed this game for about three hours. I think I was getting lucky. I WAS also very excited about the prospect of completing missions in a survival game. Here are some things that ruined the game after the initial glow wore off.
1. Big missions seem more or less impossible to beat in games with random marauders running around.
2. Courier missions (sounds fun, right?) End with PCs camping the goal zone. So you run for ~ 15 minutes and get shot.
3. Camping PCs have crazy/scary equipment that they bought with real money. F@#$ off. Get the F@#$ out of here. Unnacceptable.
4. Stuff spawns into the world randomly and without logical placement. I realize this is a genre standard - but it is a pathetic genre standard.
5. The world is too small for the style of gameplay. I saw the whole thing.
6. The buildings are SO similar that they may as well be proceduraly generated - which would massively improve this game BTW.
7. Here's an important one that nobody seems to mention - the Nether (monsters) TELEPORT and are UNESCAPABLE. I understand that this may be a clever way to prevent them from glitching but it also randomizes and renders unrealistic combat with them. It is ultimately annoying to fight them as a result. You run backward while they teleport toward you over and over - It's neat that they're dangerous but it is sad that they TELEPORT.
8. The level system is . . . uninteresting and seems not worth paying attention to. I think it'd be much better to just start everyone out fully leveled because 1. my fat cousin can run farther than my "survivor" and 2. My "survivor" eats loads more than my fat cousin. WTF. If there MUST be leveling, I'd like it to be under-the-hood pracice based leveling.
9. Prey or Pray is a dumb slogan - was before I bought - just throwin that in here. Please just stop saying it.
10. The masks that the serial-killer veteran players wear are. . .juvenile. I wound up hating all of them. In the time I played I remained a noob and the game felt VERY much about vets mercing noobs. To me that seems like a poor design. Noobs dont want to be bullied and vets dont (in most games) enjoy bullying noobs. These guys do it anyway - which makes me hate them. The juvenile masks make me hate them more. I don't want to spend my free time with these people.
I know the game is in Alpha and that's why I've left out coments on glitches, completion, lame lighting effects and so on. These gripes are deep design issues and. . . well they aint likely to go away. Sorry.
Here's some things that could improve it for me:
1. Non PVP server for doing some of those sweet lookin missions. Also a no paid-content option would be nice. I feel like paid add-ons in a PVP game is a bit of a deal breaker for me.
2. Bigger (Way) map, preferabley proceduraly generated - I know it's too late for that.
3. More sensible item spawning, perhaps mildly instanced item spawns - i.e. if I'm hurt it'd be nice to find bandages in an ambulance - ever.  I should be able to make logical descisions about where to go for what.
4. No lame outfits. Lame means - anything 13 year olds think looks cool. Just do a test group and delete everything they like.
5. Some way to punish Vets for mercing noobs. If there is some system for that it isn't working.
6. Color. The apacolypse will not dull the color of leaves. Leaves will be leaves. Paint will not dull inside away from UV damage. The post-apocolypse will be in full color spectrum color. Please stop this idiotic mistake. Thanks Bethesda.
7. Make the Nether escapeable. It WOULD be more fun for EVERYONE to be chased by big scary stuff and have to hide.
8. Make it so players can run. Like a real person can run. Most adults could run across this map in one go at a good clip. It's like four city blocks on the long side.
9. Get rid of safezones.
10. Share rewards within vicinity with cooperation thus encouraging teamplay.

Out of 10:
Graphics - 9 <- point off for the lame old post-apocolyptic color pallette blunder.
Sound - 6 <- good but thin and repetive.
Community - 2 <- Vets mercing noobs with "Manhunt" style Jason masks ruins this game for me. How about some goggles or some scarves or something. . . why phychopathic serial killers?
Concept - 7 <- In theory this game could be good. In practice most of the ideas aren't realized at all.
Design -5 <- The monsters are great, the city is pretty good, the People are REALLY lame. (bright green napsacks?) Where are these halloween masks coming from? I actually saw witch hunting hats like the ones from Warhammer 40k. Seriously, they're in there. hahahahaa.
Mechanics - 2 <- Game mechanic integration ruins this game for me. It just isn't fitting all together. Random spawns. There isn't much to do - or you don't get to do it with jerks randomly killing you.
Fun - 6 at first then on down to 1.

Game over.

This... Masterpiece...  Is beyond any horror game I've ever played before.
Having played every game in Frictional's lineup, I can say with 100% certainty that this is by far their best.
The enemy types are diverse and I counted at least five or six types, a vast increase from Amnesia's two.  They never stay with the same one for too long, and that makes the terrifying stealth sections never get stale.
The puzzles are also very interesting.  Some may complain about them, but I think it felt awesome to tinker about with the strange, high tech machinery you are presented with when it's puzzle time.  They aren't all that difficult, but they are a welcome breather from those horror sections.
But where this game really goes beyond anything I've seen, is in it's incredible storytelling.  My number one story in a game has been The Last of Us ever since it's release, but this game makes me second guess that.  The range of emotions you will feel on your journey is wide and powerful, and the ending... Oh god that ending.
This game will make you question what it really means to be sentient, and I honestly have walked out of this experience with a completely new understanding of AI and how we should treat the future of artificial intelligence development.
I'm really at a loss for words on how to describe this amazing experience without spoiling anything, since you'll be uncovering things from beginning to end.  Your entire worldview willshift with every step you take, and you will not escape this with the same mindset you had going in.
Please, PLEASE do yourself a favor and pick this game up.  I originally thought the price was a bit much considering what Frictional's games have been like in the past, but seriously- I'd pay $60 for this game, easy.
Grab yourself some surround headphones, crank up the volume, and enjoy this fantastic story.
You won't regret it.

Tormentum the Dark Sorrow is an adventure game lush with macabre imagery.
THE LOOK
This stuff would have been extra stylish and cool at the age of 12 or so. If we had done a schooltrip to a museum with these kind of paintings, my regard of the school system would have been much improved. Alas, we never did go to such a museum.
Now, somewhat later, the visions of Tormentum appear almost cheery in their visceral glossyness, like a gallery of old paintings of hell drawn by the ghost writer for H.R. Giger. With the overflowing amount and the fantastical consistency of the presentation, the emotional effect it all creates quickly trails towards calm acceptance. A world made of grinning, impaled skeletons, buildings and beings twisted, everything torn and burning and contorted and in the process of dying... it becomes the new normal. Its like listening to three Cannibal Corpse records in a row while looking intently at the covers.
THE MOOD
Tormentum is macabre, not scary. Despite all the pain and suffering and cruelty portrayed, the game does not relate these but rather a slight mood of melancholy. The cryptic tangle of the art evokes mild curiosity.
THE CAST
The characters are laconic and somehow matter of fact, giving occasionally a detached feeling. Perhaps the lack of voice acting is part of the reason.
THE CHALLENGE
You need to avoid a grizzly fate, so off to puzzle solving you go. The puzzles are easy, there's a lot of handholding. Sometimes the solutions are handed right out somewhere, you'll just have to look. Its always obvious which solution solves which puzzle. To gauge the easiness, you'll find much more challenging puzzles in the Wadjet games, and the brain-melters like the Myst series belong to a different galaxy entirely. As an interesting twist however, unlike in many adventure games, Tormentum actually allows you to choose what you do, sometimes. This is nice, although when these choices are moral, it is often easy to figure out after a moment of reflection which direction the choices likely point to.
THE VERDICT
Unusual, macabre experience and as such worth a look. Not a horror game in the sense of "boo!" or "yikes!" sensations -- unless something like Clark Ashton Smith books or the old testament manages to scare you. Somehow childish narrative. In difficulty, a casual game rather than an adventure game. Can be played through in a few hours without walkthrough.

After about 10 hours here are my first thoughts, will update as I play more or game changes.
The highest I can score the game at the moment would be around 5.5 to 6/10, it just lacks all the social elements to make a good racing MMO at the moment. It’s a decent game, with potential, but some distance to go. If you want a finished product wait a bit longer and check out the game again further down the line. I can only recommend this game to people willing to accept a pretty barebones product to casually race around in and maybe unlock a few cars to be ahead when the game nears it full release state, and accept the risk that that day may not come. If I could give a sideways thumb I would, but I’ll give the game a recommend, especially since it is clearly listed as an early access game, but only for people that view the game in the light that I mentioned above.
More on the game:
==Graphics==
Both the cars and surrounding look nice. I can play at ultra graphics and still get good performance with an i5-3470 and RX 480.
==Handling and controls==
This game is definitely 100% arcade, so if you are more into sim racing, I can’t recommend this.
On the keyboard, handling feels fine and not too sensitive, cornering does feel like it has some “weight” to it and a bit of braking may be required when taking sharper corners. I find the driving experience with a keyboard in WoS acceptable for an arcade game.
With my Xbox 360 controller for windows (wireless), the experience in less enjoyable, through some sharper corners you can keep the throttle down and just shove the joystick in the direction of the corner, this makes taking 90 degree corners feel more like throwing the car in a direction than steering it and ultimately the cars feel weightless at times. On straights, the cars feel a bit twitchy and move around a lot even with the smallest joystick inputs and I find myself having to correct it often.
==Maps and Tracks==
The game currently contains the following tracks: Street circuits from Moscow and San Francisco, there are a few different tracks per city available with reverse versions available for some of the tracks in practise mode. Racing tracks, only Nordschleife (as a full track or broken up into 3 parts) is currently available. Countryside/Highway type tracks: Azure Coast and California Highway are the two available tracks at the moment. They are also available in their full configuration or broken up into 3 stages.
Currently the only way to drive on a track of your choice is through practice mode where you can select and drive on any of the available sprint and circuit tracks, you can do 1-9 laps on the circuit tracks in the practice game mode. For MP racing you cannot select a track to race on.
==Customisation==
Performance: Very little can be done here to differentiate your car’s performance from others, everything is just unlocked and bought which gradually improves the performance of the car. There is no tuning or building a car to perform better in certain aspects available. The only choices to be made are based on tyres, where you select which type you wish to race with before each race. The 4 tyre types are: stock, drift, street, track. The latter 3 have to be unlocked separately for every car before you can choose to use them in a race.
Visual: Bonnet, Boot, Skirt, Rims, Front Bumper and Color are customisable items. About half of the paint colours are available from the beginning, the rest of the paint colours and items have to be unlocked first. Obtaining items requires dealer points for the specific class to unlock it and credits to purchase and install it. One nice thing though is that once an item has been unlocked and bought you do not have to re-purchase it if you change over to and back from another paint or part. Visual parts do not seem to have an impact on performance.
Only the Subaru BRZ, Ford Mustang GT and BMW M3 E30 (the 3 Early Access DLC cars) have a single permanent livery each available at the moment, there aren’t liveries for any of the other cars (credit and diamond purchased), and are listed as “coming soon” for them.
None of the customisations are behind a paywall or random rewards from races so maxing out a car or getting it to look how you want it to only requires credits and dealer points, which are both earned from racing.
==Social and Playerbase==
This is the area that I’m the most negative about. At times this feels like a single player game with a multiplayer gamemode rather than a racing mmo.
At this point the game lacks the ability to add friends, invite them to private races (which don’t exist) or queue for MP races together in a group.  Text chat is only available right before and right after the race and only with others in the race. I feel that a large part of what will make this game successful is a good implementation of social aspects – making friends, racing together and chatting with people – and a crew/club system. The game is just not ready for people who want to start a new crew or multi-game crews/clubs to branch over here at the moment.
The majority of the races I’ve done had at least one AI player in with quite a few being against just bots. I only found out that this game was finally out when I checked in on the old website and was directed to steam, something has to be done to inform people who signed up to play this game long ago and all but forgot about it as time went on as more people are clearly needed to fill lobbies at the moment.
This game seriously needs a social hub to meet up and hang out with other people to create some much needed atmosphere, whether this is at the airfield playground that was announced and talked about when the game was announced or somewhere else.
==Currency==
Credits: Credits are received by participating in races or converting them from diamonds (1 diamond = 50 credits) The amount of credits earned in a race can be boosted by placing a bet on finishing a certain place or higher as well as meeting some other criteria (overtaking, slipstreaming, drifting, top speed) at the start of every race. There are 3 tiers (easy, medium, hard) the pay-in is greater, but so is the pay-out for higher tier bets. Credits are used to place bets as well as buy cars, upgrades and visual parts after unlocking them. Credits are also used to repair vehicles as their state decreases after racing.
Diamonds: Diamonds can be purchased with actual cash or received when buying DLC. Diamonds can be used to purchase premium cars (1 per tier from C to G), converted to credits or used in the process of transferring dealer points from one tier to another
Dealer Points: Dealer points are earned from racing. A tier “A” car will receive tier “A” dealer points and so forth. These points are used to unlock cars, upgrade kit stages and visual parts before they can be purchased. Dealer points can be transferred between tiers at a cost of 1 diamond per 10 DP transferred.
XP: Not a currency but fits the best here. XP is needed to level up and levels in turn unlock higher tiers of cars that you can start unlocking and buying.
==Cars==
The cars in the game are split off into tiers from A to I. Tiers are unlocked as you level up. Premium cars – whether DLC or special diamond cars – can be bought and used before you reach the required level to unlock the regular credits purchased cars from the same tier.
Premium cars grant an extra 50% XP, cash and dealer points at the end of each race when used.
So far it seems that a credits only path through all available tiers is viable which will bode well for competitiveness when/if a f2p post-beta launch happens.

I didn't think I'd like this game since I do not usually like Real Time Strategy games, but after only a couple of months Offworld Trading Company is already one of my most played games on Steam.
What makes OTC so special is how different each match is. While other games in the genre require constant study of builds as the meta shifts, here the randomized maps and varied strategies from opponents force players to play each round differently. Whereas one match might see the price of food skyrocket you to victory, the next match might find food barely worth the cost of the building. The player most able to see and take advantage of gaps in the market wins.
The result is a game that still makes me sweat after 200 matches played, yet even when I lose I still enjoy myself. What better compliment can you offer a competitive multiplayer game? I highly, highly recommended.
edit: This game has only improved over the course of Early Access, and it's still a game I play regularly!

The weakest edition of Duels of the Planeswalkers to date in my opinion, but it does feature custom deckbuilding from scratch. This is balanced and in the end crippled by two things.
-The fact that card variety is very limited, (Little over 300 different cards counting the expansion)
-Card set limitations based on rarity. (4 common, 3 uncommon, 2 rare, 1 mythic)
Short version:
slow and kind of a luck based progression in the beginning unless you pay for expensive microtransactions that unlock more cards for your deck. Even then the planeswalker difficulty really feels luck-based on some battles. Building the deck is fun but UI is extremely clunky and almost certainly ported from tablet.
This takes the whole game down a notch as it is tedious to make menu selections, scroll cards, tap lands, using abilities and just about everything else when played with a mouse and keyboard. The menus use mouse scroll when they feel like it, but they favor using drag as if played with a tablet. Menus don't activate if you drag a slightest bit when clicking with the mouse, cards zoom if you give a light touch to the scroll. The gamepad controls probably work as intended but I haven't tested. The game also feels slower than previous versions.
Long version:
The game can be very frustrating because you are against pretty competent decks with better synergy for the most part than is available to the player. They have a huge amount of cards not available to the player and they don't share the rarity limit.
You choose a deck with two colors and kind of a weak description at the end of the tutorial. Then you need to unlock rest of the cards by defeating opponents. One win equals one booster pack and you can't get more by defeating the same campaign opponent multiple times.
Different planes reward different cards, but you need to open every plane separately by defeating the campaign levels in the previous plane. This makes building a decent deck even slower because there are only about 10 or so different cards per color per plane.
The final opponent gets a special mentions as you need to win two battles in a row and if you're not lucky it can take frustrating amount of retries.
I don't really think the expansion is worth the price, It features a single plane(Alara) and you're locked to garruks deck without having a good idea of what cards you actually have in the deck, the deck also changes in every battle according to the storyline. The cards awarded are fun but have limited synergy with the rest of the sets and there are too few from the alara set to really construct fun decks from that block. It does feature a couple of triple lands available for deckbuilding though.
Opponents seem to think longer than they used to in previous versions but I'm not 100% certain about this. and all the rules don't seem to always work. One opponent played two of the same legendary without the ability to sacrifice one. The other went to graveyard, the other to the battlefield with tokens from the legendary that went to the graveyard. Also the game sometimes hangs up when you want to cancel a spell with multiple targets.
I haven't played the multiplayer but from what i've read from other reviews, there isn't much variety on strategies and decks because of the limited card collection. Also Free for all is the only supported multiplayer mode.
In the end i really can't recommend this one over previous editions unless you're dead set on making you own decks from a shallow pool of cards.

I'll keep this short and sweet.  Amnesia: The Dark Descent is without a doubt one of the greatest horror experiences you can have.  The story is pieced together by the main character Daniel who awoke with amnesia and after that you begin understanding his objective throughout the game.  Gathering information on this beautifully crafted and immersive little world involves finding notes scattered in all sorts of places.  Exploration is important.
This is not your traditional horror game where you can fight back.  Your only means of survival are hiding, running or distracting enemies then progressing to the next area which is done seamlessly thanks to the  automatic save system.  While you explore you will encounter instances where puzzles must be solved in order to progress.  You solve them by interacting with objects in the world, be they rocks, boxes, gears, etc.  Some puzzles are simple, others require a little more thinking outside the box.  Keep in mind that if the solution is too obvious, it's actually very likely the correct one!    You can also throw objects to cause distractions.  All of these things combined makes for an incredibly immersive experience.
You have two forms of life, standard health and sanity.  If either one depletes entirely you're dead.  Thankfully you can find items that will heal both of these. You start off with a lantern and must search for fuel to keep it lit.  Another means to help you are tinderboxes which are used on various light sources such as torches.
I don't really have a negative thing to say about this.  It's unique, terrifying, creative, immersive, gorgeous, with a brilliantly written story.  This is one of those games that will age greatly.
Oh, and one more thing, there is only one way to play this: in complete darkness with a set of decent headphones and the volume cranked.

I've played a lot of racing games in my life, from Life for Speed to The Crew. I've mainly played Drift City for around 8 years, and Need for Speed World for some time as well, so I basically knew what to expect from a racing MMO game.
World of Speed isn’t a sim racing game – far from it. If you’re looking for a sim racing game, don’t even bother reading this review and carry on.
This is an arcade racing game. Basically a fusion of NFSW graphics with Drift City gameplay, together with no optimization at all, which results in a poorly run game. The physics are non-existent, you can finish a race without touching the brake pedal once, but it’s an arcade racing game so it shouldn’t surprise you. Hitting poles and trees don’t affect you at all.
Upon starting the game for the first time, you’ll notice that you’ll have 500 “Diamonds” and 15 days of “Premium”. Diamonds are basically the real-money currency system in World of Speed, and you get 2.5 euro’s worth of diamonds, which can be used for various small stuff explained a bit further down. Premium is something like a membership which gives you 1.5x more credits, XP and dealer points. Dealer points are explained a bit further below if you don’t know what they are.
Once you’re finally in game, there’s not a whole lot you can do. There’s a huge “PLAY” button at the top to join a racing lobby. This lobby will at most take 1:51 minutes of your life before it throws you into a lobby mainly filled with either bots or Russians. Bots are easily recognizable because of their names, which look like this: AmbertBarton, MattJordan, NancyTate and so on. If you’re not interested in joining a lobby, you can also practice on empty tracks.
You’ll mostly race on 3 tracks, but occasionally you’ll play on the Nordschleife or some highway track in California, but it’s mainly some lap tracks in San Francisco and in Moscow, together with a sprint race near some coast.
When racing, you can get so-called “Action points” by doing certain stuff, like:
-	Reaching 5th gear, which givs you “Top speed” points
-	Drifting, which give you “Drifting” points
-	Slipstreaming, which give you “Sliptstreaming” points (No mistake, it’s really written like this in game.)
-	Overtaking, which give you “Overtaking” points.
These “Action points” are absolutely worthless, unless you’re taking a “bet” when starting the race.
These bets are divided into 4 tiers:
-	No bet, no rewards, no risk.
-	Easy bet, end up in the top 6 and get 1 task which is related to one of the four before mentioned action points.
-	Medium bet, end up in the top 5 and get 2 tasks which are related to one of the four before mentioned action points.
-	Hard bet, end up in the top 3 and get 3 tasks which are related to one of the four before mentioned action points.
These bets are literally the only source of good income of credits when playing the game, but they’re obviously a risk, so take a bet wisely. When playing against easily recognizable bots, it can be an easy source of income. When you’re playing against real players, it could be wiser to take easier bets to not lose that many credits when losing the bet.
Your car has nitro, but it won’t recharge, so use the nitro wisely. Many people just punch it all away in the beginning, only to end up without nitro at the end, where it’s actually a lot more important than in the beginning. But many people fail to realize this and you can end up taking advantage of that.
Upon finishing the race, you’ll get 3 rewards based on the place you gained in the race:
-	Credits, this speaks for itself.
-	XP, this also speaks for itself.
-	Dealer points, what?
Dealer points are required to unlock certain stuff related to vehicles. Dealer points can be used to unlock cars from the dealership, which is necessary before purchasing a car. Obtaining dealer points from a race is based on the car you’re using. If your car is a B grade car, you’ll get B grade dealer points. Upon trying to unlock a car from the dealership, you will get a random car from the tier you’re trying to unlock. I’ll repeat it again: the car you’ll unlock is random. If there are 5 cars in a tier, there’s a 20% chance of you getting the car you actually want.
There are 9 different grades of cars currently in game, of which 1 is unavailable. These grades of cars can be bought after reaching the level needed to unlock these cars. The grades A till H are locked till you reach level 1 till 8 respectively. The former grades are slow cars whereas the latter grades are obviously faster cars. These cars become more expensive to purchase and upgrade, so they’re obviously not that easy to obtain unless you open up your wallet.
Dealer points are used to unlock visual upgrades to your car. You want to unlock some sweet rims or some skirts? Unlock them first with dealer points. If that wasn’t enough already you need to pay some credits to actually get it as well. Basically requiring 2 payment methods to get the visual upgrades that you want.
Dealer points can also be used to unlock upgrading parts from your car. There are 6 tuning kit stages available for any car, and each stage can be unlocked with dealer points. Upon unlocking the tuning kit stage, you can upgrade certain parts in your car for credits. In the first three tuning kit stages you can unlock three different tyres:
-	Drift tyres, giving you more “drift” stat together with xx% more drift action points.
-	Street tyres, giving you more “grip” stat together with xx% more slipstream action points.
-	Track tyres, giving you more “brake” stat together with xx% more top speed action points.
The higher the grade of your car is, the more expensive it becomes dealer points and credits wise.
After finishing a race, your vehicle’s state decreases by 20%. This happens every race till it drops to 0%. When it drops to 0%, your car loses its stats, but they’re very little losses. Repairing your car back to 100% costs around 500 credits, but it’s effective not to repair your car when trying to save up some credits, because the benefits of repairing your car is small.
So, what are these “Diamonds”?
With diamonds, you can purchase credits. Really. You can skip the grind by literally opening up your wallet. 1 race gives around 330 credits upon finishing 1st, without any bets. You can exchange 1 diamond for 50 credits. For 9 euros you can buy 2000 diamonds, meaning 100,000 credits.
If that wasn’t enough already, diamonds can also be used to transfer dealer points to another car grade. For example, you can transfer your A grade dealer points into B grade dealer points for a rate of 10 dealer points for 1 diamond. So if you want to turn 100 A grade dealer points into 10 B grade dealer points, it’ll cost you 10 diamonds.
There’s also a thing called “premium cars”. These cars are exclusively bought with diamonds. At first glance that doesn’t sound that bad, but upon learning that “premium cars” bought with diamonds give 50% more rewards after finishing a race, it’s showing the real thoughts of these developers.
Levelling is a pure pain in the♥♥♥♥♥– and I love to grind, so if you don’t like grinding, look at the following the way you want to look at it:
Level 1: 1100 xp needed to reach the next level.
Level 2: 2200 xp needed to reach the next level.
Level 3: 4400 xp needed to reach the next level.
You get the picture. Levelling is a giant grind in this game, giving no benefits after reaching level 8 – the “H” grade cars can be unlocked when reaching level 8, but after that there’s no point in levelling. The levels itself are meaningless as well, they’re only used to unlock car grades.
Now that I’ve explained every single thing in this game, it’s up to you to see if this game is worth your time or not. For me, this arcade feeling tickles me in special places, which I like. But all this paying nonsense makes it look like a crappy mobile racing game published by EA, in a hopeless attempt to make bank on people.

Ubermosh is a pretty simple game. Jump into it, use your giant blade to kill your foes and to reflect their bullets back at them. Pick up weapons from fallen enemies and use it to your advantage. Get as much kills as possible with'n the game's time limit with out dying, rinse, improve your score, and repeat.
Aesthetically I don't have much complaints. I like the pixel art and the sound track is amazing, it might be my favorite part of the game and hope to see the OST released for sale in the future.
Ubermosh isn't very expensive, about $2.00 USD, and the content reflect the price. There's not a whole lot here, no multiplayer, no extra modes or features, it's just going to be score attack over and over again. Luckily for us, what is here currently is great! The combat is a lot of fun and well designed. It's challenging with a high skill ceiling, and as mentioned before, the music is amazing. Ubermosh is currently in early access, so that could explain the lack of content, but hopefully we'll see much more added to the game as I feel like it has a lot of potential.
Overall Ubermosh has a lot of promise. The combat is exciting, the music is fantastic, and the challenge is enjoyable, I just want to see a lot more of all these things in the near future.

Walter Machado, developer of last year's PC Action title
, returns with a brand new venture simply titled
. While the follow-up release isn't quite done, Walter has gone ahead and made it available through Steam as an "Early Access" purchase at a nice budgetary cost of two dollars US (cheaper if you picked it up on sale around the time of launch). But, what exactly is it, and, even at this point in development, is it anything worth keeping an eye on?
is being described as "a shot of adrenaline", offering an experience similar to that of "a pinball table or a coin arcade machine" according to the game's "about" section. In its current state, you play as an unnamed protagonist in a Cyber Punk world with growing hordes of opponents you need to defeat in order to survive the imposed time limit. It's kind of like the atmosphere of a
title laced with the core principles of
. The only difference is that, as time goes on, it seems to escalate into a Bullet Hell style offering sans the SHMUP style of gameplay.
While it would work nicely as a twin stick shooter, this is more a keyboard and mouse operation on par with
or
, but in a tightly confined space. The keys allow you to race around the field, while the mouse moves the targeting reticle and acts as your mode of attack. The main goal is to deflect bullets from your foes in order to survive, not to mention acquire their ranged weaponry. Of course, if you're like me, you'll probably get more enjoyment out of slicing your opponents in half with your sword than shooting long distance with the various guns that become available.
The problem right now with this idea is that, when you fire so much as a single shot, you automatically pick up any new weapon you run over, changing the firing method. So, say you have a spread shot of some sort, and you prefer it or just have gotten accustomed to it this time around. If you run over another weapon, you might acquire a thin laser shot or bulky bullets instead, which changes the whole dynamic of your ranged attacks. A lot of this seems to depend on the enemy you kill as well, so avoiding their aptly color coded guns for the sake of sticking with the one you prefer can be a little more tedious when it comes to that shot of adrenaline you're looking for.
Recently there was an update that added in a level boss. This enemy, when defeated, would drop a special gun that will never replace any others scattered about the battle field. It's a nice little perk that seems to have longer range and take out more foes grouped together compared to the single bullet deaths of these one-hit-kill enemies. Sadly, there's no major indicator of who the level boss is unless you know all the standard minions, which isn't too hard after a while since there seems to only be a handful of various character designs at the moment. The first time I even knew I had killed the boss was because I had a gun that acted differently compared to the others, not to mention could not be replaced by walking over any others. It would be nice to have some sort of indicator so that gamers know where that objective is within the swarm of enemies rushing you. It doesn't need to point off screen either, maybe just a little downwar arrow above its head when it comes into frame.
The amount of terrain also seems fairly limited right now, only keeping with rather flat color palettes within the randomly generated outdoors world. Hopefully in future builds we'll see levels inside or designs that better reflect the Cyber Punk universe this world is meant to take place in, but, for now, those flat, earthy tones clash with the brighter colors of enemies to help you discern foes to an extent. Regardless of how observant you are, you're still going to miss one or two wandered into frame or appeared out of nowhere.
Finally there's the mixture of Industrial and Metal instrumentals that make up the soundtrack. The sound effects are decent for the eight-bit style Arcade graphics on display, and the faster speed and pacing of the horde growth are both well done to play up the adrenaline side of things. It's all just complimented by static, tribal drum rhythms, or a harsher, grittier battle soundtrack that many developers nowadays would have no problem slapping Alternative Rock songs onto to cater to a wider audience. It seems as though Walter is aware of just who will be playing this title and is focusing on making those individuals happy, something I thank him greatly for.
So, as it stands, this is a quick game of randomly generated terrain you need to run around in and destroy enemies by deflecting bullets or cutting them in half with your sword, only to pick up their guns and start blasting around, all within a very limited amount of time. For as basic a core concept as that is,
is an incredibly fun little top down Action game that challenges you to beat your previous score with each new round. The title screen displays your top kill amount up to this point (though the last update reset that for me, so future ones may do the same), allowing for instant bragging rights among friends, or a challenge if one happens to surpass it while playing under your name. There's also an option for extras, but there's none available at this time, so there's that to either look forward to, or dread. Hopefully it's just for small things like community downloadable content alterations or simple gimmicks like options to make everyone have clown heads or silly things like that.
isn't the most expansive at the moment either, and there's clearly more to come from the roughly year long development the early access outline points out. Hopefully those future additions or alterations won't nerf the challenge or destroy the established classic arcade style game play that makes this idea as a whole work. There are many comparisons to the game
as well, which I can't really comment on as I haven't played it yet. They do look similar, but that's all based on the few trailers I've seen. But, in the end, if you happen to have a couple dollars on your Steam account and want something you can kill five or ten minutes with,
is definitely well worth it at this point in time. You probably won't run marathon gaming sessions, but as a casual pick-up-and-play offering, it's an intense little ride you won't soon regret.
