80 days is an Adventure based on Jules Vernes Around the World in 80 Days. I have been a big fan of Verne since I was a kid and have read the book several times so I was really looking forward this game.
As the game description says, the game has a steam punk "twist". It's not entirely out of the blue, given some of the contraptions in the book, let alone Vernes other books. But it seemed more than half the stories and journeys are on those lines and that is a little too much for me.
That said the characters of Fogg and Passepartout are faithfully recreated and it seems obvious that the games makers where fans. Despite the steam punk aspect, the game does a good job at recreating the feel of the book.
The game is very replayable with many variations and plot twists that are possible each time. The interface is simple and easy to use. The game is very simple- there is an inventory which you can use to buy and sell things but other than that there are no RPG elements or indeed anything to distract from the journey around the world and the choices you make along the way.
I'd say if you like the book or the idea of a simple, casual adventure game then this worth a go. On the other hand if you like the game and haven't yet read the book then you should read it.

Jets'n'Guns is maybe one of two or three games where I'd seriously consider getting in a fistfight with someone who spoke ill of it. It has its flaws, as any game does, but what it also has is planet-loads of charm, an amazing soundtrack, a body count that would make war criminals jealous, and some of the craziest weapons this side of Raptor: Call of the Shadows. A great way to blow off some steam after slogging your way through crowds of people you CAN'T murder with a space plane all day.

To be honest here the game has quite a lot of problems, mostly with the units pathfinding and overall grind to get enough resources or crowns to build important buildings or even stone walls which kinda killed it for me a little but the combat can be very interesting. When it comes to the combat it can be a real challange at first, not so much because of the pathfinding for me though, but because the AI's are able to move more units then you can to specific spots. But thats the fun about it, you can easily out take out the AI if you do things right but sometimes you can easily screw up and lose a bunch of units, which to me is fine again, forcing the player to think about how to go about it without losing every soldier they gained. Not to mention that the game dev's are constintly at work to fix many of the problems that are poping up, they are very aware of the situation that the game is in but are having trouble fixing them due to a recent failure going to NW2 which caused a few problems as mentioned in the recent updates section. Many people say that it isent working but to be honest once more I have a feeling that they just are trying to be trolls cause I have one of thee 2nd worst gaming laptops in my house and it runs very smoothly after I adjust the graphics. Lastly overall the graphics bring me back to my childhood days of gaming, like I said above this resembles Battle for Middle Earth quite alot in the way of graphics but I am by far fine with that, I never was a stickler when it came to things like that, just so long as the models arent sticks flouting around. Overall to me this has so far been a great experience and might even put a bit of money into it just to possibly get the starter pack or something mostly to support the dev's and because I feel like throwing money in their faces, lol. I may add more to this review wether bad or good over the coarse of the next few months and I am planing to deffinitly play this over thanksgiving, so things may change but my opinion of the game will never change, epecially since this is a newly made game, were anything could happen....and yes 3-4 years old is still considered new to me considering ages for other games.

For many this may not be the Shadow Warrior sequel that they wanted but the game does, nothing that downgrades the action packed gameplay of the previous game. It only adds rpg-ish elements to what was already there. I played through the game on hard and while some enemies tooks some more hits to kill they all still die fairly quickly. You are after all mainly fighting monsters and robots, but there is also a small selection of human enemies for which this approach may feel weird. So I think it can get away with enemies feeling a little bullet-spongy, and they have done a good job of implementing different elements into a game that would otherwise just have become a rehash of the first one.
Objectively the first game, a more linear story game, was better at almost everything except what is was all about, action. SW2 is very violent, even more so than the first one. Movement is very fluid and battles on higher difficulties are very fast paced. Like the previous game you don't just kill enemies, you literally destroy them. Hack them into little bits or blow them to pieces. But this time there is also gold and weapon upgrade items falling out of them like pinatas. Maybe that's a little weird, but it works quite well and adds some depth to game, something else to do besides dashing through the air all the time. For me they work a little like intermissions between fights. Walk, kill, dash, kill, loot, look at upgrades, repeat.
The cons are that the endgame is not that great for an rpg-ish game. And overall it is a little short when you don't play on a higher difficulty (because it obviously takes longer when enemies have more health). So i recommend playing on hard because it's not too hard but still challenging. Also there is not much variation in environments, which the diablo-style level generation is partly to blame for. And despite environments being generated you don't really notice it that much.
************************************************************************************************

This is a difficult thumb down from me. I didn't thumb it down because it is a bad game, but only because I want to send a message to the people reading the review. The game features awesome gunplay, but it is all so bland and feels uninspiring. The Shadow Warrior 2013 had a lot of memorable moments and awesome storytelling that did not hinder the gameplay experience as it was in between chapters and it was brilliantly presented.
Shadow Warrior 2 improves on the movement and gunplay mechanics of the reboot as one would expect from a sequel, but apart from the core gunplay, everything else falls flat. The levels are simply poorly designed. You do not find any bit of it memorable, and it's just unimaginative and uninspiried.. It feels like a map designed by a normal guy instead of a game developer who would  carefully design the structures and corners to make combat in such places entertaining. They did not put any thought into designing these levels, when come to think of it, it's supposed to be a staple in a game such as Shadow Warrior. Fine, no modern game has complex level design nor are they maze like. Atleast it could've tried to have varied levels with different settings like the 2013 SW. It's just plain bland here, completely uninspired.
Another drawback of this game is the enemies. A staple to old school shooters is the enemy variety and how you "tackle" every enemy type. SW2 has bullet spungy enemies. I'm not against bullet spungy enemies in games generally, but it's objectively bad in this kind of game because in an old school shooter that SW2 was supposed to be, you had to use specific guns against specific enemies during specific situations. Here that is done artificially by letting you equip "elemental powerups" to your gun. The stupid thing is, you can pause the game in the middle of a fight, unquip one elmenetal powerup and add in another one. Agreed not many people are willing to do that out of laziness, but that's my point. That's not proper game design in this type of game. Because a machine gun and shotgun don't exactly feel powerful or "necessary" in a situation you would expect it to be, because of these elemental powerups that you attach to these guns. For eg, an enemy is up close in your face. In an ideal situation you're supposed to use your shotgun against it. But when that specific enemy is resistant to the elemental eqipped on the shotgun, you're doing far less damage to it than say what an assault rifle with the right elemental equipped would do to that specific enemy. Long story short, the guns just feel fun to use but feel purposeless for the way it's supposed to feel useful. The elemental powerups matter here and that is the reason you're switching weapons, and not because of the weapon itself, and that, my friend, sucks, and it is a damn shame.

I had originally written a negative review for this game, but due to the things that have happened recently I've decided to switch it.
Originally the game was good at it's core, but completely ruined by a horribly toxic community and a prevailing KOS favoring style of gameplay. Add on top of that that the developers didn't seem to pay much care to the community in the first place.
Long story short, the game ended up being a dismal failure for an online MMO survival game. The majority of the community wanted PVE options, and the devs didn't deliver. Players bailed on the game like rats from a sinking ship.
Then the game changed hands... it went to another company who heard the players, albeit a bit too late, and added PVE options. Then things got a bit stale again.
Flash forward some more, and the original devs got the game handed back to them, this time possibly wiser. They've rolled the game back, kept in the PVE, cut out the RMT options, and removed the official servers; instead setting things up so that the players could run the servers themselves.
It finally feels like I'm getting what I paid for in this game, looooong overdue. The game is enjoyable, it's still can be quite a challenge.
Now you can host your own server and have your friends join it instead of being stuck in that hell that was official servers full of KOS players and/or hackers.
The game is dark, and moody; great atmosphere. More than a few times I've found myself trying to sneak around a nether that was in my way, holding my breath as I did so.
It's tense, though I wouldn't exactly call it a horror game.
I will say kudos to the devs for coming back on what I thought was going to be just an abandoned waste of money, and turning it into something that actually resembles what I wanted back when I purchased, even though it's been -again- a really long time coming.
TLDR:
Added private server options! No more official servers full of KOS hackers! You can finally enjoy the game!

This may be early access, but it's pretty much shippable now. That's saying a lot. It's fun. It doesn't sound like it would be. But this is one of the most addictive games I've played in a long time.
It's RTS-like, but there's no direct combat. This is a purely economic game. Take a look at what resources are on the map, collect the rarer ones, sell them. Buy the ones that are more common.
You win via hostile takeover (buying your opponent's stock up). When you lose, you get a $3 mil severance paycheck.
The economy is awesome. Twelve resources is a lot to keep track of, and all of the prices fluctuate based on availability and how much people are buying/selling. Every game plays differently because of this. Steel tends to be fairly valuable, but the last game I played, it was the cheapest resource the whole game. Another game, the map had only 3 waters on it, and I camped on all of them. Monopoly!
Player stock price fluctuates based on your assets, your income, and your debt. When you buy out another player, you get all of their assets. Which means that once someone buys out multiple competitors, the game is basically over, because there's no way to compete. While steamrolling someone usually is an annoying quality in games, it works well here, since once you reach that point, the game ends swiftly.
I don't know what they're going to do before they ship the game. It's worth buying now. If it gets even better, this might be the first game I am hooked on since the early 2000s.

An economic RTS sounds boring, doesn't it?
This game, however, is not at all boring. Strangely enough, I feel more engaged as each buy and sell is incredibly significant. Every action you do will have impacts for the entire game, from where you place your initial base, to every limited parcel of land you buy, to what resources you will produce. Each decision impacts your viability against the other companies. Having to decide quickly which resource to forgo as you try to ensure the quickest and most efficient rise to glory is tense. Deciding when to pour your money into other companies to eventually buy them out or buff up your own stock to shore up your financial defenses is tough.
If you've played MULE a long time ago, or played Meyer's Railroads! not that long ago, or any of the Anno series more recently and enjoyed those types, this game is definitely the next successful iteration of this very small economic game market. Fast paced and replayable thanks to different factions, tech avenues, and resource availabilities, it comes highly recommended!

I was skeptical because this was early access, I liked the developers other works and I figured I'd give it a try.  The Economic RTS is really a big change as♥♥♥♥♥♥moves and market forces can really change a game around.   I really like how maps start unexplored and it is slowly releaved.  You can choose and deploy your colony at any time but waiting till later also has its advantages, if you deploy too early and spend a lot of resources trying to corner the aluminum market you might miss the massive deposit on the edge of the map.
OTC is really about picking the best tradeoffs to get you where you want to go, which is fitting as it's an economic game.   Each colony type has different advantages and needs. expansionists are good at the early game land grab, Scavengers don't need steel and get early warning for random events.  Robots don't need food, but take power instead; and scientists can skip some of the early steps of the production chain by putting factories right over resources.
The early access parts show in that some units don't have detailed textures yet, and they use text to speech instead of voice acting.  There were also a few minor issues I had like not getting an opponents patents after buying out his company.  Overall the game is stable and looks better than most early acess games on steam.

Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II - The Sith Lords is a game originally developed by Obsidian entertainment. The game release back in 2004 was riddled with missing gaps, as the game was rushed out and lots of intentional game implementations never made it on release. Fortunately, the TSLRCM (The Sith Lords Restoration Content Mod) brings back the missing spots, thanks to the fact most of the "cut content" was found in the game files.
This game came out on Steam not too long ago, and initially it got bad reviews for having a lack of up-to-date support on Steam, thus leaving people on their own to figure out how to run the game. Fortunately, eventually some developers came in and actually fixed the game with a nice patch. Aspyr Media, being the bros that they are; developed a Linux port for this game which I must say; is phenomenal. Not only did they port this game, but it runs fantastic; but there is no surprise there with a 11 year old game. Still, I am impressed they chose to take this older game and port it. With TSLRC Mod added through Steam Workshop, this game is even BETTER than it was when I first played it back in 2004.
The graphics show their age, but there are some mods around the corner that look like they are trying to upgrade the lower end graphics. I am simply blown away that this game was taken and given a nice update on steam as well as workshop integration featuring some really nice mods. The windows side works great too, but now I am playing it on Linux and I am loving it too on Linux! One simply does not play this game without including the TSLRCM, that completes it.
8.5/10.0 - Amazing revitalization of a older game. The Ithorians who are restoring Telos would be proud. Now I would love to see the first Knights of the Old Republic ported over to Linux, with full workshop support!

Ok, so i just finished the game.
And actually I liked it a lot.
But before you buy this, you should know about a few thing, so you are not disappointed.
For me, this game is no real horror game in the usual context. It uses a very well designed story, that you need to discover in the world of Soma. And the more you explore, the more details about what was and is happening you will actually get.
The setting of the game and the ideas tied to the story are quite terrifying, but more on an emotional level.
So if you are looking for a horror shocker / jump scare title, Soma might not be right for you.
If you like storytelling, exploration, spiced up with a little bit of jump scares and a lot of "Holy Sh*t, does that mean, that... holy sh*t"-moments Soma is the right game for you. And there are lots of moments where this game punches you in your guts and leaves you with a disturbing feeling of loneliness, thinking about the meaning of life and how to define it.
Here some thoughts:
Its not a really difficult title, there are some monsters, that you need to avoid, as you cannot fight them. But in general you quickly learn to deal with them  and they become more sort of an annoyance. I died like five or six times throughout the game and I'm not very familiar with these type of games.
Choices don't seem to influence the story itself, they are more used for you to think about what is happening and what it means to you. As the game progresses, it forces you more and more to face your own thoughts about what is going on. This may sound as a weakness, but for me, it was not. The game is more about the experience of the story than about you adjusting the outcome. And it does this very well.
Grafics and Sound are truely amazing.There is so much atmossphere created. I loved it.
The characters, ok there are only few, are amazing too - both on the writing and the voice acting.
It is definetly one of the best storytelling games I played so far.
I had one bug during my playthrough, that I could solve by reloading.
It took around 10 hours for a playthrough, I think, I might play it a second time, and spent even more time on exploring the little details, because I rushed some parts of the game - I wanted to know how all ends.. XD But I don't believe I'll play it a third time.
But that although means for the length of the content it is quite expensive.
If it is on sale for 15€ or less, you should absolutely get this thing.

SOMA is ideal for horror fans, regardless of one's experiences with Frictional Games. The story drives the game like no other horror I've played before. Think BioShock, but philosophical and bed-wettingly scary. It surpasses that of its competitors: Frictional Games' previous titles, as well as other horror like Outlast.
But the story's brilliance doesn't outshine the horror aspects of the game. I played SOMA with a friend and we thoroughly enjoyed the abundance of scary moments. The creatures in Pathos-II and the surrounding ocean are horrifying, a vast improvement to the battery pigs in the latest Amnesia title. They intelligently alter gameplay style, unlike most survival horrors where the only solution is to run.
Catherine was an interesting accomplice, who would only interact with the player when necessary. A lot of the characters you learn about are never present in person, and yet have a strong prescence throughout; especially leading up to the ending, which was wholly satisfying. We particularly liked the adorable robot K8.
SOMA is an excellent addition to the genre, and I would strongly suggest it to anyone, survival horror enthusiast or not.

It's a straightforward point and click adventure game. I don't want you to get the wrong impression by me using the word "straightforward," though. In my opinion, most games in this genre have a horrible problem of including puzzles that are either too vague to figure out or having solutions that make no sense to anyone except the developers of the game. I've seen some people complaining that the game's puzzles are too easy, but to me, that just means the mechanics were clearly telegraphed, which is the sign of a good game. In my opinion, I shouldn't have to be running around, trying hundreds of different combinations in a desperate attempt to make progress in the game.
The story is pretty basic, but the world they created to host it is not. I almost wish they'd done more with some of these characters in regards to how they interact and where they end up after you're done with them.
The artwork is obviously gorgeous and lends to the experience a lot.
Sound is pretty good too. I can maybe see why they chose not to, but I think including voice acting for the dialogue would have gone a long way for this game. In general, I think they could have done a little more with the audio to really bring the world to life, but that's just my opinion.
The game is short, but it does encourage at least one replay, so there's that, and it may also seem shorter than other games in the genre just because it's so incredibly well streamlined and clear. If you encounter it on sale and are at all interested, you probably won't be disappointed.

I haven't paid for this game because i picked this up when it was free for a short time and is still don't want to play it because it's (atleast for me) very boring. I will explain my experience with this game so you can decide if those issues would bother you or not. It certainly doesn't statisfy me.
The game plays and feels like a generic third person shooter with minimal story. The main complaints would be the repetitive, casual gameplay that only has hints of depths with the use of some stealth elements which are not really there after you have played for 30 minutes, the very stupid KI which just runs straight at you so you can shoot them one by one (and there are masses of them in many levels i have played). The leveldesign is basically non-existent. There are a few houses you cant enter but other then that everything is static and the Layout represents a straight line from A to B. The few additional ways you can walk despite the main route on every level are mainly there to hide gold(collectibles) which don't feel rewarding when you collect them at all. The controls are unpleasant although i have to give credit to the Dev's that they allow to turn off mouse acceleration (i will never play a game that forces mouse acceleration, it just sucks big time), although it's turned on by default. The bad level design is also reflected by the choice of having automatically generating health and ammo supply that is so great that it feels infinite.
The only thing i found to be original and was actually good fun is the "KillCam"-Feature which let's you see in SlowMo how your bullet hits the enemy and breaks organs and bones on the way through. It's very unrealistic of course but very fun and feels great.
I can recommend this game to casual/console gamers that don't want to be occupied with games for  longer than 30 minutes at a time. It just lacks diversity and depth in order to be a good game that a pc-gamer who likes original, challenging and motviating gameplay would want to play.
Ah another thing iIalmost forgot: This game also has great performance issues on some machines, i haven't bothered that much with fixing those as the game wasn't worth the work but it may be something i should mention.

Writing this as an adventure game veteran there is literally only one reason to play Tormentum: You like spooky art drawn in a Geigeresque fashion.
Everything else that makes an adventure game good - well thought out puzzles, a good story, and an interesting protagonist - are missing here. The puzzles are very straight forward. You will only get stymied on the non-contextual puzzles - stuff like solving a rubik's puzzle or a literal jigsaw puzzle. Or on areas that require a keycode and you need to find where that password is randomly scrawled in the background. The story is a journey through the artist's conception of purgatory. There is a moral choice system, but you will frequently accidently pick the wrong option not realizing that this WAS a choice that affects the game's ending. Not that it really matters as you can probably finish the whole thing in 6 hours on your first play through. There's not really anything in the way of character development. The complete lack of voice acting is an extreme detractor for a 2016 adventure game.
But if you like lots of pictures of skeletons, sinew, and tendons then this is the game for you. I'd rather play Deponia, Monkey Island, or any of the classic LucasArts games.

One of the best shmups you can get your hands on. It has the old school feel of games such as G-Darius or Zero Wing, plus it adds an awesome feature of customising your battle ship. Customize with a capital C. You start off with a few pea shooters and as you progress you get access to lasers, frag guns, missiles, bombs and new ships. Every weapon also has several levels of upgrades, including fire rate, damage and special effects like penetration or shrapnel rounds. The campaign is fairly long, spanning through various environments such as outer space (duh), jungles and even underwater. Some of the bosses will give a run for your money and defeating them comes with a sense of accomplishment. Replayability is also high, after clearing the final boss battle you start the campaign from the beginning on a higher difficulty. There are many secrets to discover, ranging from new ships and weapons to "Lame secret spot marking items" which can be sold for cash in the shop after every mission.

This is a pretty fun game, my brother and I found some people and we all started building a town.  We had a stone wall, a blacksmith, warehouse, etc. and a few rival neighboring towns who we would get into the occasional skimirsh with.  It was a pretty fun experience playing and working with a bunch of people.
Completing tasks like building structures or crafting weapons and armor can be very rewarding because of the time it takes to complete, but the Catch 22 is that this does take a lot of time and not everyone can put that into a video game.  It is not a game you can jump in and out of.  It should really be reserved for kids on summer break or the unemployed.
Also, the biggest drawback is how bad the combat system is.  It is terrible.  I could have gotten really into the game if the combat system was a lot less glitchy and nuanced.  As it is, you just swing and *sometimes* you hit the person?  And blocks are pretty much inconsistent.  It could have been a good game because of the scope and complexities of it, but the comabt turned it into a mediocre to bad game.

I do suggest reading the justifably negative comments here before my opinion. As someone who is essentially new to MtG, I wouldn't be too familiar of how the game stacks up against earlier DotP versions (not well). Nonetheless, I must say I've enjoyed the game so far, based on a newcomer's experience.
There isn't much of a story structure (which I believe has always been the case since the dawn of MtG), but I felt compelled enough to prod through the missions. Admittedly, the game feels quite quite short, so it wouldn't be too long before you focus just on grinding, multiplayer or achievements. Speaking of grinding, I didn't mind it too much; it doesn't take too long to complete your collection. This is why I don't really consider it p2w if you decide to simply buy the collection (which defeats the purpose of enjoying the game, but w/e).
The card pool is quite limited though; you'll also be seeing cards that campaign duelists have cards that you won't be getting. As a note, there's no replay value for facing these campaign duelists (which is kinda dumb, as some of them have interesting decks).
The tutorial is decent, but not perfect; Google became my friend for even certain basic mechanics. Oh, and I highly suggest not choosing the black/blue deck to start with; AFAIK, it's impossible being the first boss with it, save maybe a hosed situation (try white/red instead). I was kinda annoyed the deck was saved over from the demo, and even more annoyed I had to restart the game (which can't be done through the menu nor re-installation; you need to go into your game folder and remove a particular file).
Despite all this, I still suggest this game & the expansion DLC, especially when it goes on sale.

After two days of playing Nether I've decided to give it a thumbs up. It does a great job of instilling in you that feeling of doom and horror with the scenery and the sounds. The enviroment is filled with mutated zombie type creatures of varying sizes and strengths that not only chase after you but they also have the power to teleport. Now you have to keep in mind that this game is a PvP game so the game tends to have those griefers that camp areas where they can prey on defenseless people and then fill the chat area with "F" bombs and other obscenities. After a while I learned to ignore them. On one server there were even a group of players hunting the pkers so not all experiences with them are bad. My biggest issue with Nether was getting it up and running. After installing the game you have to set up an account and then sync the game with your Steam account. The sync part was a bit tricky. It took me a lil while but eventually I got the game working. Hopefully Phosphor will get that issue resolved. After that it has been alot of fun. The world you play in is pretty large so it can be easy to go periods of time without running in to other players (which is best because most other players will shoot you on sight). Nether is still in development so the designers will continually be adding new content over the next few months. If you're looking for a good horror zombie style first person shooter that is online then Nether is for you.

Normally I would play a substantial amount of the game or finish its story before writing a review about it, but playing Duke Nukem Forever feels like a chore - a horrible, boring, unending chore.
It is impossible to ignore the protracted and difficult development that this game had, having taken 12 years and 5 studios to actually produce, since it is obvious that Duke Nukem has suffered from the years. The gameplay is boringly generic and offers nothing new to the genre, which is considerable given how revolutionary Duke Nukem 3D was back in the day, whilst the graphics and humour are both horrible outdated; some textures date back as far as 2005 - a whole 7 years before the finalised product - and the environments aren't particularly pleasent to look out. The humour is also extremely poor despite Jon St. John's performance which is, as it was in the original games, fantastic - but the lines he delivers feel a decade past their sell-by date.
In short Duke Nukem Forever is a horrible game that suffered from its hell in the development stage; this could have been a great old school FPS with some witty one-liners but instead suffers from a lack of identity as it tries to be a 21st century FPS whilst retaining the qualities of its heyday and just becomes a glorious mess. There's no fun and Duke Nukem will go back to its dormant state. FOREVER.

Okay, here's how I see it. Many people are peeved that this games is either "too hard for them" or they are simply not happy with the mechanics of the game or they claim that it doesn't have enough cards. I see it like this. TRY LOOKING AT WHAT HAS BEEN RELEASED FOR THE ACTUAL 2015 TCG AND THEN MAKE YOUR JUDGEMENT!!! The game has almost every card for the 2015 pack. It does take a little bit to get started, I admit. I actually liked the challenge presented to me for creating new and diverse decks. The game play could use a little tweaking, as I have found a few deviations from the rules that I find only mildly annoying. As far as an over-all review goes: I love the game. My suggestion is this: Make your own deck! Figure out what style works best for you and go with that. Expand on it. Optimize it. And when you get to the point that you get tired of your current deck, build another one and start cleaning house with that. This is a TCG-based game, it's not Borderlands, Mass Effect, or ES: Skyrim. It's not made to be a vast adventure that you embark on to rid the world of all evil in a 3-D setting with a diverse character set, customizable characters, and graphics that will blow your mind. It's A TCG-based game. Simple, with a basic story line in which the fate of the multiverse relies on your cards. Simple, fun, and concise.

Duke Nukem Forever is a bad game.
I wasn't dissapointed in the release of DN:F because I didn't buy it when it first came out and I didnt play Duke 3D before the rerelease on Steam (That was taken down by Gearbox because they took the rights or something away form 3D Realms. Now good luck playing the actually good Duke Nukem games because 3D Realms can no longer distribute Duke Nukem games). I've seen people say this 'thing' is a faithful sequel to Duke 3D, and those are the type of people that have 72 hours in Black Ops 3 Multiplayer and 0.2 in Duke Nukem 3D. So you can make your own opinion on those people.
Level Design:
Duke Nukem 3D's level design was open, it allowed you to enjoy the level in your own way and find secrets. DN:F's level design is about as open as a mole's eyelid and about inspired as CoD 4's Multiplayer Map, Shipment. I tried exploring but it was just so 'chore like' so i stopped trying. From the levels I played, I found only one secret (in the first level) and it was being able to... pick up a soggy turd and throw it around the room. Probably put there to reflect the gameplay.
Gameplay:
Enemies in Duke 3D would spout blood out like a fountain and sometimes even kneel down allow you to kick them right in the face. DN:F's enemies have less blood shooting out of them but when their body parts go flying you feel like you can take the world... Until you run into the horrid checkpoint system, sometimes putting you at the beginning of levels and some times through the actual floor. Enemies may have an interesting gib system but it doesn't make up for how they just become bullet sponges and on higher difficulties kill you quite fast.
Overall Duke Nukem: Forever is a clunky mess with outdated, childish humour, taking you through phallac alien hives with hanging breasts on the wall with the option to 'press x to slap' and 'tickle' a n u s looking gateways and to top it all off, end it with fighting a three boobed alien queen mith matching jiggle physics.

I heavily recomend playing this. A superb game pulled out by the Frictional Games team. A game about life, choices, morality, phylosophy... it makes you think, it makes you grow your mind. The game starts pretty easy and then builds up the tension and the story. "It really makes you think what it means to be human". In the end you reach the peak.
The monsters are nicely designed, not hard to understand. I only had a problem with the "last" monster (won't spoil it but it's actually the one before the last), which I couldn't understand really. The monster sections were actually not long. Unlike the reviews say though, it doesn't require a try and fail approach to understand them, but just taking care of reading the notes and listening to what the characters say. The game has pretty many jump scares, even if some are small, they are mostly unexpected. You'll build up adrenaline with monsters around anyway.
The story...what can I say... you'll love the twists. They are just epic. The story is just AWESOME. The choices you take, even if they don't affect the game really much, will make you think very hard, they will question who you really are, and what you think. I won't spoil anything. I will just say the end will... shock you.
The graphics are cool, especially in the underwater parts. I let you judge them yourself, but they are a big improvement from HPL2
The sounds and music... I don't have to say anything about this. The author name says it all. They are one of the most important things in this game. Just superb.
I have to add: unlike the reviews say, I find Simon voice REALLY, but REALLY REALISTIC. Simon will not talk everytime. The game will leave you the silence for your mind to speak.
I recommend this game for real. Don't miss the opportunity to play this, and don't watch videos if you REALLY want to enjoy the story, and the game itself. Otherwise it doesn't have much sense... you got to play it yourself.

Just finished it, and here is what i have to say:
+ The graphics are very nice and compared to Amnesia, its a big step up. Even though some complain about bad textures, it looks just awesome with the right gamma settings.
+ The voiceacting is great and a lot better than it was in previous games.
+ The game was not too long, and not really too short. It had a good variety of environments and the level design was awesome.
+ The soundeffects constantly make you feel like you are beeing watched and add a new layer of fear. They are of great soundquality too.
+ The Story was very interesting and gets you thinking about what just happened, which is great.
The Ending was incredible and left you with all kinds of thoughts.
+ The "maps" were quite big sometimes, and it felt like there was always something to explore.
+ The creatures were scary and constantly moved around so you never knew where they would come from.
Some negative things:
- The characters sometimes seemed a bit careless in contrast to what was going on. The voiceacting, even though its great in quality, was missing at some key events. The character seemed a bit too chill in some situations and didn't talk about things that would have been important to notice. I think you get what I mean after playing ;)
- The "monsters" where not that well intruduced at first. What i mean with that: The first really scary one didn't keep its "fear factor" for too long, since you kind of just had to push through it and avoid to look at it. Then you were perfectly save. The third one was kind of badly placed. You could just sit above it and watch it run around, which also removed some scare factor.
!BUT! They ARE scary and will make you freak out in other places. Just the way they got introduced was not too complementing.
- / + the npc's gave the game a bit more life which is cool, but at the same time they looked a bit unreal in some ways. Their animations kind of remindet me of the charakters in Half life 2, meaning they moved a bit odd.
Overall I really enjoyed playing this game and I can really recommend it to everyone who likes scary, but also very story based games. It is not a game you should run through just for the scares. You really should switch off the lights, put headphones on and dive into the story and the atmosphere. That is what makes the game so great for me.
The story gets you thinking a lot and I haven't seen anything like it in other games.
Go try it out! It really is worth your money, unlike many other games nowadays! :P

Tragically and hauntingly beautiful. Tormentum presents the player with a question of morals, determining a "good" or "evil" choice at various crossroads. Part of the effectiveness in this game's presentation comes from the difficulty in differentiating between which choice is correct.
Do I save the man being tortured? How do I know he doesn't "deserve" his punishment?
If I murder this guard, what treasures will be mine? He is evil, I am not; therefore his gold should be mine.
She must be innocent.
He is my friend; he helped me escape. Surely there is an explanation for his actions.
Who am I to decide the fate of another?
This is the question posed to the player. Who am I, and what justifies my actions?
Do yourself a favor and set aside 2-3 hours to play through Tormentum in one sitting. The minimalist gameplay combined with vividly drawn settings create a dark atmosphere, immersing the player deep within the world of Tormentum.

Shadow Warrior 2 marks a departure from the first in that it delves into ARPG territory. I can akin it to something like Diablo or Borderlands. Does this detract from the game? It's a yes and no answer. A yes, mainly because Flying Hog seems to have been unable, so far, to correctly implement certain supporting aspects for an ARPG-like game. Straight off in the game it's obvious that grinding is encouraged due to the huge amount of randomized "gems", the HUB, the shops, the option to re-roll shop inventories, and the ability to free-roam side mission levels that have been completed. Hell even with the recent FREE-DLC, you have to farm multiple trials in order to upgrade your weapons. But there issues with these. One, the huge amount of loot you can accumulate in one level can make it a hassle to scroll through the inventory screen. Even with the sorting options, it's a pain to find that one gem you got on this mission and now wanna socket it to a new weapon you just found. I can akin the gem inventory UI to something out of the Elder Scrolls, post-Morrowind. Second, there's no urge to encourage players to head back into the free-roam areas. The levels they use in this game are procedurally generated and very quickly you will notice that the game will start recycling through the same maps but with minor differences. Granted, the level of detail in these maps is pretty good but aside from chopping up random demons, there's nothing to come back to UNLESS you are hunting mini-bosses you have missed while questing. Beyond that, nothing else. Now even though farming is encouraged, it's not necessary to have a fun time.
Shadow Warrior 2 delivers an equal, if not more, visceral feel to combat. Gunplay has improved significantly. Long gone are the days of bullet sponges, now are the days of deadly weapons with punch and feel to them. Melee combat has kept to its roots from Shadow Warrior 1 but is further expanded upon by the multiple melee weapons you'll find. This goes for guns as well. Now even though this game does borrow heavy ARPG aspects, it thankfully does not follow the Borderlands style of randomly generated weapons. Each weapon in this game is unique and, if you are willing, you can upgrade them further using the crafting system introduced by Way of the Wang but that requires huge amounts of farming. There's also the multiplayer aspect of this game but I have yet to try it out since I'm a lonely pleb. Now what about the story? Well it's a mixed bag compared to the first one. That probably has to do with the larger scope of the sequel and Hoji's replacement by Kamiko. Kamiko is irritating at first and probably won't grow on you until you're half way done with the game. It would help if they allowed all her audio files to play during quests to develop her but apparently not. For Wang, he's as Wang as he can be and I love the dude. No issue there. The background lore, which can be found as random loot during missions, helps shape the world of Shadow Warrior but can become convoluted especially when trying to piece together the journals of random background characters and their relations to one another. Now the worst sin the Shadow Warrior 2 storyline commits is the abrupt cliff hanger ending. How it plays out in the end, isn't necessarily explained well because of how abrupt it is. Another controversial aspect of it is the ambiguous fate of Lo Wang at the end.
But even with this... the gameplay definitely delivers the game past it's story faults and bad grinding. Shadow Warrior 2 is a definite recommendation if you were a fan of the original or of fast paced action games in general. Where else can you find a game that plays and feels so good when decapitating demons with a katana in first person?

This was a very enjoyable revisit to a great story and fun adventure. I played the original and all of its sequels when they first came out and even though i remembered roughly how the plot would flow, it was still fun and atmospheric to redo it, and a satisfying trip down my gaming memory lane.
Initially, i found the strength of Gabriels accent really annoying, and some of the lines really cheesy, but as i played that mattered less and less, and I focussed on the nicer graphics, story and plot.
There is a really useful hints function within your in-game diary that prevents the annoying stagnation and walls you can sometimes hit in puzzle/adventure games. There are two levels of hints. The first level is a gentle one, and wont completely steal the satisfaction of solving the puzzle or days tasks. The second level hint, if you use it, is a much more detailed "cheat", that will state plainly whats required. There is a timer function that prevents you clicking the hints straight away.
I really enjoyed replaying this game, partly out of pure nostalgia, and partly because it is a worthwhile modernisation of a fondly remembered game. I was especially satisfied by the art material and graphics from the original game being viewable within your in game diary also. That content gets unlocked as you progress.
If you have love for the original, and would simply enjoy replaying it with new clothes, buy this game (again). I did, and dont regret it.

I have played this game a lot. I know almost everything about it, currently. I have built everything that there is to build, been a king, a farmer, a warrior...  so when I write a review, know that it is quite balanced. I am no fan boi, and will let you know all the pro's and cons of this game.
Pros.
1. You can tailor your characters skills to match what you wish to do in the game. Depending on the server skill cap, it can mean you can ONLY be a farmer and a bowman, or a smith and a swordsman, to being able to do everything.  Pick the server that best represents what you want. RP, pvp, rp/pvp, high skill cap (recommended for new players) or low skill cap.
2. crafting system requires a lot of steps. You want to build a small house? Alright the you either have to have a supply of trees nearby, or have forestry to plant saplings and wait half a week in real life for trees to grow enough to harvest. Then once you get the timber, you or a friend better have herbalism to get enough flux to make steel for the locks and mortar needed for doors. Then you better know enough materials prep to make glass for windows... which requires carpentry as do the doors. Oh, and smithing to make the locks... while you make clay tiles. So, you need 1. forestry. 2. logging. 3 carpentry. 4. smithing. 5. materials prep. 6 gathering. 7 herbalism... just to make the smallest house in game.  On a low skill cap server, this will take the combined efforts of 3-4 people. Now imagine what a castle takes.
3. harvesting is indepth. Need leather? Go hunt, make coops to harvest hares, and barns for animals... oh you need to actually trap those animals, or tame them.  Food is grown, and harvested... then a cook is needed ot make it into actual food. All raw resources need to be manufactured into goods.
4. giant battles. I have participated in a 64 man judgement day battle. Took hours of non stop fighting, with trebuchets flinging rocks, bombs and arrows everywhere, people murdering eachother and sometimes friends on accident.

4. broken features/bugs will drive you crazy. Wait till you die 20 times in a row, losing a ton of skill points that takes  hours to get because of a bug.
You can't play the game by yourself and expect to win. The fun is in groups. Dont buy this game if you dont want to join a group.

OVERALL REVIEW:
8/10
ABOUT:
Offworld Trading Company reminds me a lot of a business simulation I played in college called MARKSTRAT. In Offworld trading company your objective is to buy out all of your opponents. There can be only one man left standing. You start and scan a planet for resources, and then select one of 4 factions: Expansive, Robotic, Scavanger, or Scientific. Each of these factions has several unique traits. Expansive has extra claims so they can build more, Robotic only needs power and electonics, scavanger gets early access to black market items and uses carbon instead of steel, and Scientific can put buildings that need resources on hexes that have that resource thus reducing the amount of claims they need to use: EX you can put a steel mill on iron without any iron mines and produce steel. My oppinions of the 4 factions are below. The game also has a black market where you can buy things to better your faction like extra claims/protection from enemies or undermine other factions with things like underground nukes. It also adds random auctions that go to your debt, which can really help if you need to save a geothermal vent for later in the game or are in desperate need of another claim.
-Expansive: (Best)(1) This is in my oppinion the best faction. The extra claims they recieve make it much easier to be the first to get a HQ lv5. This faction will generally be the easiest to get the offworld trading export rocket, which is almost always a sure win.
-Robotic: (Good)(2 Tie) No need for water, fuel, food or oxygen. Rush for electronics early and have some power and your society will almost never be in debt.
-Scavanger: (Worst)(4) Inless the map has high carbon contents and low iron, this faction is a no-go. See what I said in cons about the black market issues.
-Scientific: (Good)(2 Tie) Great faction for maps with a large amount of water or low iron. You can keep costs way down if you build your food supply and fuel/oxygen supply on this water. A great strategy is to build two steel mills at the beginning of the game on iron since you dont need an iron mine.
PROS:
-This is the most original game I have early access played since Minecraft. I think it has a ton of potential.
-The game is pretty fun, and I think it will be much more fun when multiplayer isn't just player hosted.
-To play a round takes generally around 30-40 minutes, meaning it won't take all day.
CONS:
-$35-$40 is just flat out too expensive for an early access game like this. This game should be in the $20 dollar range. I mean you could buy Skyrim for $40!
-Big issues with the black market: No matter what faction you choose or how early you settle, the AI will always get the first action in the black market, meaning that by the time you get to it, additional land claims will be more expensive. This in my oppinion, defeats the point of going with the scavanger faction.
-Random events are too extreme. In the real world an oversupply of a resource will not have it go from $100 to $1. I would like to see these events toned down. Perhaps a oversupply would lead a $100 dollar resource to become $40.
-Offworld Export Rockets are ABSURDLY overpowered. The first person to build one will generally win the game. Generally this will be the expansive faction.
-The game ends too suddenly. All of a sudden someone will get rich from the offworld exports and in litterally 2 minutes after this is built the game is over.

I would recommend you not to read too much about the game. Play the demo first, it's a good representation.
If you, after completing the demo find the game interesting and, want to continue your experience I would suggest that you back up your saves, before the purchase, because Steam will just delete it all upon installation of the full game.
I was a bit sceptical about the game at first, especially in regards to the new boy'ish look of Gabriel Knight and this silly southern voice that is being used, but also in regard to the changes of design. It took me awhile to get past that change and I was just barely ahead of it at the end of the demo.
Truth be told I was never really a fan of the GK series even though I tried my hand with all them in their own time with a declining interest, that was completely gone after five minutes with GK3. I generally despised the Sierra Adventure games, because they were so dull, traditionally old-school and unforgiving somehow compared to the humorous and creative Lucasarts Adventure games I loved.
I am glad to see that Pinkerton Studios have gotten a much better hold on the game engine that severely scarred the previous Mobius game. Gone are the wandering eyes and jittery animations.. There is still a few minor flaws, but much less than before. There is also lip-syncing and it works surprisingly well.
I read quite a lot of reviews about the game, the good, bad and ugly, because I was a bit lukewarm about GK, but I was curious and played the demo first and even though this new version isn't quite the same high-caliber version as the original it's not a bad game, not a bad game at all, but it's clearly not a total remastery of the old game, since they've changed the voice actors. Even though I was quite resentful of the voice of Gabriel Knight in the beginning it kind of grew on me and the accent is also more downplayed as the game goes on. The rest of the voice cast is pretty decent.
My only real complaint about the game is the background Music - it's bloody horrible and totally out of place with the spirit of the game unlike the game music during cutscenes which is very well done. I was about ready to quit before the demo even got started, because of it, but I hit a key to skip the intro credits and turn off the music, which saved the day.
There is a new hint system in the game, but unfortunately it's neither very intelligent nor progress based. The few times I needed it I was way ahead of the hint system and had to wait for the hints to catch up to my point of progress, because of build-in timer, that I assume has been put in place to avoid that you spoil yourself too much and even then it was extremely rare that it was useful at all. At one point it was completely useless and I had to Google for a solution, because I got a bit ahead of myself and was unable to pick up on a vital clue on how to unlock an important puzzle.
There were times when I was a bit lost about my next move, because the game is a bit short of a narrative and there is a certain amount of things that you need to solve before the day ends, which isn't very clear, but the first hint of each day usually give you a list of to-do's of the day. I do not recommend using the hint system at all, because the game is actually quite short.
I saw a reviewer complaining about the same animations being played every time you leave an area, but that's kind of a silly point, because you can use fast-travel everywhere. You don't have to leave any area by going to an exit point at all, because you can bring up the map at any point, which is really nice, but unfortunately Gabriel Knights current location isn't highlighted on the map at all.. Sometimes I went to places where I was already.. The same teleportation system in Mobius has transferred to GK1 as well, but there are times when you need someone to follow you that it backfires.
There is still a bit of the old ghost of Sierra's unforgiving gameplay present, but the good news is that there has been added a RETRY option for those special events.
I finished the game in 15 hours and I am actually a bit surprised that I had a such a good time with it. Jane Jensen was a much better writer twenty years ago, but she also had a co-writer on GK1, and that part still stands.

With recent update, I can confidently recommend this game, but only when the game is on sale. The gameplay is interesting and I have faith in developers in delivering a decent game.
In Offworld Trading Company, you play as a CEO who builds factories on the red planet. There are 4 factions to choose from, each with their unique perks. Games are mostly driven by player decisions, which makes every game unique and exciting. Even with the same map in the daily challenge, I never end up using identical strategies.
With all the variety, the game is hard to master. Maximizing profit is difficult as prices depend on every player's action. It is hard to decide what to produce, even harder to predict how other players will react. There is also trade off between sabotage and development.
Devs have made good progress on improving game experience and adding new content. They have fixed many bugs and improved the performance of the game. The UI now is much more informative than that at release. The update logs are long and most of the features are what players have been looking for. AI players are decent and are still being worked on. Balancing and game mechanics are also being tweaked. A big thanks to the developers.
Sadly the player population is shrinking and it is hard to find a multiplayer game. Only get the game if you are fine with playing against AI players, or if you can find friends to play with. Also, despite modding being supported, I don't see active modding communities working on this game, nor is the steam workshop available.
As a conclusion, the game is in good shape, and I believe it will get better. 40$ is way too much for a simple game like this, but I'd recommend people to try when the price drops below 20$.

I would also mention Grace, Dr John, Mosely and Frick as outstanding performances.
Visually its a balanced mix of photo and painted textures, blended with pre-rendered backgrounds and real-time props & characters. A nice touch is the ambient atmospheric particles & lighting effects.

The bonus option to view old concept art from the different locations, combined with info and audio interviews with the original developers is a nice addition for fans of the old game.
I would highly recommend this game for adventure fans, looking for a story driven game. If you are already a fan of Gabriel Knight, what are you waiting for?

Overall, this is a good game. True, the interface needs some work as it is slower and clunkier than its predecessors, but there are a lot of good things about it too, and it has the potential to become the best in this great series of games with some patches and additional DLC.
I have played all of the MTG games to date, and loved them all. As you can see from other reviews, this one is not nearly as polished. The interface is slower to respond, sometimes causing you to miss crucial opportunities to cast instants and activate abilities, and it can be a little awkward and frustrating to operate. It feels like they rushed an unfinished game out before it was due in order to meet the annual release that we have come to expect.
That said, I still recommend the game to both new MTG players and seasoned veterans because of the things that are done right.
Most notably, there is now the ability to design your own deck from scratch. Finally! What's more, they've added a deck building AI so that it is not overwhelming to new players that works quite well. You can choose one or two cards that you like, and then click "auto-complete" and it will fill in the rest in a way that seeks to compliment what you chose, or you can flesh out most of the deck and see what suggestions the AI offers to improve your build.
Some people are frustrated with the start of the game where you can choose only one deck with only a vague description, and then unlock more cards as you grind through the campaign. I actually enjoyed it, and I think it, like the deck building AI, is targeted towards getting new players into the game. You unlock cards at a reasonable pace, and by the end of the campaign, I had slowly but completely transformed my deck, such that I was even using a different color scheme, so I don't see why picking just one deck at the start has upset so many people.
More cards and more content will be coming. The first expansion added a lot and I am sure there will be many more. I bought the complete edition from the start so I don't need to pay each expansion as it comes out, and I am satisfied with that. Some people said that by buying the complete edition you miss out on content because you don't have to play to unlock everything, but that is just not true. You still have to play all the way through, including exploring each plane completely, to unlock cards. The only way around that is to specifically buy the Battle Boosters DLC which just unlocks the cards you would get by battling. Anyone who says you have to pay to have equivalent cards to other players is just plain wrong.
All in all, if you want a perfectly polished MTG game right now, you'll have to buy last years edition. If you want to build your own deck, buy this one. The interface problems are managable, albeit occasionally frustrating, and they are not bad enough to outweigh just how much fun the game is now that deck construction is possible.

Pro:

Theres♥♥♥♥♥♥...thats kinda nice. (im really scratching the end of the barrel with that one trying to come up with some possitives)

Cons: (There are alot)
I could easily say everthing is a con in this game but that would be too easy.
The story is really nonexisting. Most of the time your going from mission to mission with small bits of exposition every once in a while.
Bosses are very bullet spongy especially on insane mode. The main annoying one is the octaking and the battle lord......and the electric eel. Pretty much all the bosses suck.
Alot of platforming; this would be a bad thing if it didnt subtract from the combat. The thing is if your taking out moments of combat to give the player some time to chill before rushing into more combat give us something like the strip club. That was a fun mission to escape combat.
Octabrains and their telekenises. On insane mode these enemys are kinda fast and they hit like a run away ice cream truck. The main issue is that these enemys have the ability to pick up any and all objects like boxes, barrels, and other things. Thats not the issue more as they can throw back objects like rockets you shot at them dealling enough damage to insta kill you. I wouldnt complain if i wasnt being punished for what gun i had or want to use to deal with an enemy. I would be fine if rockets had reduce damage on these enemys because of their special powers slowing the rockets velocity or something while only able to fully interact with nonmovable objects.
Water levels.That word alone should be a thumbs down unless the level is done right which for this game it did not. Whats annoying is that duke has a lung capacity of a 4yr old. Conclusion:

Other than that, this game got me thinking about all those philosophical subjects featured in the story, especially how it can be related to the real world, and it's a pretty interesting material for thought.
Overall, cool, worth buying! Plus there's modding support, looking forward to play custom maps.

Just finished it, and here is what i have to say:
+ The graphics are very nice and compared to Amnesia, its a big step up. Even though some complain about bad textures, it looks just awesome with the right gamma settings.
+ The voiceacting is great and a lot better than it was in previous games.
+ The game was not too long, and not really too short. It had a good variety of environments and the level design was awesome.
+ The soundeffects constantly make you feel like you are beeing watched and add a new layer of fear. They are of great soundquality too.
+ The Story was very interesting and gets you thinking about what just happened, which is great.
The Ending was incredible and left you with all kinds of thoughts.
+ The "maps" were quite big sometimes, and it felt like there was always something to explore.
+ The creatures were scary and constantly moved around so you never knew where they would come from.
Some negative things:
- The characters sometimes seemed a bit careless in contrast to what was going on. The voiceacting, even though its great in quality, was missing at some key events. The character seemed a bit too chill in some situations and didn't talk about things that would have been important to notice. I think you get what I mean after playing ;)
- The "monsters" where not that well intruduced at first. What i mean with that: The first really scary one didn't keep its "fear factor" for too long, since you kind of just had to push through it and avoid to look at it. Then you were perfectly save. The third one was kind of badly placed. You could just sit above it and watch it run around, which also removed some scare factor.
!BUT! They ARE scary and will make you freak out in other places. Just the way they got introduced was not too complementing.
- / + the npc's gave the game a bit more life which is cool, but at the same time they looked a bit unreal in some ways. Their animations kind of remindet me of the charakters in Half life 2, meaning they moved a bit odd.
Overall I really enjoyed playing this game and I can really recommend it to everyone who likes scary, but also very story based games. It is not a game you should run through just for the scares. You really should switch off the lights, put headphones on and dive into the story and the atmosphere. That is what makes the game so great for me.
The story gets you thinking a lot and I haven't seen anything like it in other games.
Go try it out! It really is worth your money, unlike many other games nowadays! :P

One of the best, the graphics may not look different but the new range of weapons, ability to start a small army and choose sides in an on going slaughter make Mount & Blade: With Fire & Sword one of the best in its series. If your not traveling for two days to get to some hovel filled village on the brink of starvation, or talking to the mayor of Warsaw for a job you could be killing some Swiss deserters or tarnsporting goods to make a 100s of Thalers. The joy of slashing the head off a  bandit while speeding on horseback, firing a musket shot straight through the head of a Polish Hussar from attop a hill or wildly slashing in close quarters combat. The combat controls are not too different from any other PC game, blocking is vital and I would say playing the tutorial is very useful.
In one paragraph I couldn't sum up what you can do to get money, gain reputation and level up. Sending caravans is risky, you must spend hundreds on what to send where this also includes prices for guards and other things. Most of the time you get some money and make a profit, however, the other times you are left penniless because your caravan 'was attacked' and there is nothing you can do, a very quick way to be sent into manic depression. Obviously you can do missions to heavy your purse as well as boost rep amongst the faction who gave you the task. Occasionally you are given...lets call it preporation cash, this amount is so you can get some weapons, perhaps hire some help and to act as an insentive so you get on with it! However, don't spend it all in one place! With these new found riches you automatically go to the arms merchant to the coolest looking sword or to the Armour merchent to get that "Uber awesome lookin' helmet!" I will tell you now if you lose that battle, you will be marched miles away from where you need to be, then left with no sword, or helmet, scrap of meat or coin to your name so spend wisely!
Hiring men, it's cheap depending on what they can do, so hiring 50 scythe wielding peasants to unquestionably attack 20 calvarymen in droves only to kill half, get massacred, and leave you to take out the rest is insanely useful! However the cost will rank up on their skill, and on that note, we move to ranking up. It's not too complicated and is very useful in making sure your men don't all die. Again keep in mind cost so don't think it necessary to always be a force for good. Think of it as borrowing, a late birthday gift or anything else that isn't stealing. Caravans travel all across the land, loaded with goods, ripe for the picking. However, the Caravans are not without protection, guards may be travaling with it making it seem alot less worth it. However, with your strong army you can do as you please, if you can ransack villages(which you can) then you can take on a caravan!
Factions, factions everywhere! Though you don't need to keep them all happy it doesn't hurt to try. But picking sides in a battle can have some very good results...if you win. Doing tasks for your faction can help alot in making you richer and them stronger, however, this war is alot like a boxing match, cheer for the bigger guy. Though there are not many factions here's the list:
-The Kingdom of Sweden
-Cossack Hetmanate
-Polish Commonwealth
-Muscovite Tsardom
-Crimean Khanate
-And, your own.
W-w-what? M-m-mine? Yes yours, there are several ways to crush the others and plant your banner into the soil. You can join a faction, then split by capturing towns and denouncing your loyalty. And, after that convince the other lords and ladies to join you! What's stopping you?
To conclude, Mount & Blade: With Fire & Sword is the best in the series, with good multiplayer, leveling up, combat and story, it's a breath of fresh air for the fans. Though it may lack in some graphical areas it makes up with gameplay and pure brilliance in campaign and other new features. This game may not be enjoyed by impatient gamers but is great if you like not knowing when your going to be attacked, whether your caravan will make it or whether your troops will die. As I said at the start, Mount & Blade: With Fire & Sword is fantastic.

Pros
-AMAZING artwork and visuals. It's beautiful in the most disturbing way.
-Well thought out puzzles. No pixel hunting or weird item combinations that don't make sense. Everything that's not obvious has a clue somewhere in the game world and can be solved without a walkthrough if you think hard enough.
-The mini-game based puzzles (ie: slide puzzle) are all reasonable and can be solved with just enough effort that you aren't screaming in agony but not so simple that they might as well not be in there. Some were more on the easy side, but none were too simple.
-The writing is wonderfly grim and dark which fits the atmosphere perfectly. There are very few moments you feel as if there's a ray of hope in the grim landscape only for it to be plucked away or for the moment to be ruined by some cruel act. There's a few twists that caught me by surprise and, while very simple, the plot does its job wonderfully.
-The addition of choice was a lovely addition to the game which really gave the feeling that you truely were trying to escape a hellish trial.
-The music is down right amazing and makes me wish I had the sound track.
Cons
-The game is fairly short. I completed it after playing non-stop for about 3-4 hours.
-One of the difficulties with having morality choices in a game is that, sometimes, it's not as black and white as it appears. There's two choices in particular where either you lack enough information to make a good judgement call and/or it could be argued that the "bad" choice isn't a bad choice at all.
Overall, I have VERY few complaints. If you're a fan of point and click adventure games with a love for this kind of artwork and style, it's definitely worth picking up.

Did I just spend money of this?:

If you're a diehard fan of old school death metal (like I am), you probably know who is Dan Seagrave and what kind of bizarre, surreal and dark worlds he portrays in much of his work. Add a healthy spoonful of Zdzisław Beksiński and a dash of H.R. Giger to go with it, and you pretty much have Tormentum - Dark Sorrow.
The game has superb art direction and everything feels and looks very polished. Music and sound fit the style and the mood of the game perfectly and I just generally tend to enjoy this kind of dark fantasy.
However, the game lacks in length, difficulty and gameplay. The puzzles are very easy and I completed the game twice in just under 4 hours, without ever needing to consult a walkthrough.
The main character just stands still in the scenes, limiting the feel of interactivity in the world. Moving between scenes happens instantaneously, without any walking animations. There is very little text or dialogue in the game. Also the morality of the game is very black-and-white, although the moral choices do have interesting twists.
The price of the game is a bit steep for such a short game with very little gameplay, but if you find it on a sale, I heartily recommend it for an evening of dark fantasy adventure.

This game has some of the best, if not THE best, artwork of certainly any point-and-click I have ever played, and possibly any GAME I have ever played. At the risk of selling it short, it’s an endless parade of Giger-esque 70’s metal album covers, all of them detailed to the point of astonishment and masterfully done.  The music is also fantastic and compliments the sorrowful atmosphere (hey, it ain’t subtitled Dark Sorrow for nothing).
The only fault I can find are some occasional and unfortunate English-as-a-second-language errors and verb-tense switching issues that marred an otherwise decent and philosophical story.

None of the puzzles are difficult – some might find them TOO easy; none are obtuse and the game is generous with its hints.   I had to look up a solution only once, and this was simply due to an object I had missed. This made for an enjoyable ride that wasn’t too taxing and removed the frustration that most point-and-click adventures suffer from.
I own too many point-and-click games, but I never actually play any of them. This one I bought, loaded it up, and was compelled to play it from start to finish, putting aside everything else I’m playing at the moment. I think it’s actually the first point-and-click I’ve ever completed. I played through once and received perhaps the neutral ending. I don’t usually play games twice, but I’m considering revisiting this one just to check out the other endings.
I waited for a sale before I bought, but after playing it, I wouldn’t have minded if I hadn’t.
If you enjoy point-and-click games, are a fan of H.R. Giger, and dig on cruel and oppressive dark fantasy, this game is an absolute must buy and well worth the full asking price.

Don't be fooled by all the negative reviews. Life is Feudal is a really wonderful game.
It is not an EASY game by any means. I do not reccomend playing it alone. Get four or five good friends to play with you or join a server. Life is Feudal is a cooperative game. You can scrape by on your own, sure, but you won't advance past the Stone Age. If you think you can log on, build a castle in two hours, and log off, you've got another thing coming. LiF doesn't hand you goodies on a silver platter.
If you've got a hardworking team of people, though, you can accomplish some really awesome stuff. For example: my boyfriend and I joined a server and started working toward building a house of our own. We felt insanely accomplished when we managed to build two hovels and kill a stag. It was an enormous rush! LiF makes you work for every single thing you get. As a result, the rewards matter a lot more. We eventually joined up with a bigger town and became Master Armorsmiths. It was amazing to see our hard work pay off. It gave me a sense of accomplishment unlike any other game I've played.
LiF is hard and can be pretty punishing. But the difficulty makes your rewards that much more awesome. You understand the value of an item because you worked hard to get it.
Here are the bad parts: the games crashes frequently and load times are awful. Except to spend 5-10 minutes per load screen. Plus, it's a memory hog. Buyer beware if you're running it on a laptop or an older PC.

-The music punched me in the face when I hit the title screen and absolutely stunned me. It really fits the game itself and the speed of the combat, making the gameplay more tense which I absolutely loved.
-The addition of lots of unique weapons was welcome, and the use of modifications as primary loot to boost things like crit or life-steal or elemental types attuned itself to personal playstyle (For the most part...).
-The fact that the developers so far have released several free updates that contain both balancing/quality of life changes (fixing a previously broken overly OP sword, gaining the ability to search through weapon mods, added special orbs gained in game used for further upgrading weapon statistics) and FREE content patches (Way of the Wang DLC, Christmas update) which is one hell of a breath of fresh air in a growing gaming world of microtransacting, inordinate amounts of paid DLC, and Season passes.
Now that we've covered my apraisals of the game, time for me to talk about the things I or others feel weren't the greatest.:
-The game does feature a somewhat different setting than typically seen in the series as some people have complained, but that personally doesn't really bother me. After playing Hard Reset (Also made by Wild Hog Studios) I can see some similarities of this game's setting and look with the city sections of Shadow Warrior 2. They both feature their own thing, such as HR being in a kind of Blade Runner-ish setting and SW2's cities being more of a Technilogical Utopia, but I can see some lines between the two. Personally I did enjoy this as it gave more variety to the enviorment and enemies, but this really grinded other people's gears so if you wouldn't like the deviation from the traditional setting during about half of the missions, this may bother you.
-People do have some valid complaints about the highest difficulties and some enemies giving off the "bullet sponge" feel, but this sort of thing is common with most games of this nature so I feel the criticisms are more harsh than it should be (Higher difficulty: buff enemy health, enemies resist certain damage types, buff enemy damage, the loot). Personally I do feel that the damage resistant/immune (the cause of the "bullet sponge" claims) would have worked better if it was typed to an enemy rather than random (ie immune solely for bosses/"minibosses" and Zilla City's many mechanical enemies should be weak to electric damage, neutral to ice, resist fire/toxic). Having to dash/jump all around a hoard of enemies at higher difficulties trying to get an idea of their resistances and weaknesses is annoying at best.
-The ending was a bit subpar than I would have liked. It was not at all terrible, just more of a 'meh'. Can't really say much more than that.
-Last complaint is that at endgame the loot in all areas you can go back to does not scale, so only really the last 3 areas are worth farming for powerful mods.
In short, it's not perfect but it's hella good:
Plus: Awesome soundtrack, stunning visuals, good developers who give good updates, weapon variety and mods, majority of story, humor
Meh/Neutral: Ending is underwelming, voice acting was a bit off at times, different setting which seems like a mix between their 2013 Shadow Warrior game and Hard Reset.
Minus: Enemy damage type resistence could be better implemented to prevent bullet sponge enemies, endgame is limited.
Edit: On 3/16/2017 the developers added yet another free DLC... These guys...
