One of the few loot shooters i genuinely find fun since the actual gameplay aspect of killing enemies is just so well done it never seems to get old.
The 2013 remake was a linear game with no loot system, so it's kinda odd they went with a hub world design, side quests, loot, a randomly generated level system and crafting in the 2nd game. At first i though some of these might make the experience worse but they didn't really at all, it actually makes the experience better apart from the randomly generated levels which can sometimes be lack luster when it comes to their design and pacing, i would've prefered if they just had a proper level designer team hand craft everything instead of it just being pieces which the game randomly combines each time.
The loot system the game has on offer is rather neat, it's pretty fun experimenting with the difrent combinations such as making a toxic rocket launcher or a minigun that fires lighting enchanted bullets.
It also has 4 player co-op, which i can't really experience since everyone i know doesn't own the game sadly but it functions the same way it does in other loot based games, more players, more enemies with higher HP and more loot.
Visually the game looks stunning in every aspect, especially the lighting however its human character models can look rather dated for today's standards. It runs fairly well even with my aging 760 GTX 2GB after doing some tweaking in the options menu. What i love the most when it comes to the visuals is the art, it's just so damn colorfull, every area and scene is just incredibly gorgeous to look at due to the fantastic art design and high amount of colours.
The movement in the game feels fantastic, you move pretty fast, can dash anytime with no limitations, you can double jump and vault over or up onto objects. All the guns are hella satisfying to use, the combat in general is just really addictive, often finding myself on purpose trying to kill more enemies on my way to an objective marker instead of ignoring them. What helps make it feel so good is the gore, the amount of time and love put into the crazy amounts of way you can blow up or slice parts off monsters is crazy and always looks spectacular. In general, if you played lets say the new Doom from 2016, the combat is similar to that but even more faster paced thanks to the dash move and there being no pre-animated execution moves.
If you love fast paced shooters with tons of weapons,monsters and loot then getting Shadow Warrior 2 is a no brainer.

Got this for $19.99 from Humble Bundle... thankfully. I really wish I could have gotten a refund because here's the thing:
This is not a finished game. It's unoptimized, and has a rather high amount of bugs. If this were listed as Early Access
I would be far more forgiving because I'd have known what to expect.
There's no reason why this should retail for $40 at the moment.
Okay, now that my complaints are out of the way, I will say what others have said:
The game is an awesome concept. It's pretty much a "simulator" of medieval life. People have to work
together in groups for their Kingdoms/villages to be successful, not to mention you actually begin to rely on others for things you need in order to progress. Being something as mundane as a farmer or blacksmith is actually engaging, because at some point, you could realistically have employees and accountants working for you as you step back and take on a more managerial role and possibly even start a side career in politics.
The downside to that juicy description above is that for any of that stuff to take place, the game has to not frustrate you into submission and not crash. Also, server wipes are pretty common from what I hear, and I can only imagine how irritating that has to be once you've put hours upon hours of effort into a character.
I hate to write a negative review, but until this game gets fully optimized... or at least relatively optimized, don't pay full price. It's worth checking out if you get it on sale and have disposable income, but if you're actually looking for a finished quality product? You need to look elsewhere, and by that I mean in a completely different genre. Make no mistake, LiF is the best at what it does, but sadly even the King is plagued.

A fun, albeit shallow, experience.
DptP (Duels of the Planeswalkers) 2015 changes up the formula a bit. The game offers full custom deckbuilding, which is a new and exciting feature, but it comes at a price; the few prebuilt starter decks in the game are lacking in both cohesion and power. But since the game gives you all the tools to experiment and make a better deck, I can't fault it to heavily.
Deckbuilding is implemented well for the most part. There is a unique restriction on the rarity of cards that can be in your deck - 4 of each common, 3 of each uncommon, 2 of each rare, and 1 of each mythic rare are allowed. This means that you can't really build a deck based on reliably drawing and casting a mythic rare, but it also means that decks are more varied with each play. I imagine that aspect is fun for newcomers to Magic.
DotP 2015 also includes microtransaction in the form of premium boosters that contan premium cards you can't get anywhere else. This is very unfortunate, but the cards contained in these boosters aren't overwhelming game breaking or powerful, although they do unlock new archetypes. I didn't buy any premium boosters while playing the game, and I would recommend everyone else do the same.
Overall, the game isn't pefect of even great, but I found it overall enjoyable and worth the $10 I paid for it.

I'm making this review after 124 hours of gameplay. And I can safely say that this game is a great game.
It is perhaps the most rewarding game I've ever played. If you want a game that forces you to work with others, forces you to communicate, build a community and enjoy some lovely medieval life. Then this is the game for you. Be aware, Life is Feudal does not have instant gratification.
The top 3 things you're going to *really* need to play and enjoy the game.
- Patience
- A will to work with others
- Time
If you are not a patient person, this game is not for you. This is a game where building a house, village, castle walls or a castle can take from days, to weeks to months. The idea is to create a society, and progress from living in a hut to living in a real place surrounded by real walls. The more people you have in your settlement. The easier it's gonna be to get materials, build, improve, farm, and defend yourself.
The combat is somewhat like in Mount & Blade Warband (being able to attack left, right, up & down) and it's quite well done. You're not rambo, and there are things like wounds, fractures, bleeding and poisons that will make you have to retreat or back out.
The community of the game is grand, it's lovely. Most people are communicative, understanding and friendly. Of course, there are bandits and banditry is rampant like in all PvP games. That's a part of the game, without them it would be boring.
Finally, to be honest. This game does have performance issues. Not everyone can get 60 fps, there is lag and I've experienced crashes too and so has my entire guild. But when these things are not happening, the game is incredibly fun. But as of now, the game is not perfect. It's good, but has issues. None the less I belive it's worth the price.

I find myself sorely let down by this game. The idea seemd to sound good as in a game where the idea is survival in a barren city while murderous monsters roam with the sole intent of hunting you down. However the actual way this game is played is unfortunately not in the least bit a survival game. The fact that you can buy bullets, food, medicine, melee weapons and light sources for an absolutely pathetically low price you can make it easier still by forking over five bucks of real currency. Now I will say the fact that guns are scarce and muust be found is definitely good but when you can buy all the bullets you need why even bother doing anything but hunt down other players. Finish a single courier mission and you can live the high life for a long LONG time and just mosy around doing nothing.
Everybody has a global inventory that can be accessed from any safezone so I see no reason to even carry items around with me. There is no penalty for death except losing character experience, though courier missions also gives you an insane amount of experience. Even if you play just to try and make it a survival game without using the market it is just painfully easy to kill any of the monsters. After level one you can solo all but the huge monster just by blocking. The only things I can say positive about this game is that loot spawns are nice and sparse, the world does look fairly nice, and even the atmosphering is fairly good.Though the atmosphere could be improved by not having background monster screams occuring and let the actual monsters do it.
I guess it just seems like the creators of this game wanted to make a survival/semi horror game but took one look at any sandbox fps free to play mmo and decided this was the game model that theirs should be based off of.
In the end pitifully easy monsters. infinite bullets, weapons, food and medicine. global inventory that cannot be lost on death. and pay to win capability makes this game babies first survival game (or any ftp survival game).

Generally I never been fond of remakes. I live by the rule "If it ain't broken don't fix it" so any tempering with my favorite games feels like an unnecessary risk.
However, when I heard Jane Jensen been remaking GK1 I was over the moon!  And I was right as this game clearly lived up to my huge expectations and beyond.
Not only they managed to preserve the incredible atmosphere and story they managed to improve it with better graphics and vastly improved score. Add to that few new puzzles and this is THE game you need to replay even if you played the original.
And if you are new then you are in for a treat - its a very clever game with lots of cool twists and amazing storytelling. You simply cannot avoid falling in love with the characters.
So yes, while its a "remake" - its definitely one of the best ones ever.

I have spent extensive time in the Closed Alpha, Closed+Open beta, and around 10 hours in the full game gifted to me by a friend.
:
Great game I enjoy it a lot, while the multiplayer can seem cancerous when you are getting ganked in a 1v3, those intense 1 on 1 duels when you get them make up for it by being well designed and fun. Worth a buy.

- Characters and Scenery are beautiful to look at
- Combat flows very nicely and every swing feels like it matters
- Customization is fantastic, Helmet/Chest/Arms and Blade/Pommel/Hilt type customization each with stats to make your build unique
- Almost everything can be earned with the free in game currency.
- Has singleplayer (Can be done Co-op)
- 1v1 and 2v2 duels with 4v4 Team Deathmatch and Control Points game modes feel different from eachother.
- Singleplayer has hidden collectibles that make playing the story worth it on hardest difficulty, along with teaching how to play most characters.
- Story for singleplayer feels generic and boring with a bit lack luster voice acting and dialogue.
- The whole concept of Knights v Vikings v Samurai is kind of forgotten when you are put into teams A and B which can consist of any combination of characters from all the factions.
- Combat can feel frustrating when you play matches that aren't 1v1 due to the gank strategy being all too common. Why fight YOUR enemy when you can run and hit your friend's enemy in the back?
- While there is a freely earned in game currency, the option to simply buy said currency exists.

I never really got into the whole Duke Nukem franchise or played any of the older games, so I'm just going to exclude that whole "hype train disappointment" factor from the review and get down to the actual content.
+You can practically interact with almost everything in the game. It makes it a lot more enjoyable and adds more freedom. (You can play pool, curl weights, shoot hoops, look at porn, microwave♥♥♥♥♥♥ etc.)

+Graphics are alright. Nothing top notch but pretty decent.
+B00bies...who doesn't love some b00bies?
+Fun achievements. Yes, i'm taking this into consideration. Stuff like getting 7-0 score in air hockey, drinking all the beers in the strip club, or throwing a turd at a wall.

-Storyline. (Yeah i know I haven't played the other games, but I still know the concept. It's pretty bleak, super cliche, and kind of boring.)
-No replay value
All in all, it's not a terrible game. Definitely get it on sale if you do.

SOMA offers a very interesting story and an even more impressive environment for it. The games greatest strengths are in the interesting mystery as it unfolds and the desire to learn more about the fate of the crew of the Pathos 2 facility will drive you forward. However, if you are looking at getting this game for it's horror, you may want to look elsewhere as many of the monster encounters are predictable and not very frightening (except for one perticular journey outside of the facility which was actually terrifying). Many of the encounters feel more like obstacles and chores to deal with than organic encounters as well which can really bring you out of the experience. That being said, apart from some minor pacing issues and sometimes difficult to understand story elements this game offers a great journey for anyone hungry for a story driven horror title, especially for anyone who loves mystery. If you are more into the horror aspect though, I would recommend Outlast or Alien Isolation instead, although I am not particularly scared of games like this in general so others could enjoy SOMAs horror more than me
Overall good game, although a bit pricey for a 10 hours, I give SOMA a 7.5/10

A brief description of this game may read "resource management and competitive economics on Mars" - its free from combat (at least of a gun-play kind) and runs at "realtime" - Sounds good (if you like that sort of thing, which I do) and faily original...BUT there is one central and perhaps critical flaw...
Offworld Trading Company has some truelly fantastic and compulsive elements - it has simple yet dynamic gameplay which takes seconds to learn and forever to master; the claiming and extraction of always limited resources before your competitors is simple enough (at least in theory) - the refinement of the resources into goods that demand higher prices, none too complex - manipulating the market for your benifit needs a little practice - However, learning how and when to combine black market tricks on your competitors with manufactured price hikes that trash their stock so you can buy them at a snap -- this takes time.
Sadly, time is the thing that you simply don't have.  Whilst the interface, the gameplay and the graphics are all on a scale between good and outstanding the games pacing feels all off.  It's like watching (the original) Total Recall at twenty times the normal speed; you know that there are some great moments in there that you would love to savour but it's gone before you've noticed you're enjoying yourself.  If you're victorious then it doesn't feel like you've worked for it, if you lose it dosn't feel you've had a chance to put up a fight.  A game lasts around a half an hour to an hour and moves at a pace that would give Usain Bolt jet lag...
And this is worries me because I don't know how it can be changed without removing all that makes the game stand-out from the crowd.  The Unique Selling Point of this game is "realtime" competitive economics - but that's not strictly true; REALTIME economics is slow, careful, managed.  Sure, there is shouting and screaming on the trading floor, but the wider economic world around it moves at a more measured pace.  RTS is a format that suits combat orientated games - it's frantic "WHO IS SHOOTING ME/WHEN DID THAT BLOW-UP!!" quality is appropriate to its content - war is (I imagine) chaotic and frantic - it's central gameplay is built around event's that can be drawn over realtime - namely gunfights.  But if we had a TRUE RTS economics game you would need to pass it down several generations to win - Neither nation nor global corporation gained market dominance over thirty muinets, it takes hundereds of yeears.... something thats nicely communicated and simulated in the format of a turn-based game.  The question is "who want's this game", or perhaps rather "When do I want this game"?  If I'm in the mood for something fast-paced but stratigic it makes sense to look for gunplay, if its long lasting and stratigic economic is better.  This has the flaw of being neither and both.
In the end, for all of Offworld Trading Company's good points (and it has many), its format seems irreconcilably at odds with its content; it ain't realtime economics at all, its economics so fast it feels like you can't breath - think Arnie in the red dust with eyes about to pop.
